video_title: 👧🏻 My Body Belongs to Me From My Head to My Toes

summaries.summary: Clara says her body belongs only to her, and it is very special. When she was a baby, her body looked different, but now she is growing and changing. Sometimes Clara likes to be close to people. She likes hugs from Papa, sitting on Granny’s lap, holding a little baby’s hands, and tickling a friend. These touches feel nice and cozy when both people want them. But Clara also says that sometimes she does not want to be touched. She does not like too much tickling, big sloppy kisses, a dog licking her, or being held too tight. When she does not like touch, she says, “Stop it! Don’t touch me. I don’t want you to.” She also says no when she does not want to touch someone else. If someone does not stop after she says no, Clara should tell a trusted person. Clara decides who may touch her and when.

summaries.summary: On a snow-cold day, a round old couple worked in their snug little house to get ready for Easter. The round old man blew the insides out of eggs, and the round old woman painted them with pretty colors. The little rabbit watched. Later, they made straw baskets together and then chocolate eggs on a spring day when the snow was melting. When Easter came, they gave every child in the village a straw basket full of eggs. One year, the round old couple were asleep when there was still work to do. The little rabbit hopped onto the table, put the eggs into the baskets, and carried them down the lane. He left one basket for every child. The next year, he colored the eggs, cooked the chocolate, wove the baskets, and delivered them too. The children learned that the Easter bunny came. After many years, the old couple could not help anymore, so the little rabbit found a new hidden place to make the Easter baskets. Now he and his friends work there every year, and on Easter morning he still delivers the baskets.

He kept doing this every year until the old couple were too old to help. Then he found a hidden place with rooms for eggs, chocolate, and baskets, and his friends helped him. Now the Easter bunny still delivers baskets every Easter morning.

video_title: 🐱 Splat the Cat: Makes Dad Glad

summaries.summary: On a Sunday morning, Splat the Cat felt glad after eating his favorite fish and reading Red Super Cat comics. Then he saw his dad sitting with a frown. Dad said his soccer team had lost a big game, and he felt sad. Splat wanted to cheer him up. He looked at old photos and saw Dad and Granddad winning games when they were young. Splat decided to help by joining School Game Day with Seymour and practicing hard for the three-legged race. On the big day, Splat and Dad joined the games with many other pets. They did well in the wheelbarrow race, but Splat got a thorn in his paw. In the egg toss, eggs splashed on Dad. At last, in the three-legged race, Splat’s lucky shoelace came untied, and they fell into a pond. Dad laughed and said he did not care about winning. Splat was happy because he made his dad glad.

video_title: 🦊 My Lucky Day

summaries.summary: One day, a hungry fox was getting ready to hunt when he heard a knock at his door. A piglet was outside. The fox opened the door, grabbed the piglet, and said it was his lucky day. He wanted to make a pig roast for dinner. The piglet asked to be washed first because he was dirty. The fox agreed and gave him a bath. Then the piglet said he was too small and should be fed first so he would make more meat. The fox agreed again and cooked him a nice dinner. After that, the piglet said his meat was tough and needed a massage to become tender. The fox worked very hard, pushing and squeezing the piglet. The piglet kept asking for more, and the fox grew tired and passed out. The piglet then picked up the rest of the cookies and went home. He relaxed by a warm fire and looked in his address book to see who to visit next.

A hungry fox was polishing his claws when someone knocked on the door and called for Rabbit. When the fox opened it, he found a piglet instead. The fox grabbed the piglet and said dinner had come to his door. The piglet asked to be washed first because he was filthy, so the fox made a fire, carried in water, and gave him a bath. Next, the piglet said he should eat a meal because he was small and needed more meat. The fox picked tomatoes, made spaghetti, baked cookies, and fed the piglet. Then the piglet said his meat was hard and asked for a massage to make him tender. The fox pushed, pulled, squeezed, and pounded the piglet from head to toe. The piglet kept asking for more until the fox became too tired and fainted. The piglet, now clean, fat, and soft, went home with the cookies. Later, he sat by a warm fire and looked in his address book for another visit.

Arnie still says it would look good with a frosting sprinkle mustache.

video_title: 🐸 Froggy's First Kiss

summaries.summary: The week before Valentine’s Day, Froggy thought about candy and love at school. In class, Miss Witherspoon told him to pay attention, but Froggy kept looking at the new girl, Frogalina. At recess, he saw her smile and fell on his head. At lunch, Frogalina sat beside him and gave him a juicy apple. The next day, she gave him a heart-shaped cookie. Later, the class made paper valentines, and Froggy wrote “I love you” on one card and hid under his desk so no one would see it. When he stood up, he bonked his head, and everyone laughed. The next day, Frogalina gave him a kiss on the cheek. Froggy felt strange and flopped away. On the bus, everyone teased him. At home, his mother asked about school and valentines. On Valentine’s Day morning, Froggy gave his mother breakfast in bed and gave her the heart that said “I love you.” His mother gave him many candy kisses.

His bed is warm and his pillow is deep, so he wants to keep sleeping. He says he does not care that other children are getting up all over the world, in places like Switzerland, Memphis, Alaska, China, Italy, Spain, Massachusetts, Connecticut, Maine, London, Paris, and Berlin. He says people can try to wake him in many ways. They can tickle his feet, shake his bed, pour cold water on his head, knock on his door, or even yell until Christmas, but it will not help. He also says sweet foods, dogs, roosters, geese, the police, newspapers, the United States Marines, TV, and a big brass band will not make him rise. In the end, he stays in bed, and the other person says he can have the egg.

summaries.summary: Cookie Monster was very hungry and waited for his groceries to come. When the doorbell rang, a delivery girl brought a box. Cookie Monster looked inside and did not see cookies. He found carrots, celery, broccoli, a beet, a squash, an onion, and potatoes. He used the carrots like a pencil and a hat, the celery like a back scratcher, the broccoli like a feather duster, the beet like a top, the squash like a telephone, the onion like a ball, and the potatoes like things to juggle. Then Ernie and Bert came in with the wrong groceries. They said the supermarket had mixed up the orders. They showed Cookie Monster that the vegetables were for soup. Bert and Ernie washed and cut the vegetables, cooked them, and waited until the soup was ready. Cookie Monster cooled the soup, then ate it all. After that, he ate the cookies too.

Cookie Monster sat waiting for cookies and other groceries from the supermarket. A delivery girl brought a box, but it held vegetables, not cookies. Cookie Monster tried to use the carrots as a pencil and telescope, then wore them as a hat. He used celery as a back scratcher, broccoli as a feather duster, a beet as a spinning top, a squash as a telephone, an onion as a ball, and potatoes for juggling. Then Ernie and Bert arrived with bags of groceries and said the supermarket had mixed up the deliveries. They told Cookie Monster the vegetables were for vegetable soup. Bert and Ernie washed the vegetables, cut them up, and cooked them in a pot with salt and pepper. Cookie Monster kept asking if it was soup yet and tried to cool it by blowing and fanning. When Bert said it was cool enough, Cookie Monster ate the whole pot of soup. Then he ate the cookies too.

After that, he ate the cookies.

summaries.summary: Alistister the Elf left Elfen Corners for the North Pole. The village said goodbye, and the mayor said Santa had asked for their merriest elf. At the North Pole, Alistister was the littlest elf, and head elf Macafferty could not find him a job. He could not hammer a wagon, paint a dollhouse roof, stuff bears, or sweep with the big broom. The other elves laughed and said he was useless. Alistister felt sad and ran away. He hid by the wood pile near the reindeer pen and met an old elf named Nicholas. Nicholas asked his name and invited him to help with the reindeer. Alistister fed the reindeer, watered them, and sang songs with Nicholas. Later, Nicholas was gone, and Alistister worried and went to Santa’s house. There he found Nicholas, who was really Santa Claus, and learned he had a special job: to ride in the sleigh and help with Christmas Eve deliveries.

Nicholas was kind and let him help feed, water, and sing to the reindeer. Alistister came back every day. Then Nicholas was gone, and Alistister worried. He went to Santa’s house and found Nicholas there. Nicholas said Alistister was a big help and had a special job. Alistister would go with him on Christmas Eve to make deliveries in the sleigh.

summaries.summary: Owl took a kettle from the cupboard and said he would make tear water tea. He put the kettle on his lap and sat very still. Then Owl thought of sad things, like chairs with broken legs, songs with forgotten words, spoons lost behind the stove, books with torn pages, stopped clocks, mornings nobody saw, mashed potatoes left on a plate, and pencils that were too short to use. As he thought about these things, he began to cry. His tears dropped into the kettle. He cried and cried until the kettle was full. Then Owl said, “That does it.” He stopped crying and put the kettle on the stove to boil. At last he filled his cup and drank the tea. He said it tasted a little salty, but tear water tea was always very good.

Owl watched as the moon climbed higher and became a full, round moon. He looked at it for a long time and said that if he was looking at the moon, the moon must be looking back at him, so they must be good friends. Owl told the moon he would come back again, but first he had to go home. When he walked home, he saw that the moon was following him. He asked the moon to stay over the sea, then over the trees, and not come home with him. Owl said goodbye and climbed a hill. The moon went behind clouds and disappeared. Owl felt sad. At home, he put on his pajamas and got into bed. Then the moon came out again and filled his room with silver light. Owl saw the moon in his window and said it had followed him all the way home. He felt happy and was not sad anymore.

Owl went to the seashore at night and sat on a big rock. He watched the moon rise from the sea and become bright and round. Owl talked to the moon and said they must be friends because each one could look at the other. Then he said he would see the moon again later and started home. As he walked, the moon seemed to follow him in the sky. Owl asked the moon to stay over the sea, but it kept coming. He said the moon should not come to his small house, because it would not fit through the door and he had no supper to share. The moon followed him over the trees. Owl climbed a hill and shouted, “Goodbye, moon.” After that, the moon went behind clouds and was gone. Owl felt sad about saying goodbye. He went home, put on his pajamas, and got into bed. His room was dark until the moon came back out and shone through the window. Owl saw the moon and said it had followed him home. Then he was not sad anymore.

At night, Owl sat on a rock by the sea and watched the moon rise. The moon got bigger and brighter in the sky. Owl spoke to the moon and said they must be very good friends. He told the moon he had to go home, and he walked down the path. But the moon kept coming along with him. Owl asked the moon to stay over the sea and not follow him. He said his house was small and there was nothing for the moon to eat. Still, the moon sailed after him over the trees. Owl climbed a hill and shouted goodbye. Then the moon went behind clouds and disappeared. Owl said it was sad to say goodbye to a friend. He went home, changed into pajamas, and got into bed. The room was dark and he felt sad. Then the moon came out again and filled the room with silver light. Owl looked out the window and said the moon had followed him all the way home. He put his head on the pillow and felt happy.

One dark night, Owl went to the seashore and sat on a large rock. He watched the moon rise from the edge of the sea until it was full and shining. Owl said that if he looked at the moon, the moon must be looking back at him, and he called it a good friend. Then Owl said he would come back another time and started walking home. The moon stayed in the sky and seemed to follow him. Owl asked it to stay over the sea, then over the trees, and not come to his small house. He said the door was too small and there was no supper for the moon. Owl climbed a hill and shouted, “Goodbye, moon.” The moon went behind clouds and disappeared. Owl felt sad and said goodbye was hard. He came home, put on pajamas, and got into bed. His room was dark until the moon came out again and shone through the window. Owl saw the moon and said it had followed him home. Then he closed his eyes and did not feel sad anymore.

Owl went to the seashore at night and sat on a rock. He watched the moon rise high in the sky and shine over the sea. Owl said the moon and he must be friends because they could look at each other. He told the moon he would come back later, but first he had to go home. As Owl walked down the path, the moon followed him. Owl asked the moon to stay where it looked fine over the sea, and then not to come home with him because his house was small and there was nothing to eat. The moon kept following over the trees. Owl climbed a hill and shouted goodbye. Then the moon went behind clouds and was gone. Owl felt sad when he said goodbye. He went home, put on pajamas, and got into bed. summaries.summary: Frog and Toad went to a large meadow to fly a kite. Frog said the wind was strong and the kite would fly up to the top of the sky. Toad held the string while Frog held the kite, and Toad ran across the meadow. The kite went up a little, then fell down. Three robins in a bush laughed and said the kite would not fly. Toad told Frog he gave up. Frog asked for a second try, then a third try, but the kite still fell down each time. The robins kept saying the kite was no good. Frog asked for one more try. Toad ran again, waved the kite, jumped up and down, and shouted, “Up, kite, up!” This time the kite flew higher and higher. Frog and Toad were happy, and they watched the kite fly way up in the sky.

Frog and Toad took a kite to a meadow where the wind was strong. Frog wanted the kite to fly all the way to the top of the sky. Toad held the ball of string while Frog held the kite, and Toad ran fast across the grass. The kite rose for a moment and then hit the ground. Three robins in a bush laughed and said the kite would not fly. Toad went back and told Frog he gave up. Frog asked him to try again, first by waving the kite over his head, and then by waving it and jumping up and down. Each time, the kite fell back into the grass, and the robins called it a joke and junk. Toad wanted to go home, but Frog asked for one more try. Toad waved, jumped, and shouted, “Up, kite, up!” Then the kite flew up high. Frog said that the last try worked, and they sat watching the kite in the sky.

Toad held the string, and Frog held the kite while Toad ran. The kite lifted up but fell down with a bump. Three robins watched from a bush and laughed at them. Toad told Frog the kite would not fly and that he gave up. Frog said they should make a second try, so Toad ran and waved the kite over his head. The kite rose and fell again. Frog then asked for a third try, with waving and jumping. The kite still crashed into the grass. The robins said to throw it away and go home. Toad came back and said the kite was junk. Frog asked for one more try, and Toad ran, waved, jumped, and shouted, “Up, kite, up!” Then the kite flew high, and Frog and Toad watched it soar while the robins could not fly as high.

summaries.summary: Owl lived in a house with an upstairs and a downstairs. There were 20 steps on the stairway. Sometimes Owl was upstairs in his bedroom, and other times he was downstairs in his living room. When he was downstairs, he wondered how his upstairs was getting along. When he was upstairs, he wondered how his downstairs was getting along. He felt he was always missing one place or the other. Owl thought there must be a way to be upstairs and downstairs at the same time. He tried running up the stairs, then down the stairs, and then faster and faster all evening. He called out, but there was no answer from the other place. At last, Owl saw that when he was up, he was not down, and when he was down, he was not up. He was very tired, so he sat down to rest on the tenth step, right in the middle.

Owl had a house with two places, upstairs and downstairs, and 20 steps between them. He spent some time in his bedroom upstairs and some time in his living room downstairs. When he was downstairs, he worried about upstairs. When he was upstairs, he worried about downstairs. Owl said he wanted to be in both places at once. He tried running up the stairs and then running down the stairs. He kept going faster and faster, all evening long. He shouted to ask if the other place was there, but no one answered. Owl learned that he could not be upstairs and downstairs at the same time. When he was up, he was not down, and when he was down, he was not up. In the end, he was very tired. He sat on the tenth step to rest because it was in the middle.

Owl wanted to be in both places at once, so he tried to run very fast between them. He ran up the stairs and said he was up. He ran down the stairs and said he was down. Then he ran up and down faster and faster all evening. He shouted for the other place, but there was no answer. At the end, Owl said that when he was up, he was not down, and when he was down, he was not up. He was very tired and sat on the tenth step, the middle step, to rest.

The story then moves to Toad’s birthday. Frog gives Toad a hat as a present, but the hat is much too big and falls down over Toad’s eyes. Frog says he will give him something else, but Toad says the hat is his present and he likes it. When Frog and Toad go for a walk, Toad trips over a rock, bumps into a tree, and falls into a hole because he cannot see. He says the day is sad because he cannot wear the beautiful hat. Frog tells Toad to go to bed and think very big thoughts so his head will grow larger by morning and the hat may fit. Toad thinks about giant sunflowers, tall oak trees, and high mountains covered with snow, then falls asleep.

While Toad sleeps, Frog quietly goes to Toad’s house and takes the hat. He pours water on it, puts it in a warm place to dry, and the hat shrinks smaller and smaller. Then Frog takes the hat back and puts it where he found it. In the morning, Toad wakes up and puts the hat on. This time it fits just right. Toad runs to Frog’s house and says that all his big thoughts made his head much larger, so he can wear the present. Frog and Toad go for another walk. This time Toad does not trip, bump into a tree, or fall into a hole. The day turns out to be very pleasant.

summaries.summary: On her first day at work, Amelia Bedelia comes to the Rogers house with a list from Mrs. Rogers. Mr. and Mrs. Rogers leave in their car, and Amelia Bedelia decides to make them a surprise lemon meringue pie before she starts. Then she reads the list and does each job in a very exact way. She changes the towels in the green bathroom by cutting them with scissors, because she thinks “change” means make them different. She dusts the furniture with dust powder, draws the drapes by making a picture, and puts the lights out by unscrewing the bulbs. She measures two cups of rice by filling two cups with rice. When meat is delivered, she trims the steak with lace and ribbon and dresses the chicken in clothes. When Mr. and Mrs. Rogers come home, they are surprised by her work. At first they are upset, but then they taste the pie and decide Amelia Bedelia can stay.

For free time, she made daisies for her mother, but Miss Edwards told her to sit down and glue herself to her seat. Amelia Bedelia did, and she got stuck. Miss Edwards later said she was a new teacher too, and Amelia Bedelia said they both deserved gold stars. It is another little mouse, and he asks again, “Do you want to be my friend?” This time, the answer is yes. The two mice are happy to be friends. summaries.summary: On Monday, Sam and Dave dug a hole. Sam asked when they should stop, but Dave said they were on a mission and would not stop until they found something spectacular. They dug so deep that their heads went underground, but they still found nothing. They took a break. Dave drank chocolate milk from a canteen, and Sam ate animal cookies wrapped in their grandfather's kirchief. Dave thought the problem might be that they were digging straight down, so Sam said they should dig another way. Dave then said they should split up, and Sam agreed. Dave went one way and Sam went another, but they still found nothing spectacular. Then Dave said they should go back to digging straight down, and Sam agreed again.

Sam and Dave kept digging and ran out of chocolate milk. They shared the last animal cookie, but they did not stop. After a while, Sam said he was tired and could not dig anymore. Sam said, "Well," and Dave said, "Well," because that was pretty spectacular. After that, they went inside for chocolate milk and animal cookies.

summaries.summary: Rabbit was hopping home when he heard a loud voice inside his burrow. He called for help. Cat came first. Rabbit said there was a giant jumper in his burrow. Cat said she would slink inside and pounce on him. But then Cat heard the loud voice, and she got scared too. She asked Bear for help. Bear said he would put his big furry paw inside and knock the giant down. But Bear heard the voice and got scared. Bear asked Elephant for help. Elephant said he would wrap his trunk around the giant and toss him away. But Elephant heard the voice and got scared too. Then Elephant asked Mama Frog for help. The other animals said the giant was too scary. Mama Frog still went to the burrow and told the giant to come out. She counted one, two, three, and out jumped baby frog. He said, “Hello, mama. I’m the giant jumperie.” Mama Frog said he was coming home for tea.

summaries.summary: One morning, little Benjamin Bunny sat on a bank and heard a pony coming. A gig came along the road with Mr. McGregor and Mrs. McGregor inside. In the wood nearby lived old Mrs. Rabbit and her children, Flopsy, Mopsy, Cottontail, and Peter. Benjamin found Peter sitting alone by the fur tree. Peter had no coat or shoes because he had lost them in Mr. McGregor’s garden. Benjamin told Peter that Mr. McGregor and Mrs. McGregor were out for the day. The two rabbits went to the wall and looked into the garden. Peter’s clothes were on the scarecrow. Benjamin helped Peter get them back. They then filled Peter’s pocket handkerchief with onions and ate lettuce in the garden. Soon they were frightened by a cat, so they hid under a basket. Peter and Benjamin stayed there until old Mr. Bunny came, chased the cat away, and took the rabbits home. Peter’s mother was glad he had found his clothes, and the onions were hung in the kitchen.

Peter told how he had run from Mr. McGregor’s garden and left his clothes behind. Benjamin said the McGregors had gone out for the day. The rabbits climbed to the wall and looked down at the garden. Peter’s coat and shoes were on the scarecrow. Benjamin climbed into the garden by a pear tree, and Peter followed. They got Peter’s clothes back and saw that the shoes were wet and the coat had shrunk. Benjamin filled a handkerchief with onions, and Peter ate lettuce while Benjamin said he often came there with his father, old Mr. Benjamin Bunny. Then they heard a cat. They hid under a basket, and the cat sat on top for five hours. At last old Mr. Bunny came, jumped on the cat, shut it in the greenhouse, and took Benjamin and Peter home.

summaries.summary: Karen wakes up after a bad dream and thinks she fell off a cliff. Kristy helps her get dressed, but Karen cannot find her new jeans. At breakfast, Andrew has finished the Crunchos box and gotten the prize, which is stickers. Karen gets a new box, but it is empty, so Andrew shares some of his stickers with her. Karen tries to feel better by watching her favorite TV show, but Andrew is already watching cartoons. Their grown-up makes them share the TV, but then the show is not on because of a special report. Karen also tries to play with Shannon, but Shannon does not want to play. When David Michael and Hanni go on a bike ride and picnic, Karen cannot go because of her cast. She feels sad and angry and thinks the bad luck will not stop.

Karen stays home and plays with Kristy, who is making brownies for the Babysitters Club. They play checkers, but Karen is upset when Kristy does not let her win. Karen then hugs Musie, her stuffed cat, and tells him about her bad day: the bad dream, falling out of bed, the empty cereal box, the missing TV show, Shannon not playing, the fight with Hanni, and Kristy treating her like a baby. Elizabeth sees that Musie is falling apart and pretends to be an animal doctor. Karen lets Elizabeth fix Musie. Elizabeth also tells Karen about a very bad day she once had, and then helps Karen start the day over by pretending it is morning again. Karen hopes the new day will be better, and she waits for the mail and a package.

Karen gets more upset when the mail truck comes and her package is not there. Then Andrew comes home with a present from Uncle and Aunt Anne: new movies. Karen is jealous and calls Andrew names, so Daddy sends her to her room. Karen feels like everyone hates her because she was mean to Andrew, yelled at Hanni, and acted badly all day. Andrew later brings her the movies anyway, and Karen says she is spoiled and gives them back. Daddy ends her punishment early, but Karen keeps singing about worms because she still feels sad. Just then she hears Mr. Tasty, the ice cream man, coming. She hopes this will be another good thing after all the bad things that have happened.

Mr. Tasty arrives, and Karen asks for cherry Italian ice, but he is out of cherry. She does not want lemon or grape, and she stays unhappy. At dinner, Karen says she is not hungry, but Daddy and Elizabeth ask her to come anyway. Karen and the grown-ups talk about bad days, and Karen says she has had one of the worst days ever. Elizabeth counts the bad things in her own bad days too, and Karen counts hers: the bad dream, falling out of bed, the missing Crunchos prize, no cherry Italian ice, no package, no TV show, and more. Elizabeth says Karen would win a prize for bad days. Then Karen gets a surprise when she goes with Sam and Charlie to Sylvania’s Sweets. She gets a root beer float, and Charlie’s friends think she is Charlie’s older sister and even ask if she is 26. Karen feels proud, and she thinks the bad day is finally ending.

At bedtime, Karen says her day has turned around. She tells Andrew she is sorry for calling him names and being mean because she was upset about not getting a gift. Andrew accepts her apology and says she can still share his stickers and watch the new movies anytime. Karen also apologizes to Hanni for calling her a bad friend, and Hanni says Karen is still her best friend. Karen thanks Elizabeth for fixing Musie and telling her about her bad day. She also apologizes to Kristy for the checker game. Kristy accepts and says she will not let Karen win next time. Karen chooses a new book to read, and Kristy begins reading it. Karen asks if pigs and witches ever have bad days, and they talk about how everyone can have one. Karen says if today was her worst day, maybe another day will be her best. She goes to bed feeling that tomorrow will be good.

video_title: Baby-Sitters Little Sister 3 "Karen`s Worst Day" by Katy Farina

summaries.summary: Karen wakes up after a bad dream about falling off a cliff. She tells Christy and Lucy that her wrist is fine but she had a scary dream. Karen gets dressed with help because of her cast, but she cannot find her new squid-sequin jeans. At breakfast, Andrew has finished the Crunchos and found the prize, so Karen only gets half of his stickers. Then she and Andrew fight over the TV, but a special report replaces Karen’s show. Karen tries to feel better by playing with Shannon, but Shannon does not want to play. After Boo Boo comes down from a tree, Karen goes to see Hanni and David Michael, but they leave for a bike ride and picnic she cannot join because of her cast. By the end of the chapter, Karen feels that the day is going badly.

Karen stays upset when she is left out of the picnic and when Christy and her friends are busy making brownies for the Babysitters Club. She plays checkers with Christy, but Christy lets her win, and Karen does not like that either. Karen hugs her stuffed cat, Moosie, and lists all the bad things that have happened: the bad dream, falling out of bed, losing her jeans, the missing Crunchos prize, the TV problem, Shannon not playing, the fight with Hanni, and being treated like a baby. Then Elizabeth sees that Moosie is falling apart and pretends to be an animal doctor. While fixing Moosie, Elizabeth tells Karen about her own worst day, when she failed a test, got yelled at, burned dinner, cut her hand, fought with a sister, and lost earrings. Elizabeth tells Karen to start the day over, so Karen lies down and pretends to wake up again.

Karen tries the new day Elizabeth suggested, but more things go wrong. She goes outside to wait for the mailman, Mr. Bennet, but a different truck comes instead. Later, Andrew comes home with a new haircut and a package from Uncle and Aunt Anne. Inside are new movies for Karen and Andrew, but Karen is angry and calls Andrew names because he has a present and she does not. Daddy sends Karen to her room for being mean. Karen feels that everyone hates her and starts singing, “Nobody likes me, everybody hates me.” Then Mr. Tasty arrives, but there is no cherry Italian ice for Karen. At dinner, the adults and children compare bad days, and Karen finds out that other people have had bad days too. She counts her own bad things and says she has set a bad day record.

The next day, Sam and Charlie invite Karen to go with them to Sylvania’s Sweets for ice cream. Karen feels grown up riding in the car with her big brothers. At the ice cream parlor, she orders a root beer float because Mr. Tasty had no cherry Italian ice that day. Charlie’s school friends are there, and one of them asks if Karen is Charlie’s older sister and says she looks 26. Karen feels happy about that. When they get home, she tells Daddy, Elizabeth, and Christy that the trip went well, that they parked right in front, and that she got a root beer float. She also says the day included another good thing: someone thought she was much older. After that, it is time to get ready for bed, and Karen notices that the family used a lot of toothpaste, setting a new film record.

Before bed, Karen makes three important apologies. She apologizes to Andrew for calling him names and tells him he can still have half her stickers and watch the new movies. She apologizes to Hanni for saying she was a bad friend, and Hanni says Karen is still her best friend. Karen also talks with Christy about the checkers game and says she is sorry for not being nice. Christy accepts the apology, and Karen says that if today was her worst day, then another day can be her best day. Christy starts reading a new chapter book to her, and Karen asks whether pigs and witches ever have bad days. Christy says everyone has bad days, and Karen agrees that tomorrow will probably be a good day. She falls asleep after saying goodnight to Christy and Elizabeth.

summaries.summary: Beagle was an imaginary friend who lived on an island far away where imaginary friends were made. Every night, he stood under the stars and waited to be chosen by a real child and given a special name. Night after night, his turn did not come. Beagle grew tired of waiting, so he did something unexpected. He set sail in a very small boat and crossed unknown waters to reach the real world. The real world felt strange at first. No one listened to music, and everyone seemed to need naptime. Then Beagle saw a place that felt familiar. He looked for a friend, but no one came. He climbed to the top of a tree and waited sadly. Soon he heard a noise below. A girl named Alice appeared, and she drew a picture of him. At first, they did not know what to do, but soon they became friends. Beagle and Alice shared snacks, told funny jokes, and went on many new adventures together.

They shared snacks, told jokes, and made the world feel less strange.

Elizabeth could not find any clothes left, so she put on a paper bag and followed the dragon. She found his cave and knocked on the big door. The dragon said he was busy and told her to come back tomorrow. Elizabeth kept talking to him and asked if he was the smartest and fiercest dragon. The dragon breathed fire again and again, then flew around the world for her. He got so tired that he fell asleep. Elizabeth quietly walked past him, opened the cave door, and found Ronald. Ronald said she looked messy and was wearing a dirty paper bag. Elizabeth said Ronald looked like a bum. They did not get married.

Rot sings a happy song about being the cutest and lines up with the other contestants. He sees many others, including a baby with floppy ears, a cuddly kitten, puppies, and jellyfish. The other contestants do not think Rot will win. Rot thinks about eating everyone, but he does not do it. He tries to make himself cuter by adding big ears, whiskers, and other things, but nothing helps. Then Rot decides to be himself. He goes on stage, smiles, and shows his best side. The judges like him very much and give him a big trophy. Rot sees his reflection in the shiny trophy and says he is the cutest in the world.

video_title: Bedtime Stories: How to Catch a Star

summaries.summary: There was a boy who loved stars very much. Every night, he looked at the stars from his window and wished for one of his very own. He dreamed that the star would be his friend and that they would play hide-and-go-seek and take walks together. One day, the boy decided to catch a star. He got up early at sunrise, but he could not see any stars, so he waited and waited. He waited through lunch and dinner. At last, just before the sun went away, he saw a star. He tried to jump for it, then climbed the tallest tree, but it was still too far. He tried many ways to reach it, but none worked. Then he saw something in the water. It was a baby star. He could not hold it in his hands. Later, he found a starfish on the sand and brought it home as his new friend.

A boy loved stars and watched them every night from his window. He wished for a star of his own, and he hoped it would be his friend. He wanted to catch one, so he went out at sunrise the next day. He waited for a long time, but no star came. At last, near sunset, he saw a star in the sky. The boy tried to reach it by jumping, but he was too short. He climbed the tallest tree, but the star was still too high. He thought about using a life preserver, a paper spaceship, and even a seagull, but none of these helped. Then he saw a pretty star floating in the water. It was a baby star, but it slipped through his fingers. The boy felt sad and walked home. On the bright golden sand, he found a starfish washed up on the beach. He took it home and read to his new star friend.

video_title: Bedtime Stories: The Man Who Didn't Wash His Dishes

summaries.summary: A man lived alone in a little house on the edge of town. He cooked his own supper, cleaned his own house, and made his own bed. One night he came home very hungry and made a big supper. It was so much food that he got tired and left the dishes in the sink. The next night he was even hungrier, so he made an even bigger supper and left those dishes too. Day by day, the dirty dishes grew. They filled the sink, then the table, then the bookshelves, then the floor, and even blocked the door. Soon he had no clean dishes left. He ate from a soap dish, then an ashtray, then flower pots, candy dishes, vases, and even the pots he cooked in. His house became full of dirty things, and he could not find his bed or his sink. Then it rained. He loaded everything into his truck and let the rain wash it clean. After that, he put everything away and washed his dishes right after supper every night.

There once was a man who lived all alone in a little house. He did everything himself. One night he made a very big supper because he was very hungry. He ate until he was tired and did not wash the dishes. The next night he was twice as hungry, so he made twice as much food and left those dishes too. As the days went by, he kept eating and getting more tired, and the dirty dishes kept growing. They filled the sink, the table, the bookshelves, and the floor. Soon he could hardly get into his house because dishes were piled by the door. Then he found that there were no clean dishes left. He used a soap dish, an ashtray, flower pots, candy dishes, vases, and finally the pots he cooked in. Everything in the house became dirty, and he could not even find his bed. Then rain came, and he put all the dishes and other things in his truck. The rain washed them clean. After that, he carried everything back, put it away, and washed dishes right after supper from then on.

summaries.summary: Molly Lou Melon was a tiny girl with a big heart. Her mom told her to be true to herself, take responsibility, accept others, and use her strong voice to help people. Molly Lou tried to do these things. At school, she sat with Ronald Durkin and Gertie. Tina Bonkel snickered at them, but Molly Lou stood up and said they were friends. In winter, Molly Lou and Bettina Bonklehead painted on their desks by mistake. Molly Lou said, “me,” and cleaned the desks during recess. In spring, a new boy, Garvin Grape, came to school and talked about gravity. Bettina made fun of him, but Molly Lou said gravity was a big deal and gave Garvin a note inviting him to recess. On the first day of summer, Bettina tripped Garvin, and his glasses flew away. Molly Lou caught the glasses and told Bettina to never do that again. Ronald and Gertie helped Garvin up, and the friends shouted together.

video_title: Bedtime Stories: Welcome Back Sun

summaries.summary: In a small village in Norway, the sun has been gone for many months. The child goes to school in the dark and comes home in the dark. The child calls this long dark time the mercatidin. Mama feels tired and fretful, and Papa works all day inside and does not see the sun. Mama tells a story about a little girl who once climbed Mount Gausta when the sun was lost. The girl walked through snow and cold wind, found the sun behind a black cliff, and led it back to the village. People still make that climb to see the sun. The child asks Papa if they can climb the mountain too, but Papa says to wait. As the days pass, Mama and the child gather branches and put them in water by the window. Then Papa, Mama, and the child pack food and climb up the mountain with other people. At the pass, the sun appears, everyone cheers, and they eat together. Later, the child wakes at home and sees the sun on the snow and the first buds opening. Spring has come.

The story begins in a dark winter village in Norway where the sun has not risen for months. The child feels hungry for sunshine and watches Mama and Papa live through the mercatidin. Mama tells about a little girl from long ago who could not wait for the sun, so she climbed high into the mountains. After days of snow and ice, the girl found the lost sun behind Mount Gausta and brought it back to the valley. Later, the child asks to climb the gauss, but Mama and Papa say to wait. The sky slowly brightens, and Mama and the child gather branches to keep indoors in water. They watch the buds. Then thick gray clouds cover the valley, and even Papa wants the sun to return. Papa, Mama, and the child pack cheese, flatbread, salmon, and water. In the morning they join other people climbing Mount Gausta. At the pass, bright sunlight bursts out, and everyone smiles, waves, and cheers. They eat on the warm rocks, then go home. The child wakes up later and learns that the sun followed them into the valley. The buds have opened, and spring has finally come.

summaries.summary: Ronan was a mighty barbarian leader who invaded, raided, and traded for gold, jewelry, weapons, and tools. One raid went wrong when he found a book and first thought it was useless. He tried to get rid of it, but after seeing a picture, he began reading. He read the first sentence, then more and more until late at night. The next day, his friends Krom, Gunner, and Helgi found him reading instead of raiding. Ronan went raiding with them, but he could not stop thinking about the book. After the raid, he hurried home and read to the end. Soon he wanted more books, so he raided and read again and again until books piled up on his boat. To solve the problem, he built a library and opened it with a celebration. At first his friends mocked books, but Ronan read aloud to them, gave out library cards, recommended books, and started a book club. In the end, the barbarians read books too.

Billy was sent to jail. After a long time, he felt sorry for his thievery and wished his bad mustache would go away. Then his mother got him out of jail, and his father said the new neighbors had a baby coming to play.

summaries.summary: Elephant woke up grumpy. When the doorbell rang, he stomped downstairs and said, “Go away! I’m grumpy.” On the doorstep was a present. Elephant opened the box and found hats. He liked the hats and felt a little happier. Zebra was not happy at first and said, “Go away! I’m grumpy.” Elephant gave zebra a smooth hat, and zebra smiled. They cheered, “Hooray for a hat!” Then they went to turtle, who stayed in his shell, and gave turtle a hat too. Turtle cheered. Next they showed owl. Owl did not want to look, but elephant gave owl a hat, and owl smiled. Elephant, zebra, turtle, and owl marched to lion. Lion did not want visitors, but elephant gave lion his last hat. Lion was still sad because a friend was not feeling well. So elephant, zebra, turtle, owl, and lion made a surprise for giraffe and gave giraffe all the hats. Giraffe felt better, and everyone cheered and said to be a good friend.

summaries.summary: Jerome collected words. While other people collected stamps, rocks, coins, art, bugs, baseball cards, or comic books, Jerome listened for special words everywhere he went. He wrote down words like Peru, Willow, Emerald, Cage, Drift, Bloom, Geometry, Kaleidoscope, Symphony, Aromatic, Vociferous, Effervescent, Molasses, Bellow, and Rex. He kept his favorite words in scrapbooks and sorted them into groups like dreaming, science, sad, action, and poetic. One day, while carrying his words, Jerome slipped and the words flew everywhere. As he picked them up, he saw new and surprising word pairs, and he began making poems and songs from them. He used simple words too, like “I understand,” “I’m sorry,” “Thank you,” and “You matter.” The more words he collected, the better he could share his thoughts and feelings. At the end, Jerome poured his words into the wind from a hill, and children below began to catch words too.

Jerome loved collecting words. He noticed words in signs, books, and sounds, and he saved the ones he liked best. He liked short words, long words, words that sounded nice, and words that matched their meaning. He put them into scrapbooks and organized them by type. Then one day, Jerome slipped while carrying his collections, and all his words spilled out. When he gathered them again, the words were mixed together in new ways. Jerome used the words to make poems and songs, and the words moved and delighted people. He also used simple words to say important things, like “I understand. I’m sorry. Thank you. And you matter.” As Jerome collected more words, he could tell the world more clearly what he was thinking, feeling, and dreaming. In the end, he carried his word collection to the highest hill and let the words go into the wind, where children in the valley below shouted about collecting words from the breeze.

video_title: Bedtime Stories: Ruby Finds a Worry

summaries.summary: Ruby loved swinging high and exploring faraway places in the garden. One day she found a small worry, and it kept growing bigger and bigger. The worry was with her at breakfast, at school, and at night, and it stopped her from doing the things she loved. Ruby tried to ignore it, but she kept worrying about the worry, and that made it huge. Then Ruby saw a boy sitting alone in the park who looked sad, and she noticed he had a worry too. Ruby asked him what was wrong, and as he talked, his worry got smaller. Ruby then talked about her own worry, and her worry shrank too. Soon both worries were gone, and Ruby felt like herself again. Ruby learned that worries do not have to stay forever, and talking to someone can make them shrink.

But the more she thought about it, the bigger it became. One day Ruby saw a boy alone in the park. He looked sad, and Ruby saw that he had a worry too. She asked him about it, and when he told her, his worry began to shrink. Ruby talked about her own worry, and it also became smaller and smaller until it disappeared. Ruby felt happy again and learned that sharing a worry with someone can help it go away.

Then a tiger came by and said exercise might help, so Suki ran, rolled, and walked in different ways. After that, the parrot told him to soak in the river like a crocodile. They told Suki he was a perfectly dandy little elephant, and Suki danced happily with them while the parrot watched.

Again, the duck, pig, and cat would not help, so she cut it herself. Then she took the wheat to the Miller, and the Miller ground it into flour. The Little Red Hen made the flour into dough and baked the bread herself. When the bread was ready, the duck, pig, and cat wanted to eat it. But the Little Red Hen said no, because they had not helped. She and her three chicks ate the warm bread.

Ariel and Flounder swim fast through the ship, but the shark follows them. They escape when the shark gets stuck in an anchor. After that, Ariel and Flounder visit Scuttle the seagull. summaries.summary: One day Mickey Mouse saw a plane fly fast over his car. Mickey wanted to fly too, so he decided to take flight lessons. He went shopping and bought a pilot’s jacket, a cap, and a scarf. The next day he met his teacher, Ducky Lindy, at the airport. Mickey learned that flying is not as easy as it looks. He practiced many lessons, learned about buttons in the cockpit, and learned how to stop a spiral and fly upside down. While Mickey was busy, Minnie, Goofy, Donald, and Daisy asked him to play, but he was always learning to fly. Soon Ducky said Mickey was ready for his first solo flight. Mickey flew well and passed the test. Then he looked for his friends and found them having a picnic with a banner that said, “We miss Mickey.” Mickey landed, joined them, and ate lunch. After that, he said he would take them for plane rides, and Minnie became his first passenger.

summaries.summary: Rapunzel lived in a tall tower with her very long hair. Every day, Mother Gothel said, “Rapunzel, let down your hair,” and Rapunzel pulled her up. Mother Gothel used Rapunzel’s magic hair to stay young and beautiful. Rapunzel did not know that Mother Gothel had stolen her from the king and the Queen. Rapunzel had a friend named Pascal. On her birthday, she saw shining lights in the sky and wished to go see them. Then Flynn, a thief, came to her tower. Rapunzel thought he wanted her hair, but he did not. Flynn took Rapunzel to see the lights. They met friendly people, escaped from Maximus and the Royal Guards, and found their way out of a cave with Rapunzel’s glowing hair. Rapunzel saw the kingdom celebrate the Lost Princess. She learned the truth, and Flynn came back to save her. Mother Gothel hurt Flynn, but Rapunzel’s tear brought him back. Rapunzel went home to the king and the Queen.

One day, Flynn the thief climbed into the tower to hide from Maximus, the horse from the royal guard. Rapunzel thought Flynn wanted her hair, but he did not. She asked him to take her to the lights, and he said yes. They went to a pub, escaped from Maximus and the Royal Guards, and got out of a cave by using Rapunzel’s glowing hair. At the kingdom, Rapunzel saw lanterns, a flag, and a picture of the king, the Queen, and their baby princess. She learned she was the Lost Princess. Mother Gothel took her back to the tower, but Flynn returned to rescue her. Mother Gothel hurt Flynn, then Rapunzel’s tear saved him. Rapunzel went to her real parents and came home at last.

summaries.summary: On the first day of Dragon School, Long goes with his new classmates, Camila, Willie, and Mia. Professor McKay welcomes them and says they will learn their special talents. First, the class tries to cook with fire breath. Professor McKay shows them how to roast a potato with a bright burst of fire. Then the young dragons try, but each one makes a mess. Camila makes lava, Willie makes fire, Mia makes ash, and Long only sprays water because dragons from his home breathe water, not fire. Long worries and tries many ways to make fire, but nothing works. He practices and practices, yet he still cannot do it. At the end of the week, the class gets ready for a picnic. The others cook their food, and Long is asked to roast the pumpkin. He feels sad and thinks he will let everyone down. Professor McKay tells him to try his best. Long remembers to relax and focus, and this time his water turns into hot steam. The pumpkin is steamed, and the class enjoys the picnic together.

summaries.summary: Subway was born the color of midnight, while her mama was the color of dawn, her baba was the color of dusk, and her sister Mitch was the color of high noon. She tried to rub off her dark color with a big eraser and even used Mama’s makeup. Then she ate only light-colored foods and prayed for a miracle to wake up bright as the sun. The next morning, she was still dark. Mama asked her name and told her that brightness is not in skin, and beauty comes from the mind and heart. That night, a shooting star came and took Subway away. The star showed her a story about Night and Day, who were both needed. When Subway woke up, she felt beautiful inside and out and went back into the world.

summaries.summary: Jasper Rabbit needed new underwear, so Mom took him to the store. He saw a pair of creepy underwear that looked cool and comfy, and he asked Mom to buy them. That night, Jasper wore them to bed, but they glowed a ghoulish greenish glow. He got scared, changed into plain white underwear, and hid the creepy pair in the laundry hamper. The next morning, the creepy underwear were on him again, so he threw them in the garbage. But they came back in his dresser drawer. Jasper mailed them to China, but they returned with chopsticks. Then he used Mom’s sewing scissors to cut them up. After that, he checked his drawer and found plain white underwear. He thought the creepy underwear were gone, but they still came back. Jasper finally took a shovel, dug a deep hole at Creek Hanger Hill, and buried them. When he got home, he found only plain white underwear in his drawer. Later, he bought more creepy underwear with his allowance and hung them up like string lights. That night, he was not scared and slept happily.

summaries.summary: Angelina Ballerina loved to dance more than anything. She danced everywhere and often forgot to do other things. Her mother called her to tidy her room and get ready for school, but Angelina wanted only to dance. She danced in her dreams and hoped to be a real ballerina someday. At breakfast she stood on her bed doing curtsies. At school she tried on her mother’s hats, was late, and got scolded. On the playground she spun so fast that the other mouselings could not catch her. After school she danced in the kitchen and knocked over milk and cheddar cheese pies. Her mother was upset and sent her to her room. Then Mr. and Mrs. Mouseling bought Angelina a pink ballet dress and ballet slippers. The next day she went to Miss Lily’s ballet school, worked hard, and was told she might grow up to be a real ballerina. From then on, Angelina came when called, tidied her room, and went to school on time. She practiced every day and later became the famous ballerina Mademoiselle Angelina.

summaries.summary: Martin Luther King, Jr. tells about the fight for civil rights after the March on Washington. Even after new laws were passed, black people still could not vote in Alabama. In Selma, 600 activists began a 54-mile march to Montgomery to ask for voting rights. Police stopped them with billy clubs and tear gas, and many people were hurt, but the marchers stayed peaceful and got back up. Two days later, they tried again with 2,500 people, but they still did not reach Montgomery. On Sunday, March 21, 1965, they tried a third time with 8,000 people. Black and white people, Christians and Jewish people, marched together in rain and tiredness. The world watched, and President Johnson sent troops to protect them. At last, they reached Montgomery with tears of joy. Dr. King says people should answer hate with love, violence with kindness, and keep marching together for freedom.

video_title: 👧🏾 Ruth and the Green Book 📗 Kids Book Black History Month Read Aloud Story

summaries.summary: Daddy drove up in a new automobile, a 1952 Buick called Sea Mist Green. The family planned to use it to visit Grandma in Alabama. Ruth packed her bag and brought Brown Bear. As they left Chicago, Daddy told stories, and Mama packed picnics for lunch. At a service station, Ruth and Mama were told the restroom was for whites only, so they had to go into the woods. Later, they tried to stay in a hotel, but the desk man turned them away. They drove all night and kept singing. Many places would not let them eat, so they ate picnics by the road. In Tennessee, they stayed with Daddy’s friend Eddy and his wife, Alice. Eddy told them about Jim Crow and said they should look for Esso stations. At one Esso station, they learned about The Negro Motorist Green Book. Daddy bought one, and Ruth kept it. It helped them find places to stay, even when the car broke down. In the end, they reached Grandma’s house soon after, and Ruth gave Brown Bear to a scared little boy at the inn.

The trip began when Daddy brought home a 1952 Buick, Sea Mist Green, for the family’s ride to Grandma in Alabama. Ruth was excited and took Brown Bear with her. They left Chicago, and Daddy told stories while Mama made food for the road. At a gas station, Ruth and Mama could not use the restroom because it was for whites only. Later, a hotel would not let them stay there, so they kept driving through the night. The next day they sang songs and ate picnic meals because restaurants would not serve them. In Tennessee, they stayed with Eddy and Alice, who welcomed them warmly. Eddy and Daddy talked about Jim Crow and how things were still hard for Black travelers. Near Georgia, an Esso station owner showed them The Negro Motorist Green Book. Daddy bought it, and Ruth read it carefully. It helped them find a tourist home, a place to fix the broken car, and an inn when they could not reach Grandma that day. Ruth gave Brown Bear to a little boy and shared the Green Book with his mother.

Eddy warned them about Jim Crow laws and told them to look for Esso stations. When the car broke down, the Green Book helped them find a garage and an inn. Ruth later gave Brown Bear to a little boy and showed his mother the Green Book.

summaries.summary: Long ago, before the Civil War, an old sailor named Peg Leg Joe worked on a cotton plantation and helped enslaved people escape. At night, after work, he taught them a song called “Follow the Drinking Gourd,” which was really a secret map to freedom. One day, Molly saw that her husband James had been sold to another master. That night, Molly, James, their son Isaiah, old Hattie, and Hattie’s grandson George sang Joe’s song and followed the stars. They ran through fields, crossed a stream, and hid from the master’s hounds. For many nights and days, they traveled by the signs in the song, sometimes hungry and sometimes in danger. A farm boy once brought them food, and later they reached the Ohio River, where Peg Leg Joe was waiting. He carried them across and sent them to safe houses on the Underground Railroad. In the end, they reached Lake Erie, boarded a steamship, crossed to Canada, and were safe at last.

Peg Leg Joe was an old sailor who wanted to help enslaved people get free. He worked for plantation owners during the day and, at night, taught people a secret song: “Follow the drinking gourd.” The song told them how to travel by stars and land signs to freedom. Molly’s family used the song when James was sold away and their family was torn apart. Molly, James, Isaiah, old Hattie, and George left that night and followed the stars. They ran until they crossed a stream, then hid from the master’s dogs in the woods. For weeks they moved at night and rested by day, using the river bank, dead trees, and the stars to guide them. A kind farm boy gave them bacon and cornbread. At last they found Peg Leg Joe at the Ohio River. He took them across and showed them the Underground Railroad, where safe houses, hidden rooms, and helping farmers waited. After many more stops, they reached Lake Erie and crossed to Canada on a steamship, where freedom was waiting.

summaries.summary: William lived in a small village in Malawi where there were no lights and very little money. At night he dreamed about machines, trucks, and radios, and he listened to his grandpa’s stories. But when the rains stopped, the sun dried the fields and the maize turned to dust. William’s father told the children to eat only one meal a day, and then William had to leave school. He felt sad and sat under a mango tree for many weeks. Later, he found a library with science books and learned how engines and radios worked. One picture showed a windmill that could make electricity and pump water. William decided to build his own “electric wind.” He collected parts from a junkyard and built a machine with help from his cousin Jeffrey and his friend Gilbert. When the wind blew, the blades turned and a bulb lit up. Later, he used his windmill to power lights and pump water for his family.

summaries.summary: Rosa grew up near Montgomery, Alabama, with her mother, brother, and grandparents. Her grandparents told her about slavery and how black people were treated unfairly even after slavery ended. Rosa saw white children ride the school bus to a big school, while she had to walk to a one-room school for black children. When she grew up, she still had to follow unfair rules in stores, on buses, and in public places. Rosa married Raymond, who worked for fairness, and she began helping fight for more rights for black people. One day, a bus driver told her to give up her seat for a white person, but Rosa said no. She was taken to jail, and when she came home, she kept fighting. Many black people stopped riding the buses, and they walked instead. After a year, the Supreme Court said bus segregation was wrong. Rosa later moved to Detroit and kept working for fair schools, jobs, houses, voting rights, women’s rights, and the rights of people in prison.

They walked to school, work, and stores until the rules changed. After the Supreme Court said bus segregation was wrong, Rosa moved to Detroit and continued to fight for fair treatment for many people.

summaries.summary: Lola goes to a school where many children are from far away places. Miss Obie asks the class to draw a picture of their first country. Everyone is excited, but Lola feels sad because she left the island when she was a baby and cannot remember it. She asks for help, and Miss Obie tells her to talk to people who do remember. Lola asks her cousin Leticia, Mrs. Bernard, Jonathan, other neighbors, and Mr. Mir about the island. They tell her about big bats, lots of music, dancing, coconut water, sweet mangoes, bright colors, and hot weather. Lola’s mother also tells her about the hurricane that blew houses away when Lola was born. Then Mr. Mir tells Lola about a terrible monster that scared the island for many years until heroes fought it and banished it. Lola stays up drawing page after page until her island book is finished. The next day she brings it to class, and when Miss Obie asks to see it, Lola opens the book and the island seems to burst out.

At Lola’s school, Miss Obie gives the class a special assignment: draw the country they are originally from. The other children quickly begin talking about pyramids, canals, and their first homes. Leticia remembers blanket-size bats. Mrs. Bernard remembers music and dancing. Jonathan and the people in the barber shop remember coconut water, huge mangoes, and colorful houses and people. Lola also learns from her mother about the hurricane that hit the island when she was born. After that, Mr. Mir tells her the island was once hurt by a terrible monster, but brave heroes fought it and made it leave forever. Lola draws all of these memories into a book. The next day she takes it to class, and when she opens it, the island fills the room with its pictures.

summaries.summary: Molly Lou Melon was the shortest girl in first grade, and she had buck teeth, a funny voice, and clumsy hands. She did not mind because her grandma taught her to walk proudly, smile big, sing out clear and strong, and believe in herself. Then Molly Lou Melon moved to a new town and had to leave her grandma and friends. On the first day of school, Ronald Durkin called her shrimpo, but Molly Lou Melon caught a football, ran under Ronald’s legs, and scored a touchdown. The children were amazed, and Ronald felt foolish. On the next days, Ronald teased her about her teeth, her voice, and her snowflake, but Molly Lou Melon showed her big smile, sang so strongly that Ronald fell back, and made a beautiful snowflake. At the end, Ronald gave her a penny for her tooth, and Molly Lou Melon wrote to her grandma to say her advice was right.

video_title: Ben and Emma's Big Hit by Gavin Newsom | Read Aloud Books for Kids

summaries.summary: Ben loved baseball and could see shapes all around the field, like the diamond, the pitcher’s mound, and the ball curving through the air. But reading was hard for him because he had dyslexia. In class, Miss Kim helped Ben and the other students by matching letters with sounds. Ben did not like that the letter B sounded different from the way he had learned it before. Reading time made him feel nervous and sick, especially when he saw Emma, who always carried big chapter books. During reading group, Ben could not sound out the words, and when he got stuck again, he ran out of the room. Miss Kim found him by the water fountain, and after he took deep breaths, they went back to class. Ben learned that Emma also could not really read her big books yet, and Miss Kim said learning takes practice. Later, the class helped Miss Kim practice baseball, and she finally hit the ball. Ben saw that everyone must keep trying and can get help from their team.

When Ben went to bat in baseball, he noticed the field, the mound, and the ball in a new way. He also knew that books held stories, but reading was very hard for him because he had dyslexia. Miss Kim taught reading by saying letters and their sounds, but Ben got confused and upset, especially when the letter B did not sound like he expected. Reading group was hard for him, and Emma seemed to read easily with her big books. Ben could not make the letters turn into words, and when he felt too upset to stay, he ran out of the classroom. Miss Kim found him and helped him calm down with deep breaths. Back in class, Ben learned that Emma picked big books even though she could not read them yet. Miss Kim said reading takes practice, just like baseball. Then the children helped Miss Kim practice hitting a baseball, and after missing twice, she finally hit the ball. Ben and Emma cheered, and Ben understood that he would keep trying to read with help from his team.

He felt hot, embarrassed, and left the room. Miss Kim found him at the water fountain and helped him breathe and calm down. After they returned, Ben learned that Emma also could not read her big books yet and only pretended she could. Miss Kim said she had once never gotten a hit in baseball, even though she loved the sport. Ben and Emma then helped teach Miss Kim to hit a ball at recess. She missed two times, then hit the ball and was very happy. Ben saw that trying hard and getting help mattered in both reading and baseball.

video_title: The Incredible Shrinking Lunchroom by Michal Babay | Read Aloud Books for Kids

summaries.summary: Parley Elementary had a lunchroom that was very loud and crowded. Students could not find places to sit, and they wrote to Mrs. Mench, the principal, asking for help. Mrs. Mench thought for a while, then made changes that made the lunchroom even worse. First, she put science projects in the room, so there was less space. Then she moved classroom pets there, and the lunchroom filled with snakes, tarantulas, hamsters, and worms. After that, she brought sports teams inside because it was too hot to practice outdoors. Balls flew, whistles blew, and the room became messy and smelly. The students kept sending notes because they were unhappy. At last, when the heat wave ended, Mrs. Mench moved the sports teams back outside, returned the animals to their classrooms, and put the science projects in the hallways. Then the students had a quiet, roomy lunch and thanked her with chocolate and notes.

The lunchroom at Parley Elementary was noisy, crowded, and full of clutter. Students shouted, looked for seats, and could not hear each other, so they sent a letter to Mrs. Mench, the principal. She wanted to help, but her first idea made things tighter by filling the lunchroom with science projects. The students wrote again because they had to squeeze between tables and kept knocking things over. Next, Mrs. Mench moved classroom pets into the lunchroom for a “learning zoo.” A snake got out, tarantulas molted, hamsters squeaked, and worms looked like spaghetti. The students complained again. Then Mrs. Mench brought sports teams inside during a heat wave, and the lunchroom became even louder and messier with balls, rackets, and whistles. Finally, when the heat wave ended, she sent the teams outside, returned the animals to their classrooms, and moved the science projects to the hallways. After that, the students enjoyed a calm lunch and thanked her.

summaries.summary: A peaceful spot talks to help calm down an angry spot, which means anger. It explains that people can feel anger, sadness, and anxiety, but they feel best when they are peaceful. Angry spots can show up when someone feels frustrated, afraid, or hurt. The peaceful spot teaches a special trick. First, put up one hand and imagine four red spots on the fingers and one green spot on the thumb. Then count the spots from 1 to 4 and tap each one. After that, fill your lungs with peaceful air and coat your spots with love and care. The story then shows this trick being used in different situations. When someone cannot draw the way they want, the angry spot gets big. When a toy is taken, the angry spot gets big again. The trick helps the angry spot get smaller. In the end, the calm child can think clearly, find a missing dinosaur, and see that a spilled painting is really splatter art.

summaries.summary: The story begins with a peaceful spot and a blue sadness spot. The narrator explains that a sadness spot can show up when someone feels upset, disappointed, or has lost something. Sadness is one of many emotions, and people feel best when they calm it into a peaceful spot. The narrator says sadness can be seen in small or large spots, and it is okay to have it, but it should not stay too long. A sadness spot can be helped by other people, and it can show even if someone is not crying. If a person is frowning, moping, lonely, or worried, they may need a friend. The story shows ways to help, like asking if they are okay, listening, saying hello to a new kid, helping find a lost unicorn, giving a hug, and sharing happy memories. It also shows ways to calm your own sadness spot with music, drawing, writing, and a hand-tracing breathing trick.

The story starts by saying a sadness spot is a blue spot that may look like it needs a hug. It can appear when someone is sad, lonely, disappointed, worried, or has lost a pet, friend, or family member. The narrator explains that people can help each other with sadness spots by noticing body language, like frowning or moping, and by being a friend. If someone feels alone, another person can ask if they are okay, listen, and say they are not alone. When a new kid comes to class, saying hello and introducing them to friends can help. If a problem seems big, teamwork can help make it smaller. The story also shows helping someone find a lost unicorn and comforting someone with a hug and happy memories. At the end, the narrator teaches ways to calm your own sadness spot, like using music, drawing, writing, and tracing spots on your palm while taking deep breaths.

A peaceful spot and a sadness spot are introduced at the beginning of the story. The narrator says sadness can happen when someone feels upset, disappointed, or has a loss. It is one of many emotions, along with anxiety and anger. The story explains that sadness spots can be small or large, and it is okay to have one, but people feel better when it calms down. A sadness spot may not always come with tears, so people should look for signs like frowning, moping, or seeming lonely. The narrator shows how friends can help by listening, welcoming a new classmate, and offering support when someone misses friends or feels they do not fit in. The story also includes helping find a lost unicorn and comforting someone who has lost a pet, friend, or family member. In the end, the narrator gives a calming trick: circle spots on your palm, count, and take deep breaths to help the sadness spot become peaceful.

summaries.summary: A confidence spot helps a child believe in themself. It can sit on a shoulder and whisper kind words, or stay by the side and hold a hand. The confidence spot grows when people feel love, learn new things, and use brave words like, “I am brave. I am loving. I am kind.” Family, teachers, and guardians help this spot grow by encouraging children to try new things. The story says children can also help their own confidence spot grow. They can set goals, keep practicing, be creative, and try again after mistakes. Courage, kindness, positivity, determination, and smiling all help too. Even when something feels hard, children can keep going and learn from it. The story ends by reminding children to use the affirmation card each day and listen to the voice inside their heart.

summaries.summary: A little spot of love tells us that love is the feeling we get when we care about someone or when someone cares about us. Love can grow big, and that is okay because everyone needs to be loved. When love grows, people feel good about themselves and treat others better. The story shows many ways to grow a love spot. Words can help, like saying “I love you,” giving compliments, or writing a kind note or letter. Confidence can help too, by saying good things to yourself like “I am brave,” “I am loving,” and “I am kind.” Actions also grow love, such as helping clean up or doing something nice for someone. Spending time together, listening carefully, playing, giving gifts, and sharing hugs, high fives, fist bumps, waves, and thumbs up can also show love. The story ends by saying people like different ways of being loved, and it asks the reader to think about their favorite way to grow a love spot.

summaries.summary: Scribblespot is all tangled up with emotions and does not feel well. The story says it is healthy to have feelings, but when they get mixed together, it can be hard to know what you feel. To help, the story shows different spots for different emotions. The green peaceful spot is calm and relaxed and scribbles trees and vines. The blue sadness spot appears when someone feels upset, disappointed, or has lost something, and it scribbles clouds and teardrops. The yellow happiness spot shows joy and scribbles sunshine and flowers. The gray anxiety spot feels worried or scared and does not scribble anything because it worries it will not look good. The orange confidence spot believes in itself and scribbles strength and determination. The red anger spot feels frustrated, afraid, or hurt and scribbles chaos. At first, the story forgets love, but then adds the love spot, which scribbles hearts. After that, Scribblespot is not tangled anymore and makes a rainbow because every emotion is inside us.

It shows how each emotion can look in scribble art. Peaceful is a green spot that draws trees and vines. Sadness is a blue spot that draws glooby clouds and teardrops. Happiness is a yellow spot that draws sunshine and flowers. Anxiety is a gray spot that worries and draws nothing. Confidence is an orange spot that draws strength and determination. Anger is a red spot that draws chaos. Then the story remembers love, which includes caring, friendship, kindness, and respect, and the love spot draws hearts. After all the emotions are named, Scribblespot is no longer tangled. He scribbles a rainbow, showing that every emotion is inside us, and the story invites readers to scribble their own emotions with crayons.

He could be green, baby blue, or many bright colors, and he liked changing colors as he walked along. One day, Scribble went on a short walk and found a house. He stopped and said hello, and he asked if they could play. The house had never seen anyone like Scribble before. It asked what he was and then said his lines were not straight and his colors were too bright. Scribble asked for a chance, but the house told him to go away. Scribble felt very sad, but he changed his colors and kept walking. Then he met the sun and the clouds, and they also told him to go away. Scribble said that being different did not make him bad. The next day, the house, the clouds, and even Rainbow came back and asked him to play. Scribble forgave them, and they all made beautiful art together.

After that, the cookie felt more confident, kept writing, and learned that people can be smart in different ways.

summaries.summary: A little spot of love explains that love is the feeling you get when you care about someone or when someone cares about you. Love can grow big, and that is okay because everyone needs to be loved. The story shows many ways to grow a love spot. Words can help, like saying “I love you” or giving compliments such as “You are smart.” Writing can also help, like making a surprise note or letter. Confidence matters too, because kind words to yourself can help you feel brave, loving, and kind. Actions are another way to show care. Helping someone clean up, listening closely, and spending quality time can make others feel loved. Friendship, gifts, hugs, high fives, fist bumps, waving, and thumbs up can all grow a love spot. The story ends by saying people like different kinds of love, and asks the reader to share their favorite way to grow a love spot.

The other eggs did not follow rules. They stayed up too late, ate sugary cereal, cried, and broke things on purpose. He decided to leave the carton and go on his own. On the road, he spent time walking, reading, floating in a river, writing in a journal, breathing, and painting. Slowly, his shell healed. Then he went back home, and the other eggs were happy to see him. He understood that the other eggs did not need to be perfect, and he did not need to be perfect either.

summaries.summary: The story explains that there is a peaceful spot and an anxiety spot. The anxiety spot shows up when a person feels worried, nervous, anxious, or scared. It can appear when trying new things, like playing soccer or taking a test, and it often asks, “What if?” The story says you can answer, “I can do this,” to help turn the anxiety spot into a peaceful spot. Eating healthy food, getting enough rest, and using music, drawing, or writing can help keep anxiety small. When worries grow fast, a child can use a hand trick, say the calming words, and take deep breaths to blow the worry away.

The story teaches a way to shrink an anxiety spot when it grows quickly. First, a child looks at their hand and imagines five gray spots on the fingers and one green spot on the palm. Using the pointer finger of the other hand, they draw an imaginary line from a gray spot to the green spot and say, “From the tip of my finger to the middle of my palm, I can do this. I can be calm.” This is meant to move worry from the gray anxiety spot to the green peaceful spot. Then the child takes a deep breath and blows the worry away while repeating, “This worry grew too big and cannot stay.” After that, only a calm green spot remains. Slow, deep breaths help calm anxiety and stop it from causing more worry.

The story then shows how to use the trick in real situations. On the first day of school, a child may feel scared because they are away from their parents or guardian, and they may worry about meeting new people or not fitting in. I will see you later.” The story also gives another example at a party, where a child may worry that people will not like them. Instead of letting the worry grow, they use the same trick, calm the anxiety spot, and remind themselves, “This party is fun.”

The story explains that each time a person shrinks their anxiety spot, their peaceful spot becomes stronger.
