Cleo said these differences made everyone special. Ashura understood the lesson and joined Bella and her friends in tag and other games. When he got home, he told his family about his day and wished to go back to the park again soon.

He washes his hands, eats with his mouth closed, helps clean up, and says “thank you” and “goodbye.”

He also says “excuse me” when he needs to pass in front of people. When he sneezes, he uses a handkerchief or tissue. Clifford has many friends, and he shares his toys with them. When he is finished playing, he puts his toys away, and his friends help too. He is also a good tennis player who follows the rules, stays calm when angry, and acts like a good sport whether he wins or loses.

He uses a handkerchief or tissue when he sneezes. He shares his toys with his friends, and they help him put them away. Clifford is also a terrific tennis player who obeys the rules. He calls ahead, arrives on time, knocks before entering, wipes his feet, greets his sister and her friend, washes his hands before dinner, helps clean up, and says “thank you” and “goodbye” before leaving.

summaries.summary: Central Park has a zoo where many animals live with their own families. In the penguin house, Roy and Silo are two boy penguins who do everything together. They bow, walk, sing, swim, and sleep in a nest of stones they build for themselves. Mr. Gramzy, their keeper, sees them and thinks they are in love. Roy and Silo watch the other penguin families, but they do not have an egg or a baby. One day Roy brings a rock to the nest, and Silo sits on it, but nothing hatches. Then Mr. Gramzy brings them a real egg that needs care. Roy and Silo take turns keeping it warm, turning it, and sitting with it day and night. After a while, the egg cracks open, and a baby penguin comes out. They name her Tango. Roy and Silo feed her, sing to her, and snuggle her. Tango grows strong, swims with them, and the children at the zoo cheer for the family.

The child wishes the ostrich back to the zoo, and the next morning he is gone. The child then plans to visit the zoo and wish for a unicorn.

summaries.summary: I am Jazz. Jazz loves pink, silver, and green. She likes dancing, singing, backflips, drawing, soccer, swimming, makeup, and pretending to be a pop star. She loves mermaids most of all and sometimes wears a mermaid tail in the pool. Her best friends are Samantha and Casey, and they all have fun together with princess gowns, high heels, cartwheels, and trampolines. Jazz says she has a girl brain and a boy body. When she was little, her mom called her a good boy, but Jazz said, “No, mama, good girl.” Her family was confused because she liked princesses and mermaid costumes, not trucks or superheroes. Jazz kept saying she was a girl and felt unhappy wearing boy clothes. Then her parents took her to a new doctor, who asked many questions and told them the word transgender. After that, Jazz could wear girl clothes to school, grow her hair long, and change her name to Jazz. Some teachers and kids were confused, and some teased her, but the friends who knew her were kind.

summaries.summary: When little box turtle Terence hatched, his parents saw that something was missing, but they were not upset. They gave him a name and a shell that fit him just right. Terence liked his shell because it kept him dry on wet days, safe from strangers, and warm on scary nights. Then one day, someone said, “Your shell is weird!” Terence felt bad and left his shell to look for a better one. He searched high and low and tried many shells. Some looked sleek, some looked classy, some looked fasty, and one had polka dots, but none of them fit. Terence gave up. Then a hermit crab showed kindness and helped him. Terence found his old shell again, but it had changed. He and the hermit crab fixed it together. They worked on it for a long time, and the shell was finished. It was still weird, but Terence was happy because he was more than just his shell.

summaries.summary: Germs are very tiny, so people cannot see them. They can be in the air, in food and water, on the body, and on things people touch. Germs are not for sharing because they can make people sick. When a person coughs or sneezes, the germs can come out. The story says to cover the nose with a tissue and cover the mouth too. If germs get on hands, they can spread when people hold hands, play games, or give high fives. Germs can stay on doorknobs, coins, phones, keyboards, shoes, pets, toys, poles, sponges, and the toilet. They can stay there for up to two hours. To wash germs away, use warm water and lots of soap. Scrub the hands, rinse them, and dry them with a clean towel. Wash hands before eating and after many dirty things.

summaries.summary: Sophia Valdez was a baby who liked to help. Her Abuelo also helped people in Blue River Creek by doing chores, walking pets, and visiting lonely friends. Each morning, Abuelo walked Sophia to class, and they went home together on Blue River Pass. One day, a pup chased a squirrel and ran away. Sophia and Abuelo followed it up a hill made of trash. The hill broke, and they fell into mud. Abuelo got hurt, and the next day Sophia walked to school alone. She did not like that the hill of trash was still there. Sophia decided to fix it and make a new park. She asked neighbors for ideas and drew a map. Then she learned the town thought she would build it alone. Sophia felt scared and went to city hall. At first, the clerk said she was only a kid and could not build a park. Sophia spoke up, and the mayor let her start a petition. With help from family, neighbors, and school friends, the town built the park together.

summaries.summary: Mom is cooking in the kitchen, and Grandma stands nearby as they get ready for New Year’s. They talk about a dragon that can bring health and fortune. Every year, people decorate the street with fai chan and red lanterns, and this year they look for a real red dragon. They try many traps. First they use food, but the dragon comes back for more. Then they try a cozy dragon inn, but it does not work. They try loud bees and big gold bait, but the dragon still gets away. At last, they use the dragon dance, which the dragon loves. The child has fun, but the dragon is still not caught. The family makes a mess and cleans up together. The child feels sorry, but Mom hugs them and says, “I love this dragon.” Then they watch fireworks with Mom and Grandma and feel lucky together.

summaries.summary: Pip lived on an island in the middle of the sea with other birds. They stayed on the ground under a tree and ate seeds and old fruit. Pip wanted something more and wanted to reach high places. First she tried to jump up to a piece of fruit, but she missed. The other birds laughed and said there was no such thing as jumping birds. Then Pip tried running up the tree, but that did not work either. The birds laughed again. After that, she tried flapping her wings, but she still stayed on the ground. That night, Pip sat alone and saw a firefly flying high. This gave her hope. In the morning she tried again. She ran, leaped, and finally flew up to the fruit and took a bite. After that, Pip showed the other birds how to fly, and soon their home was the sky.

The other birds laughed each time and said birds do not jump, run, or fly. Pip felt like quitting that night, until she saw a firefly flying by. She decided to try one more time. Before dawn, she went back to the tree. She flapped, ran, and leaped, but first she fell hard. Still, she stood up again and tried once more. This time Pip flew to the fruit and ate it. Then she taught the other birds how to fly, and they all lived in the sky.

When she gets to school, she goes into the elevator while other children walk down the hallway. She goes to the library, where she takes more than five books, even though the sign says only five. Later, she draws a picture of herself riding a giant turtle while other children draw trees and cats. She reaches out to a student no one else wanted to talk to, enjoys the rain while others hide, and then speaks at show and tell. At the end, she rides the bus home with her new friend, rests with her cat, and gets ready for bed, saying she will be fierce again tomorrow.

summaries.summary: On January 1st, Squirrel hangs up her new nut of the month calendar and hears on the radio that it is a good day to make a resolution. She asks Bear at the Lonewood library what a resolution is. Bear explains that it is a promise to yourself to be better or help others. Bear says his resolution is to teach others how to read, and he plans to teach Skunk when she gets well. Squirrel visits sick Skunk, who says she wants to learn to read too. To cheer her up, Squirrel plays hide-and-seek and pops up with “boo!” until Skunk laughs. Dr. Owl comes and says Skunk is feeling better and can visit Bear after a healthy lunch. Squirrel keeps trying to make her own resolution while helping Mole, Turtle, Porcupine, and the other animals. At the diner, Rabbit tells her to think of a way to improve herself or use what she is good at to help others. Squirrel realizes she has already been helping everyone and has made her first resolution.

video_title: Little Blue Truck's Christmas by Alice Schertle and Jill McElmurry

summaries.summary: December comes, and Little Blue Truck is full of cheer. Blue has a Christmas delivery job. Five green trees are loaded onto the truck, and Blue says, “Beep, let’s hit the road.” Blue meets friends along the way who need trees. The goose honks and takes the big tree. Then the cow moos and takes the tall tree. Next the pig oinks and takes the fat tree. After that, the goat says, “Ma,” and takes the short tree. Each time a tree is given away, there are fewer trees left in the truck. At the end, only one tree remains. Little Blue Truck still needs a Christmas tree, so Blue beeps, “This one’s for me.”

summaries.summary: Schmelf worked in Santa’s workshop checking lists to see which children were naughty or nice. Near Christmas, he saw many good children who would not get presents from Santa. He felt sad and went to the head elf. The head elf told him those children were Jewish. They did not celebrate Christmas. They celebrated Hanukkah with their families, and their moms and dads gave the gifts. Schmelf went home and later visited one house on the list. He saw menorahs, dreidels, gelt, and latkes. He also saw presents for each night of Hanukkah and heard about the story of the Maccabees and the oil that lasted eight days. Schmelf understood Hanukkah and told Santa. Santa was happy and gave Schmelf a new job. Schmelf got white and blue clothes, a special sleigh, and a Jewish reindeer named Asher. Now Schmelf travels to bring Hanukkah joy and help children get special gifts.

Santa gave Schmelf a special new job, Hanukkah clothes in white and blue, a flying sleigh, and Asher the Jewish reindeer so he could bring magic to Jewish children every year.

She sang to birds and frogs, and she loved the stage. Tamika had been many things in shows, like a cucumber, a space cowgirl, a dinosaur, and a singing mermaid. Now she wanted to be a princess in the Snow White musical, so she went to auditions on both days. On the first day, she helped other children and heard some kids say she was too tall, too chubby, and too brown to be Snow White. Tamika felt sad and stopped dancing for a while. At dinner, her mom and dad told her she was tall enough, chubby enough, and brown enough to be a perfect princess. The next day, Tamika went back, remembered their words, and sang and danced with joy. She shone on stage and showed that she could be a princess.

When he sits down to practice cello in the dining room, his mother calls him from upstairs, but he asks for a minute and keeps playing. At home, practicing is hard because he lives with three older siblings, and his mother has been acting strangely about his music. Marcus remembers that her younger brother Shane was a very gifted cellist who died at age 12, the same age Marcus is now. Because he cannot stop hearing music, Marcus first talked about it constantly as a child, then visited a doctor who suggested medication. Later he began playing whatever instruments he could find, and adults started noticing his talent. One day his mother brings him a letter from Larkspur Academy for the Performing Arts in New York State, inviting him to study there for free after a scout heard him perform. Marcus is shocked, and then hears an even louder, strange burst of music that his mother cannot hear.

Marcus Geller is a boy who hears music no one else notices, and he feels he has to play it whenever he can. While he sits with his cello in the dining room, his mother calls him from her bedroom, but he asks for a minute and starts practicing. Marcus finds it hard to get privacy in a house with three older siblings. He also thinks his mother has become upset because her brother Shane, who was an excellent cellist, died when he was 12, the same age Marcus is now. As a child, Marcus tried to explain the music by humming and talking about it, but after a doctor suggested medicine, he kept the music secret and began copying it on different instruments. This led to praise from teachers and other adults, though Marcus did not feel sure he deserved it. Then his mother gives him a printed letter from Elle Definium, director of Larkspur Academy for the Performing Arts, inviting him to study in New York State with full costs paid. Marcus is stunned, and at that moment he hears a huge, unfamiliar blast of music that his mother cannot hear.

Marcus Geller hears music inside his head or around him that no one else seems to notice. One afternoon, after he sits with his cello in the dining room, his mother calls him upstairs, but he asks for a minute and plays instead. Marcus has always struggled to practice at home because he has three older siblings, and now he thinks his mother is upset because his talent reminds her of her younger brother Shane, a gifted cellist who died at age 12. Marcus remembers that when he was younger, he kept talking and humming about the music, so his parents took him to a doctor who suggested medication. After that, Marcus made the music a secret and started using whatever instruments he could find to copy the melodies. Adults began paying attention to his talent, even though he felt uncertain about it. Later, his mother gives him a letter from Larkspur Academy for the Performing Arts in New York State, offering him free study after a scout heard him perform. Marcus is shocked, and then he hears a sudden, overwhelming new sound that his mother cannot hear.

Marcus Geller lives with music that only he seems to hear, and he cannot fight it. When he sits down to practice cello, his mother calls him from upstairs, but he asks for a minute and begins playing. He knows practicing at home is difficult because of his three older siblings, and he believes his mother is reacting badly to his playing because her younger brother Shane, who was a very talented cellist, died when he was 12, the same age Marcus is now. Marcus once told people about the music all the time and hummed it aloud, but after a doctor suggested medication, he decided to keep it secret. He then started using instruments from school and from his uncle’s old collection to copy the melodies he heard. This brought attention from teachers and other adults. One day, his mother returns with a printed message from Elle Definium of Larkspur Academy for the Performing Arts, inviting Marcus to study there in New York State with all costs covered. Marcus asks if it is a joke, and then he is hit by a loud, strange burst of music that only he hears.

Marcus Geller hears music that nobody else notices, and he keeps trying to play along with it. At the beginning, he sits in the dining room with his cello, but his mother calls him from upstairs. He asks for a minute and keeps practicing, even though home is crowded because he has three older siblings. Marcus thinks his mother is uneasy about his music because her younger brother Shane was once a brilliant cellist and died at age 12, the same age Marcus is now. As a child, Marcus spoke and hummed about the music until his parents took him to a doctor, who suggested medicine. Marcus then chose to keep the music secret and began copying it on any instrument he could find. His talent drew attention from teachers and other adults, though he did not feel sure about it. Later, his mother shows him a letter from Larkspur Academy for the Performing Arts in New York State, offering him a place to study for free after a scout heard his recital. Marcus is surprised, and then he hears a powerful new blast of music that his mother cannot hear.

Then the baguette starts to crack and crack. Soon, there is no more baguette left. Nanette gets upset and thinks her mom will be mad. She asks to go home, and her dad asks where the baguette is. Nanette says she did not forget it, but she is sad. Then Stan says, “I ate the baguette.” Mom hugs him. The warm baguette was wonderful. The day is not over yet, so they start again and get another baguette from Juliet. Now they are all set, and the day is one Nanette will not soon forget.

summaries.summary: In a cave in the woods, a great brown bear sleeps in his deep, dark lair through the cold winter. The wind blows, but the bear snores on. Then an itty bitty Mouse creeps into the cave from the snow. Mouse lights some twigs with a small spark. Soon Hair comes to the den and says, “Long time no see!” Mouse and Hair pop white corn and share food, but the bear snores on. A badger comes by with honey nuts, and they eat together. Then a gopher and a mole come up through the floor, and a raven flies in through the door. They all stay in the bear’s den, talk, and laugh, but the bear snores on. Later, Hair stokes the fire, and a small spark makes the bear sneeze. The bear wakes up, growls, and roars because everyone has been in his lair. Mouse tells him not to fret, and they share more food. When morning comes, the bear cannot sleep, and his friends snooze.

A great brown bear sleeps in a cave in the woods all winter long. The cold wind howls outside, but the bear snores on. An itty bitty Mouse tiptoes into the cave and lights a little fire with twigs. Soon Hair appears, and Mouse and Hair pop corn and drink together. The bear keeps sleeping. Then a badger comes in with honey nuts, and everyone shares the food. After that, a gopher and a mole come up through the floor, and a raven comes through the door. They all crowd into the bear’s den, chatter, and enjoy the night, but the bear snores on. Later, Hair stokes the fire, and a small spark makes the bear sneeze. The bear wakes up and gets mad. He says the friends have been in his lair and had all the fun while he slept. Mouse tells him not to worry, and the group shares more food. When the sun rises, the bear cannot sleep, but his friends do.

summaries.summary: In a cave in the woods, a great brown bear sleeps through the long cold winter. He snores loudly while the wind howls outside. One day, an itty bitty Mouse tiptoes into the cave from the snow. Mouse lights some twigs with a small spark, and soon the cave begins to fill with other animals. Hare arrives first, and Mouse and Hare pop corn and brew drinks together. Then Badger comes with honey nuts, and they share the food. Gopher and Mole tunnel up, and Raven flies in through the door. They all talk, eat, and stay warm in the bear’s den while the bear keeps sleeping. Later, Hare stirs the fire and makes a sneezy mixture that wakes the bear. The bear gets angry because everyone has been having fun in his lair. Mouse calms him down and offers more food and company. By dawn, the bear is full and awake, and his friends are asleep.

summaries.summary: Three baby owls, Sarah, Percy, and Bill, lived with their owl mother in a hole in a tree. One night they woke up and found that their mother was gone. Sarah said she was hunting for food, Percy agreed, and Bill said, “I want my mummy!” The baby owls came out of their home and waited on the tree. Sarah sat on a big branch, Percy on a small branch, and Bill on an old bit of ivy. It was dark in the wood, and they stayed brave while they waited. They moved together onto one branch and thought about where their mother might be. Sarah worried she could be lost, and Percy wondered if a fox got her. Bill still said, “I want my mummy!” Then they closed their eyes and wished for her return. Soon their mother came softly through the trees. The baby owls cried “Mummy!” and flapped and danced. Their mother was back, and Bill said, “I love my mummy!”

summaries.summary: George was the scruffiest giant in town. He wore old brown sandals and a patched gown, and he wished he could be smart. One day he found a shop full of new clothes. He bought a shirt, trousers, a belt, a stripy tie, socks, and shiny shoes. Then he met a giraffe who was cold. George gave the giraffe his tie for a scarf. Next he met a goat whose sail had blown away, so George gave the goat his shirt. Then he met a mouse and her babies, and he gave them one shoe for a house. After that, he gave a fox one sock for a sleeping bag, and a dog his belt for a path over the bog. George kept walking, but now his trousers fell down and he felt cold. He went back to the shop, but it was closed. Then he found his old gown and sandals, put them on, and felt cozy again. At home, the animals gave him a present with a gold paper crown and a card.

George was a giant who did not like being the scruffiest giant in town. He went to a new shop and bought smart clothes. On the way home, he helped many animals. A giraffe needed a warm scarf, so George gave away his stripy tie. A goat needed a sail, so George gave away his shirt. A white mouse and her babies needed a house, so George gave them one shiny shoe. A fox needed a dry sleeping bag, so George gave away one sock. A dog needed a safe path across a bog, so George gave away his belt. After helping everyone, George felt cold because his trousers were falling down. He went back to the shop for more clothes, but it was shut. Then he saw his old gown and sandals and put them on. They felt comfortable, and he went home happy. Outside his door, the animals were waiting with a big present. Inside was a gold paper crown and a card.

George was a giant in old clothes. He wanted to be the smartest giant in town, so he bought new smart clothes from a shop. As he walked home, he met a giraffe, a goat, a mouse with babies, a fox, and a dog. Each one needed help. George gave his tie to the giraffe for a scarf, his shirt to the goat for a sail, one shoe to the mouse family for a house, one sock to the fox for a sleeping bag, and his belt to the dog for a path over the bog. George sang as he went, but then his trousers started to fall down. He felt cold and had to go back to the shop. The shop was closed, so he sat on the doorstep and cried. Then he saw his old gown and sandals in a bag. He put them on and felt warm and cozy. When he got home, all the animals were there with a present. They gave him a gold paper crown and a card.

Inside the present was a gold paper crown and a card for George.

video_title: The Selfish Crocodile [Children's story | Read Aloud]

summaries.summary: Deep in the forest, a large crocodile lived in a river. He was selfish and shouted at all the other creatures to stay away. He said the river was his and that he would eat anyone who came near. Because of this, no fish, frogs, crabs, or other animals came to the river. The forest creatures were afraid and went far away to drink and bathe. One morning, the forest heard a loud groaning sound. The crocodile was lying on his back with a swollen jaw and tears in his eyes. The animals watched, but no one helped. Then a little mouse came. He ran along the crocodile’s body, went into his mouth, and pulled out a bad tooth. The crocodile’s pain stopped. He thanked the mouse, gave him a nut, and later became his friend. After that, the crocodile invited all the animals to the river, and they came back safely.

A selfish crocodile lived in a river in the forest. Every day he shouted, “Stay away from my river!” He did not let any animals drink or bathe there. The fish, tadpoles, frogs, crabs, and crayfish stayed away, and the forest animals had to travel far to find water. One morning, the animals heard a loud noise. They found the crocodile in great pain, holding his swollen jaw. The animals looked on, but nobody helped him. Then a small mouse came and climbed onto the crocodile. He went into the crocodile’s mouth and pulled out a bad tooth. The crocodile felt better right away. He thanked the mouse and gave him a juicy nut. The mouse later buried the tooth under a tree. After this, the crocodile and the mouse became friends. The crocodile sent an invitation to all the animals and told them they could drink and bathe in the river again. The river soon filled with fish and other creatures.

In a forest river lived a big crocodile who wanted the river for himself. He chased other animals away and told them not to come near. He said he would eat them if they did. So the animals stayed away, and they had to go to other rivers and streams when they were thirsty. Every day the crocodile lay in the sun and picked his teeth with a stick. Then one morning he cried out in pain. The forest creatures found him with a swollen jaw. They watched him, but they did not help. A tiny mouse came along and bravely climbed over the crocodile’s body. He went into the crocodile’s mouth and pulled out a bad tooth. The crocodile’s toothache stopped. He gave the mouse a nut, and the mouse buried the tooth. After that, the crocodile was kind to the forest animals. He invited them to use the river, and they were no longer afraid. Soon the river had fish, tadpoles, frogs, crabs, and crayfish again.

video_title: The Lion Inside [Children's story | Read Aloud]

summaries.summary: In a dry, dusty place, a big flat rock stood on gold sand. Under the rock, a very tiny brown mouse lived in a small house. He was so small that no one noticed him. He was stepped on, sat on, and left out. Up on the rock, a strong lion lived. He was loud and proud, and everyone looked at him. The mouse wished he could be more like the lion. One dark night, he had an idea. He decided to learn how to roar. He climbed up the rock to ask the lion for help. The lion woke up and saw the mouse. He got scared and backed away. The mouse said he was a friend and wanted to learn to roar. After that, the mouse felt bigger inside. The lion and the mouse became friends and shared the rock. The lion still roared, but now he roared with laughter.

A little brown mouse lived under a big rock in a sandy place. He was quiet and small, and nobody noticed him. A lion lived on top of the rock. He was loud, strong, and important. The mouse wanted to be brave like the lion. One night, he thought about changing. He decided to learn how to roar. He climbed and climbed until he reached the lion. The mouse asked the lion to teach him. The lion woke up and felt scared when he saw the mouse. Then the mouse spoke kindly and said he was a friend. The lion stopped being afraid. The mouse did not need to roar to be strong. He found his own voice. After that, the mouse and the lion lived as friends and shared the rock. The mouse felt bigger inside, and the lion laughed instead of only roaring.

In a place of dry sand and a golden rock, a tiny brown mouse lived below the rock. He was small and often missed. On top of the rock lived a big lion. He was loud and made sure everyone saw him. The mouse looked up at the lion and wished he could be like him. Then, late at night, the mouse had a brave idea. He wanted to learn how to roar. He climbed the rock and went to the sleeping lion. When the lion woke up and saw the mouse, he became frightened and moved back. The mouse told the lion not to be afraid and said he was a friend. The mouse learned that he could speak out without roaring. From then on, the mouse and the lion were together as friends. They shared the rock, and the lion still roared, but now it was with laughter.

A very small brown mouse lived in a tiny house under a big rock. He was so small that others ignored him. On top of the rock, a lion lived. He was big, loud, and strong. The mouse wanted to be like the lion. One night, he decided to change. He climbed up the rock to ask the lion to teach him how to roar. When he reached the lion, he woke him up and asked his question. The lion opened his eyes and got scared. He moved back and said, "Don't hurt me." The mouse said he was a friend and wanted them to have fun together. After that, the mouse felt strong inside. He did not need to roar to matter. The lion and the mouse became a pair and shared the rock. The lion still roared, but now he roared with laughter.

Under a craggy rock in a sunny, dusty place, a little brown mouse lived alone. He was tiny and often forgotten. Far above him, a lion lived on the rock. The lion was loud and proud, and everyone noticed him. The mouse wished he could be big like the lion. Then one night, the mouse had a new idea. He would learn how to roar. He climbed the rock, even though it was scary. At last, he reached the lion and asked for help. The lion woke up, saw the mouse, and became afraid. The mouse told him he was not a foe, but a friend. After that, the mouse felt brave and found his own voice. The lion and the mouse shared the rock. They stayed friends, and the lion did not only roar in a loud way anymore. He also roared with laughter.

video_title: Superworm [Children's story | Read Aloud]

summaries.summary: Super Worm is long and strong. He helps many little animals. Baby toad hops onto a big road, and Super Worm makes a lasso to help. Bees are bored, and Super Worm gives them a game. A beetle falls into a well, and Super Worm helps again. Toads, beetles, bees, bugs, snails, and slugs all cheer, “Super Worm is super long. Super Worm is super strong.” Then Wizard Lizard sends his black crow servant to bring Super Worm to him. The wizard uses a magic flower and makes Super Worm look for treasure in the ground. Super Worm digs and digs, but he only finds small things like buttons and a cork. The wizard says he must try again, or the crow will eat him. The garden creatures make a plan. They take the wizard’s magic flower, make a strong web, and trap him. The wizard is pushed into the rubbish dump, and Super Worm comes back.

Super Worm wiggles and squirms, and all the garden creatures clap for him. When baby toad is on a major road, Super Worm uses a lasso to help. When bees are bored, Super Worm gives them a new game. When a beetle falls in a well, Super Worm helps there too. Everyone chants about Super Worm being super long and super strong. Then Wizard Lizard in his lair calls for Super Worm. His servant crow brings Super Worm to him, and the wizard waves a magic flower. He makes Super Worm tunnel and search for treasure in the oil. Super Worm is cross, but he cannot get away. He digs and finds only small things. The wizard says he must try one more time or the hungry crow will eat him. So the garden creatures bring a honeycomb, chew the petals from the magic flower, and make a web. They trap the wizard and send him into the rubbish dump. Then Super Worm returns, and everyone cheers again.

Then the ground rumbles, Super Worm comes back, and everyone cheers and chants again.

video_title: Six Dinner Sid Children's story  Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Sid was a cat who lived in six houses on Aristotle Street. Each night he went from number one to number six to eat six dinners. He had chicken, fish, lamb, mince, fish again, and beef and kidney stew. The people on the street did not talk to their neighbors, so each one thought Sid was only their own cat. Sid had to remember six names and act in six different ways. He was swanky as Scaramouche, had a job as Bob, was naughty as Satan, silly as Sally, smooched as sooty, and acted rough as Schwartz. One cold day, Sid got a cough and was taken to the vet six times. The vet gave him medicine and then noticed six sick cats in Aristotle Street. He called the owners, and they found out about Sid. The owners were angry and said he could only have one dinner a day. Sid then moved to Pythagoras Place, where everyone talked to each other, so everyone knew about his six dinners and nobody minded.

Sid lived in number one, number two, number three, number four, number five, and number six on Aristotle Street. At each house he got a different dinner, so he could eat six dinners every night. As Scaramouche he was fancy, as Bob he worked, as Satan he was naughty, as Sally he was silly, as sooty he gave smooches, and as Schwartz he was tough. Then Sid caught a bad cough on a cold, damp day. He was taken to the vet six times, once with each person. The vet said the cough was not very bad and gave him a spoonful of medicine each time. After seeing the same cat many times, the vet checked his book and saw six cats with coughs on Aristotle Street. He told the owners, and Sid was found out. The owners were angry and said no more six dinners. Sid moved to Pythagoras Place, where everyone knew the truth from the start and did not mind.

summaries.summary: In a tall forest, autumn came and the air turned cool. Most animals had already stored food for winter, but Cyril the squirrel had not. He had spent the year playing and had no food in his hollow. Then he found one pine-cone with the last nuts of the season inside. Just then, Bruce, who always planned ahead, also wanted the pine-cone because he thought he was one short for his own stores. Cyril and Bruce raced after the cone as it fell from the tree and bounced over bushes and rocks. It landed in the water, and both squirrels followed. A bird swept in and carried the cone away. The squirrels almost fell over the edge, but Cyril grabbed a branch and pulled Bruce to safety. After that, Bruce saw how silly they had been. The two squirrels stopped fighting and began to gather food together, sharing and laughing as friends.

Summer was gone in the forest, and autumn made the sky red and the air cold. Bruce, another squirrel, saw it too. Bruce had already gathered much food, but he still wanted this one pine-cone for his stores. Both squirrels rushed after it. Their chase shook the tree, and the cone fell. It bounced on the ground, hit a sleeping bear on the nose, rolled to the water, and then a bird flew in and took it away. Cyril and Bruce chased it too far and nearly fell over the edge. Cyril caught a branch and saved Bruce. Afterward, Bruce said they had been silly and greedy. From then on, Cyril and Bruce gathered food together and shared what they found.

summaries.summary: A tiny snail with an itchy foot lives on a black rock by the sea. She looks at the ships and says she wants to sail because the sea is deep and the world is wide. The other snails tell her to stay still, but she makes a plan to hitch a lift. One night, a great gray blue humpback whale comes when the tide is high and the stars are bright. The whale sings to the snail and carries her on his tail across the sea. They see icebergs, coral caves, shooting stars, big waves, fish, sharks, storms, and golden sand. Then the whale loses his way and is pushed too close to shore by noisy speedboats. The tide goes out, and the whale is left beached in a bay. The snail cannot move him alone, so she crawls to a school, and children and firemen come to help. The tide returns, the whale is saved, and the whale and snail go back home. After that, more snails climb on the whale’s tail and sail too.

Soon a huge humpback whale came in the night. He sang a song and let the snail ride on his tail. The whale carried her over the sea to icebergs, caves under the waves, fiery mountains, and golden sands. The snail saw big waves, fish, sharks, and a stormy sky. Then the whale got lost. Speedboats raced around him and made him swim too close to the shore. The tide went away, and the whale was stuck on the sand. The snail called for help, but the whale could not move on land. The snail crawled to the school in the bay, and the children told the teacher. The children ran to get the firemen and helped make a pool. When the tide came back, the whale was safe. The whale and snail returned to the rock, and the other snails heard their story. Then many snails sailed on the whale’s tail.

summaries.summary: Greta lived in a beautiful forest. One morning she found many forest animals hiding in the garden. A wolf asked her for help because the giants were breaking the forest and ruining their home. The giants kept chopping down trees to build bigger houses, towns, cities, factories, shops, cars, and planes. Soon there was hardly any forest left, and the animals were scared and had nowhere to go. Greta wanted to help, so the next morning she went to the middle of the forest and held a sign that said, “stop!” At first the giants walked past her. On the fourth day, a little boy joined Greta, and then more people and animals came too. They made a huge crowd and stopped the giants. Greta told them the forest was being damaged and the animals were homeless. Everyone shouted for the giants to stop. The giants were sorry, and after that they slowed down, planted gardens, and helped care for the forest until it became beautiful again.

summaries.summary: Little Cell went with her mother to Blueberry Hill to pick blueberries. Cell had a small tin pail, and her mother had a large tin pail. Mother said they would take the berries home and can them for winter. Cell picked a few berries, but she ate many of them right away. Her mother kept walking through the bushes and filling her pail. Cell put one berry in her mother’s pail, then reached in and took it back, pulling out a handful by mistake because the pail was already full of berries. Her mother told Cell to pick her own berries. Cell sat in the bushes and kept eating. On the other side of the hill, Little Bear came with his mother, and he also ate berries instead of picking many. Soon Cell and Little Bear were mixed up with the wrong mothers. Each mother saw the wrong child, then went away to look for her own child. In the end, both children went home with their mothers, and both families had blueberries for winter.

summaries.summary: Nikki wanted new mittens made from wool as white as snow. Baba did not want to knit white mittens at first, because she said one could be lost in the snow. But Nikki wanted them, and Baba made them. She told him that when he came home, she would first look to see if he was safe and sound, and then she would look to see if he still had his snow white mittens. Nikki went out, and one mitten dropped in the snow and was left behind. A mole found it and climbed inside. Then a snowshoe rabbit came, then a hedgehog, then an owl, then a badger, then a fox, then a great bear, and finally a tiny meadow mouse. The mitten stretched and stretched but stayed together. The mouse made the bear sneeze, and the mitten flew into the sky. Nikki saw it and ran to get it back. When he came home, Baba saw that he was safe and sound and still had his mittens.

Nikki went outside, and soon one mitten was lost in the snow. A mole found the mitten and went inside to rest. A snowshoe rabbit joined him, then a hedgehog, then an owl, then a badger, then a fox, then a great bear, and then a little meadow mouse. The mitten became very full, but it did not break. The mouse tickled the bear, and the bear sneezed hard. The mitten flew up into the sky and the animals scattered. Nikki saw the white mitten in the air and ran after it. At home, Baba looked out the window and saw that Nikki was safe and still had his mittens.

summaries.summary: Deep in the woods, an old white cabin stands with pumpkins in the garden. Inside live a cat, a squirrel, and a duck. They make pumpkin soup together: the cat slices the pumpkin, the squirrel stirs, and the duck adds the salt. They eat the soup, play music, and sleep in a quilt made by all three. One morning, the duck wants to be the head cook. He takes the special spoon and says it is his turn to stir. The squirrel and the cat say no, and they fight. The duck is upset and leaves in a wheelbarrow. The cat and squirrel look for him, but they cannot find him. They feel sad and make the soup too salty. Then they search in the dark woods and near a steep cliff. At last they see light in the cabin and find the duck home. They cook soup again, and this time the duck stirs while they stay quiet. The duck teaches the squirrel to measure the salt, and the soup is good again.

In an old white cabin in the woods, a cat, a squirrel, and a duck live together. They make pumpkin soup and share the work. The cat cuts the pumpkin, the squirrel stirs the pot, and the duck adds just enough salt. After supper, they go to bed in a quilt made by all three friends. One day, the duck wakes up early and wants to be the head cook. He takes the squirrel's special spoon and says it is his turn. The squirrel and the cat do not want to give it up, and soon they have a big squabble. The duck says he is leaving because no one lets him help. He packs his things and waddles away. The cat and squirrel search for him all day, but he is gone. Their soup tastes too salty, and they cry into it. Then they go into the dark woods to look for him. Later, they find the duck back at the cabin. They cook pumpkin soup together again, and the duck stirs and shows the squirrel how to add the salt.

summaries.summary: Little Bear asks Mama Bear what she would do if she were the doctor at the zoo. Mama Bear gives answers for many animals who are sick. She would help Ali with the flu, chimp with a limp, deer who cannot hear, mircat who is too fat, Fox with chickenpox, goat with a sore throat, Beaver with a fever, and weasel with the measles. Her ideas are funny and silly, like using a cake with pills, a candy cane, a megaphone, cheetah running, a striped sweatshirt, a frozen milkshake, ice cream, and a ditch. A boy suggested giving him a paper to read, so the mayor agreed. Groundhog opened his eyes and slowly read the paper. Then he still would not come out because he said he was not fed. A little girl suggested breakfast, so the people brought him coffee, toast, and a flower bouquet on a tray. Even then, Groundhog stayed in bed because it was warm. Next, a girl told them to get him slippers because the floor was cold. After wearing slippers, Groundhog danced to the door and stepped outside. Because the sun was bright, a child gave him sunglasses. The mayor said there would be no shadow and the chilly weather was going away. Groundhog then played with the children, and they made a snowman. At the end, he said he would go back to bed and see his friends again when spring came early.

The people shouted again and begged him to come out, but Groundhog said he would stay inside until he was fed. Then a little girl suggested breakfast in bed, so the town served him coffee, toast, and a flower bouquet. Groundhog liked the hot coffee, but he still stayed in bed because it was warm there. After that, another girl said he needed slippers because the floor was chilly. The mayor found a pair, and Groundhog danced to the door. He stepped outside, blinked at the bright light, and received sunglasses. The mayor said the weather was changing. Groundhog played with the children, they made a snowman, and he ended the day by saying he would return to bed and see them again when spring came early.

summaries.summary: In Arendelle, the king and queen had two daughters, Anna and Elsa. Elsa had a secret: she could make ice and snow with her hands. One night, Anna asked Elsa to make the ballroom into a winter wonderland. While the sisters played, Elsa lost control and hit Anna with ice. Anna fell down. The king and queen took the girls to the trolls. Grand Pabbie healed Anna by taking away her memory of Elsa’s magic. He said fear would be Elsa’s enemy. The king and queen closed the kingdom gates and gave Elsa gloves. Elsa stayed away from Anna because she was afraid of hurting her. Later, the girls’ parents were lost at sea. At Elsa’s coronation, Anna met Prince Hans, and they wanted to marry. Elsa would not bless the marriage. Then Elsa’s magic came out in front of everyone, and she ran to the mountains. Anna went after her, met Kristoff, Sven, and Olaf, and learned that only true love could save her frozen heart. In the end, Anna saved Elsa, Elsa ended the winter, and Arendelle was happy again.

Later, the king and queen were lost at sea. When Elsa became queen, the people came to the coronation. Anna met Prince Hans and quickly said yes when he asked her to marry him. Elsa would not give her blessing. Then Elsa’s magic burst out, and Arendelle saw her secret. Elsa fled to the mountains and made an ice palace. Anna followed her with Kristoff, Sven, and Olaf. At the end, Anna chose Elsa’s safety, froze solid, then thawed when Elsa hugged her. Elsa ended the winter, and the sisters were together again.

summaries.summary: In the kingdom of Arendelle, King and Queen had two daughters, Anna and Elsa. Elsa could make ice and snow with her hands, but the family kept this secret. One night Anna asked Elsa to turn the ballroom into a winter wonderland, and Elsa accidentally hit Anna with icy magic. Anna fell unconscious, so the King and Queen took both girls to the trolls. Grand Pabbie saved Anna by taking away her memories of Elsa’s magic and warned that fear would be Elsa’s enemy. The King and Queen closed the kingdom gates, gave Elsa gloves, and tried to keep her powers hidden. Years later, after the parents were lost at sea, Elsa was crowned queen and opened the gates. Anna met Prince Hans, and they quickly fell in love. At the coronation ball, Elsa refused to bless their marriage, and her magic was exposed. Elsa fled to the mountains, and Anna went after her. Along the way Anna met Kristoff, Sven, and Olaf, and they helped her find Elsa and bring back summer.

Anna and Kristoff reached Elsa’s ice palace with Olaf, who was a living snowman Elsa had made. Anna told Elsa that Arendelle was trapped in a terrible winter storm and asked her to stop it, but Elsa said she could not. In her upset, Elsa sent out a blast of ice that struck Anna in the heart. Kristoff took Anna to the trolls, and Grand Pabbie saw ice in her heart. He said only an act of true love could save her, and Anna thought Hans would help. Anna, Kristoff, Sven, and Olaf hurried back to Arendelle, but Hans was not there because he had gone to look for Anna. Hans and his men found Elsa’s palace, attacked her, and knocked her out. They brought Elsa back to Arendelle and put her in the dungeon. Anna found Hans in the library and begged him for a kiss, but he revealed that he had only pretended to love her so he could take over Arendelle. He left Anna to freeze, and Elsa escaped from the dungeon after freezing it shut.

Anna was getting weaker, and Olaf stayed with her and made a fire even though he might melt. He saw Kristoff returning and realized Kristoff cared for Anna. Olaf helped Anna look outside, and she saw Kristoff across the frozen fjord. But then Anna saw Hans standing ready to strike Elsa with his sword. Anna used her last strength to jump in front of Elsa, and Hans’s sword came down just as Anna turned to solid ice. Elsa held her frozen sister and cried. Then Anna began to thaw because her act was one of true love. Olaf understood that love had saved her. Elsa also understood that love was the key to her magic. She ended the winter and brought summer back to Arendelle. Hans was shocked that Anna was alive, but Anna punched him and knocked him back. After that, Arendelle became normal again, and the castle gates stayed open for good. Anna and Elsa were happy to be back together, and the kingdom was happy again too.

At first, Arendelle was a happy kingdom, and Anna and Elsa were close sisters. Elsa had magic that could make ice and snow, but after Anna was hurt, their parents tried to protect her by hiding the power. The trolls helped Anna, and Grand Pabbie warned that fear would grow Elsa’s powers. The gates of Arendelle were closed, and Elsa stayed away from Anna so she would not hurt her. When their parents were lost at sea, Elsa stayed inside until her coronation day. Then Anna met Prince Hans and agreed to marry him, but Elsa would not give her blessing. Their argument made Elsa’s magic burst out, and the people of Arendelle learned her secret. Elsa ran into the mountains, built an ice palace, and covered the land in snow. Anna followed her with Kristoff, Sven, and Olaf, but Elsa could not stop the storm. Anna was then hurt by Elsa’s magic, and the trolls said only true love could save her. Hans later tricked Anna and tried to take over the kingdom, but Anna saved Elsa from him. Anna’s love for Elsa thawed her frozen body, and Elsa ended the winter.

Elsa first used her powers in secret, and one accident changed everything. When Anna was hit by Elsa’s magic, the trolls erased Anna’s memory of the magic and told the royal family to keep Elsa’s power hidden. Years later, after the parents were lost at sea, Elsa opened the gates for her coronation. Anna met Hans, but Elsa refused to approve the marriage. Elsa’s fear and anger made her powers show, so she fled and created an ice palace in the mountains. Anna went after her and met Kristoff, Sven, and Olaf. Together they found Elsa, but Anna was struck in the heart by ice and was told that true love was the only cure. Hans returned to Arendelle, but he was pretending to love Anna and left her to freeze. Olaf helped Anna, and Kristoff came back, but Anna chose to protect Elsa from Hans’s sword. That act of true love thawed Anna, and Elsa learned that love helped her control her magic. She ended the winter, brought back summer, and Arendelle became happy again with the castle gates open.

summaries.summary: At Apple Tree Farm, Mrs. Boot lives with Poppy and Sam, and Rusty the dog. Ted works on the farm and looks after the tractor and farm machines. One very windy, cold day, Poppy and Sam play in the barn while Ted drives the tractor to check the sheep. He stops by the gate and goes into the sheep field to make the sheep shed safe. Then Poppy and Sam hear a loud crash. A tree has blown down and fallen on Ted’s tractor. Ted is upset because the tree has scratched his new tractor and he cannot get into the cab. Poppy and Sam run to get farmer Dray. Farmer Dray comes with Dolly, his big cart horse. He cuts the tree with his chainsaw, and Dolly pulls the branches away with ropes. Ted thanks them, climbs into the cab, and all go back to the farmyard. Ted then paints over the scratches and says it will soon be as good as new.

summaries.summary: In a small village in Ireland, there lived Old Pat, a kind harpist, and young Tom, who had learned to play from him. Tom bragged that he was better than Pat and charged people a lot of silver. Pat played for free when people had little money. One day, the king объявed a harp contest at the royal palace. Pat and Tom traveled there together. On the way, Tom broke one of Pat’s harp strings and would not lend him his own spare string. That night, they heard a cry for help. Tom stayed back, but Pat went to see. He found a leprechaun trapped by a rabbit. Pat helped him by barking like a fox, and the rabbit let go. The leprechaun later gave Pat a golden harp. At the contest, Tom’s harp strings broke, but Pat played the golden harp. His music made everyone dance and laugh. The king gave Pat the prize and named him Royal Harpist of Ireland.

The next morning, Pat found a golden harp in his bag. At the palace, Tom’s harp broke apart when he played, but Pat’s golden harp made joyful music. The king chose Pat as the best harpist.

Then he tried to tell a story, but the babies were noisy, hungry, climbing, arguing, getting stuck, and asking for help. Just then, his mom arrived, picked him up, calmed the babies, and made everything all right. Jim said being a mom can be fun, but it is not easy, and he hugged his mom.

video_title: Invisible Things Read Aloud

summaries.summary: The book invites readers to put on their invisible thing-spotting glasses and begin looking for things that cannot be seen. It explains that books may show bears, mice, fish, trees, and pizza, but there are also invisible things in the world. The story first uses the senses: hearing, smell, taste, touch, and sight. It gives examples of invisible sounds like a dog bark, a song, a whisper, and an echo. It says echoes repeat what people say and can be found in places like bridges, caves, tunnels, and gymnasiums. Then it shows invisible smells, tastes, and feelings. A lollipop tastes sweet, broccoli tastes bad, and hugs or petting a pet can help people feel better. The story asks readers to close their eyes, breathe, and notice invisible things around and inside them.

The story explains that some invisible things are feelings. These feelings can come one at a time or all mixed together. It names happy feelings like joy, love, hope, and gratitude. It also talks about moods, which are called vibes, and gives examples like woodsy vibes, beachy vibes, sleepy vibes, creepy vibes, and big city vibes. The book says some strange feelings can happen too, like nostalgia, deja vu, dreams, chaos, or weirdness. It describes the heebie jeebies as tiny spooky feelings that move around in dark places. If readers feel scared, the book says that is okay. It then introduces fear, which can help people be careful. But when fear stops people from doing useful things, they need guts, boldness, backbone, grit, and courage.

The book also talks about sadness. It says that when people feel sad, they may have the blues, and although they cannot be seen, they can be felt. Sometimes people can shake the blues off, and other times they need to sit with them. The story says a sad song can sometimes make people feel happy, and that is called music. It also says a rainy day can be nice and lying around can feel good. When someone is sick of feeling down, the book suggests a trick: fake laughs. These fake laughs may turn into real giggles. The book warns that giggles can multiply very fast, and soon there are many giggles. After all this, the story says it is okay to have many different feelings.

Near the end, the book explains that feelings help people understand themselves and others. It says noticing and sharing feelings can help people feel a little better. The reader is asked to pause, close their eyes, take a deep breath, and ask, “What am I feeling today?” The story reminds readers that it may take time to notice invisible things inside them. It then shows a feelings chart with many examples, including joy, the blues, hope, gratitude, anger, love, fear, the giggles, guts, worries, empathy, and the blahs. The book says noticing invisible things can keep people grounded, while also helping them think about big ideas like gravity, the sky, and infinity. It says it would be too much to see all invisible things at once, but people can focus on one or several.

At the start, the book asks readers to imagine invisible thing-spotting glasses and says that invisible things are real even though they cannot be seen. It begins with the senses and shows how people can notice invisible things by hearing sounds, smelling smells, tasting flavors, and feeling touch. It gives examples like an echo, a smell, a lollipop, broccoli, coziness, and a chill. Then it moves to invisible feelings inside people, such as joy, fear, sadness, and giggles, and also to the mood of a place, called a vibe. The story says fear can be helpful, sadness can be felt in different ways, and giggles can spread quickly. In the end, it tells readers to pay attention, because invisible things are always there if they remember to look with more than their eyes.

The bus came, and Mr. Dennis pulled a coin from behind CJ’s ear. On the bus, CJ saw many people, including a man with a guitar, an old woman with butterflies in a jar, a blind man with a spotted dog, and two older boys. video_title: The Creepy Crayon

summaries.summary: Jasper Rabbit was having trouble at school. He failed math and spelling, and only art went well. Then he found a purple crayon that was pointy, perfect, and seemed happy to see him. One night he was too tired to study because Tails from the Carrot Patch was on, so he did poorly on his spelling test. Then he took the crayon, and he spelled the words correctly. He got an A+ and a sticker. Later, the crayon helped him with math, and the answers seemed easy. Jasper saw strange purple words appear, like “Jasper and crayon forever” and “Who needs math when you have Bunny Ball Three?” He tried to hide the crayon, but his poster became a purple masterpiece. Jasper felt scared, so he put the crayon in a box, broke it, melted it, and threw it away. But it kept coming back, helping him with quizzes and even showing him a mural of his future. Finally, Jasper threw it in the toilet. After that, he studied on his own, got a C+, and felt free. The crayon floated away, and then Elliot Pelican found it.

summaries.summary: Splat looked in the bathroom mirror on Valentine’s Day and tried to make himself look just right. He had made cards for everyone in his class, and he made a special card for kitten, the cat he liked best. Kitten had snowy white paws and pea green eyes, but every time she saw Splat, she pulled his ears, poked his belly, tied his tail, called him smelly, and ran away. Splat felt sad and kept asking, “Why does she do that?” At school, the class traded Valentine’s cards. Splat carried his little red envelope for kitten, but he was nervous. On the way, he bumped into kitten, and she acted the same way again. Later, Spike saw Splat’s card and showed off his own. Splat threw his card away. But kitten found it in the trash and read, “I like you!” She smiled, sat beside Splat, and gave him a pink envelope with a card that said, “I like you!”

At school, the class exchanged Valentines, and Splat waited with his card. During recess, Spike scared him, picked up the envelope, and bragged about liking kitten too. Splat became upset and threw his card in the trash. Later, kitten found the card, read Splat’s message, and smiled. She gave Splat her own pink envelope. Inside, her card said, “I like you!”

video_title: Kids Book Read Aloud | I Love My Curly Hair

summaries.summary: The girl looks at the other girls at school and sees their long, smooth, straight hair. Her own hair is different. It bounces, twists, and curls. She learns that she got her curly hair from her mom and dad. Sometimes her mom helps her use a comb pick and asks if she wants her hair big or slick. The girl can wear it in many ways, like braided, in a ponytail, or down and bushy. Sometimes she wishes her hair were straight like the other girls, and sometimes other children make fun of her or touch her hair without asking. Then she remembers that her hair makes her unique. She starts to like her curly hair. She wears it for ballet, lets it flow when she rides her bike, and uses gel or cream to smooth frizz. She plays outside, washes her hair with shampoo, bubbles, and water, and feels proud and confident.

video_title: Who Stole MINNIE's Brownies?! | Disney Bedtime Story Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Minnie Mouse baked a whole batch of butterscotch brownies for Daisy Duck’s party. She put them in tinfoil and carried them in a pink shopping bag to Daisy’s house. At the party, Minnie danced with Mickey Mouse and forgot about the bag. When she remembered, the bag was empty. The brownies were gone, and only crumbs and foil were left. Minnie asked Daisy, Donald Duck, Mickey, and Goofy if they had taken them, but each said no. Goofy had bandages on both thumbs, so he could not have opened the package. Donald said he had smelled the brownies and peeked at them, but he said he did not eat them. Minnie and her friends searched the kitchen and found footprints. The trail led upstairs to Daisy’s bedroom and stopped under Daisy’s bed. Mickey looked under the bed and found Pluto with crumbs on his mouth. Minnie saw that Pluto was the butterscotch brownie thief and said he already had a tummy ache.

summaries.summary: Dory is with her mom and dad in Morrow Bay on their last day there. Jenny says she hopes their new home will have purple shells, and the family talks about moving. Dory wants to show her parents the reef and coral cave, and then she goes to find Nemo because he gives great hugs. In the kelp, Nemo is playing hide and seek with two new friends, a parrot fish and an angelfish. Dory joins the game, but she gets distracted by shells and then by a baby otter in the kelp. Nemo and his friends think Dory forgot them, so they come looking for her. They all try to find the otter, but he is gone. Dory, Nemo, Destiny, Bailey, and Hank work together to search for him. Bailey uses echolocation to find the otter in the kelp forest, and Hank helps too. They take the sleeping otter back home, where he wakes up and finds his parents. The otters have a big family hug, and then everyone hugs Dory, too.

summaries.summary: One morning, Andy left for school, and the toys had the room to themselves. Woody said the coast was clear and asked about a game called sardines. He explained that one toy hides, and the others look for that toy. When they find the hider, they hide there too, until the last toy is still looking in the next game. The toys understood and began to play. They guessed a number, and Ham was chosen to be it. Woody told everyone to close their eyes and count to 25 while Ham hid. Ham looked in Andy’s toy chest and under the bed, but those places seemed too easy or too scary. At the last moment, he climbed into an old lunch box and shut the lid. Woody found him first and climbed in. Jesse found them next and squeezed in too. Then more and more toys came, and the lunch box got fuller and fuller until every toy was packed inside. Rex could not fit, so Woody ended the game and sent everyone out. After that, the toys played sardines with small hiding places.

summaries.summary: One autumn morning, Sandy Squirrel and Roland Rabbit walked to school. After heavy rain, the stream was too high, and they could not cross it. This made them upset because it had happened before. They decided to build a bridge for everyone. They found fallen trees and tried to move a log, but it slipped into the water, and they fell in too. Two weasels laughed at them and walked away. A kind beaver saw what happened and offered to help. He cut wood and, with another beaver’s help, built a splendid bridge. Sandy and Roland thanked the beavers and kept their help secret. Later, the weasels came back and saw the bridge. Mr. Badger was amazed too. At school, the teacher said many children had not arrived because of the stream, and Sandy and Roland received a diploma for their efforts.

Wild mountain monsters grab frozen pants and run away in the night. Sea monsters wear pants with jewels from treasure chests on a pirate ship at the bottom of the ocean. Spiky space monsters wave and roar when bright bloomers float out from deep space. One monster has pants that are too small and wishes they were scratchy. On Saturday night, the monsters meet in a secret cave for a disco rave and dance the monster bop. When someone shouts, “Stop!”, they hurry home before daylight so no one will see them. The story ends by warning that a monster might be under your bed trying on snazzy pants.

video_title: MOANA The Ocean Chooses a 3-Year Old | Bedtime Story for Kids

summaries.summary: Grandma Tala tells the children about Maui, the Heart of te fiti, and the danger beyond the reef. Tui, Moana’s father and the village chief, comes in and says no one should go outside the reef. The children get scared when monster pictures fall down, but Moana watches the ocean with wonder. She slips away to the beach and sees a baby sea turtle blocked by birds. Moana uses a palm frond to help the turtle reach the water. Then the ocean opens a path for her and gives her shells to follow. Deep in the water, she finds a glowing green spiral stone. Tui sees Moana near the water and carries her back to the shore. He tells her the sea is dangerous and says she is the next great chief. Later, Grandma Tala quietly picks up the stone and keeps it safe for Moana.

Moana walks with her father Tui and her mother Sina through the village. Tui says the village people stay safe on their island and do not go beyond the reef. Sina hugs Moana and dances with her, and Tui shows her the village dance steps and says the song comes from their ancestors. He tells her that everyone shares food so no one goes hungry. Moana gives part of her banana to Heihei the rooster when she sees him looking for food. She watches women weave baskets and fishermen return from the sea. When she starts to walk toward the beach again, Tui picks her up and carries her on his shoulders. He and Sina show her the village, the trees, the fale, and the grand hut. Sina lets Moana try on a headdress, but it is too big. Tui says Moana will one day wear the headdress of her ancestors. Moana listens while the sound of the ocean reaches her from the shore.

He tells her not to go into the sea and says she will be chief one day. Grandma Tala later finds the stone and keeps it.

summaries.summary: In a village lived three siblings: Taotai, Lalalagi, and Masina. Taotai had their father’s fishing boat and went out on the lagoons to fish. Lalalagi and Masina kept the house neat and helped him, but Taotai became resentful. He decided not to share his fish. He caught only a few fish for himself, slept in the boat, and brought little home. Lalalagi and Masina were left hungry. After many days, Lalalagi asked to go with him and learn to fish, but Taotai refused and said the boat was his. The villagers saw how he treated his siblings. An elder told him to share, but he laughed. Then the villagers shared food with Lalalagi and Masina. The two siblings worked with an elderly neighbor in his taro fields and learned to plant taro. They also made a net and caught birds for food. Later, storms kept Taotai from fishing. Lalalagi and Masina shared their food with him, and Taotai promised to teach them to fish when the storms ended. After that, they shared food and lived happily.

summaries.summary: At dawn, Tui wakes Moana and tells her the Village Council will happen today. Then he says she will lead it. Moana feels happy because she wants to show she can be a good chief. The drums beat, and the people gather on their mats. Tui gives Moana the battle ax, and she begins to speak. A villager asks about Hey Hey the rooster, and Moana answers. Then a farmer shows rotted taro roots, and Moana says they should separate the bad crops and find a new field. Next, a fisherman says there are fewer fish in the lagoon. Moana looks at the map and says they should fish beyond the reef. Tui says no one goes beyond the reef, and he gets angry. Moana is upset and leaves the council house.

summaries.summary: One day, the kakamura appeared on the horizon in strange canoes covered with mist. At first, voyagers only saw their boats in the distance. When people got closer, they saw the tiny kakamura jumping around on decks made from many found objects. The creatures wore coconut shells on their bodies and painted faces on the shells. They often argued, stole shells, and played tricks on one another, so the men liked watching them. Then the kakamura attacked. They hid their canoe in thick fog and came close without being noticed. Their boat split into many boats and surrounded the voyagers. Spears fell on the men’s canoe, drums sounded loudly, and kakamura warriors jumped aboard with sharp claws and scary faces. They took the treasures and left the boat broken. The voyagers went home shaken and warned others, but later travelers were also attacked.

The kakamura were tiny creatures who traveled in unusual canoes through the mist. Their boats were made from different things they had found, and some even had coconut trees growing on them. People thought the kakamura were funny at first, and they enjoyed seeing them. But one day, a kakamura canoe came close in thick fog. The men did not see the danger until it was too late. The canoe split into many boats and surrounded them. Spears hit the voyagers’ canoe, drums beat loudly, and small warriors climbed aboard. The kakamura took all the valuable things and left. The men’s boat was damaged, and they returned home badly shaken. After that, more boats were attacked by the kakamura in the same way.

Mommy Pig hugged her babies, and the piggies gave Dora and Boots apples to say thank you.

summaries.summary: Peter Clinton came to the Brown Detective Agency and asked Encyclopedia to help him. Peter had a chance to trade his bicycle for a Civil War sword, but he wanted to know if the sword was real and if it really belonged to Stonewall Jackson. Encyclopedia agreed to take the case and went with Peter to the Tigers Clubhouse behind Mr. Sweeney’s auto body shop. There, Bugs Meanie showed the sword and said it had belonged to General Jackson. Encyclopedia read the words on the blade and learned that the sword was presented to Thomas J. Jackson by his men after the First Battle of Bull Run in 1861. Bugs tried to make the trade sound important, but Encyclopedia said the sword did not belong to General Stonewall Jackson. Peter then knew he should not trade his bicycle for it.

It said the sword was given to Thomas J. Jackson after the First Battle of Bull Run in 1861. Encyclopedia also noticed that the sword was very old and not worth much by itself. In the end, he said the sword never belonged to General Stonewall Jackson, so Peter should not make the trade.

summaries.summary: One bright day, Jim pansy woke up and thought everything was wrong. The sun was too bright, the sky was too blue, and the bananas were too sweet. Norman, who lived next door, told Jim he might be grumpy. Jim said he was not grumpy. On his walk, Jim met a Marabou and then a Lemma, and both said he looked grumpy because of how he stood and how his eyebrows looked. Jim loosened up and raised his brow. Then he tripped over a snake and made a frown. Norman said that was the last thing Jim needed. Jim put on a smile, but he still did not feel happy inside. Many animals asked Jim to sing, swing, roll, stroll, lie in the grass, stomp, bathe, hug, laugh, nap, eat, jump, sit in the sun, and dance. Jim did not want to do any of it. He shouted that it was a wonderful day and stormed off. Later, Jim felt sorry and said, “I guess I am grumpy.” Then he met Norman again. Norman had danced with the porcupine and was slumped and frowning. Jim asked if Norman was okay. Norman said he would feel better soon. Jim said he was still grumpy too. Norman said it was a wonderful day to be grumpy, and Jim felt a little better.

summaries.summary: Penelope Rex was a little T-Rex who felt nervous about starting school. Her mom bought her a backpack with ponies on it, and her dad packed 300 tuna sandwiches and apple juice in a pony lunchbox. On the first day, Penelope saw that all her classmates were children, and she ate them because she thought children were delicious. Mrs. Noodleman told her, “We don’t eat our classmates,” and made the children come back. Penelope tried to be friendly, but the other children stayed away from her because they were scared. At home, her dad asked if she had eaten her classmates. Penelope said she had, and her dad told her that children are the same on the inside and that friends should not be eaten. The next day, Penelope ate more classmates until everyone ran away. Then she met Walter the goldfish. After Walter tried to bite her finger, Penelope learned what it felt like to be a snack. She stopped eating children, and after that she played, ate lunch, and made friends.

The girls have made Easter pictures, and they each have an egg pouch at the end of their bed. Bingo sees glitter spilled on the rug, and Bluey wakes up. In the morning, the pouches are empty, but Bluey and Bingo find a box and a letter. They think the clues will show where the chocolate eggs are hidden. The clues lead them to the letter box, the kitchen, the fridge, the playroom, the backyard, the sand pit, the upstairs bathroom, and then their room again. Bluey and Bingo keep searching and help each other when they feel sad. Then Bluey sees Easter Bunny footprints. The girls follow them to Dad’s study and find that the Easter Bunny did remember them after all. They are happy and say, “Happy Easter!”

summaries.summary: One morning Bella woke up to Bob crawling in her room and licking her jewelry, so she shouted, “Get out of my room!” That began her “no no no” day. Bella did not want her egg, did not like her shoes, and would not stay still in the shopping trolley. She was loud in the supermarket, and Mommy said she was making Bob and everyone else unhappy. Later, Bella got upset when her cookie broke, would not let Sasha and Bob play princesses, and was grumpy at ballet class, where Mrs Clark and Miss Louisa could not practice. On the way home, Bella lay on the sidewalk and shouted. At supper, bath time, and tea time, she did not like the peas, the cold bath, or the toothpaste, and she kept throwing things. At bedtime she rolled around and said, “No bed!” But after a story with Mommy, Bella grew tired, said sorry, and went to sleep.

Bella had a very grumpy day. In the morning, Bob was in her room, so Bella shouted at him. Then she saw her boiled egg and cried that she could not eat it. She took off her shoes and said, “No shoes!” At the shop, she wriggled in the trolley and made a lot of noise. Mommy told her to stop because she was giving Bob an earache and Mommy a headache. When Sasha came to play, Bella’s cookie broke and she knocked things over. She would not play nicely and told Sasha and Bob they could not be princesses, so Sasha and her mommy went home. At ballet, Bella said the uniform was too itchy, and the teachers had to stop. A next-door lady said Bob was the sweetest thing, but Bella shouted about her hurting leg and lay on the sidewalk. Later, Bella threw hot peas, did not like her cold bath, and threw toothpaste. At last she heard a story, felt sleepy, and the next day she was cheerful and played nicely with Bob.

summaries.summary: In soggy Hollow, springtime brings animals outside to play. Hao the rabbit is happy, but Bruce the bear says, "Spring stinks." Hao wants Bruce to enjoy the smells of spring, so she shares many things with him. She puts green grass in Bruce’s basket, and grass falls on his fur. Then she gives him sweet daisies and a daisy chain. Bruce grumbles, but he keeps the flowers because they are from his friend. Hao also brings a twig from the trees and pokes Bruce’s nose by accident. Bruce still stays calm and helps carry the basket. Then a very wet moose sits in the basket and squishes it. After that, Hao puts honey on Bruce, and bees chase him and sting his bottom. Bruce falls down a hill, and his basket tumbles after him. Bruce says spring stinks because of all these bad things. At the end, Hao shows Bruce her new friend, a skunk, and Bruce says the skunk stinks too.

PJ was upset and kept trying other things, like going down a hill on a trailer, cooking mud soup, driving a little car on the road, and riding a roller coaster, but each time someone said it was not safe. The next day PJ went to Pots Pig’s house, where Pots’s mom let them eat ice cream, play outside, and go to the cinema with Polly. They ate too much, saw the scary movie in 3D, got frightened, and ran home. PJ later had a bad dream about Scary Larry, told his parents, and felt better when they hugged him. In the end, he said it was better being a bunny.

She also would not let him see Scary Larry, a scary movie about a bear. The next day PJ visited Pots Pig’s house, and everything was different there. Pots’s mom let them eat chocolate ice cream for lunch, as long as they did not eat too much. She let them hang upside down from a tree carefully, and she let them go to the cinema with Polly. PJ and Pots bought lots of snacks and watched Scary Larry in 3D, but the movie was so scary that they screamed and ran home. PJ later had a bad dream about Scary Larry, and his mom and dad comforted him. He fell asleep again and dreamed about reading stories with his brothers and sisters.

video_title: The Little Princess Treasury | I want my Mum | Mother's Day #readaloud #bedtimestories #storytime

summaries.summary: On a rainy day, the little princess paints a picture of her family. She paints her dad the king, her mom in a purple dress, and herself in the middle holding their hands. She has a crown too. While she paints, she uses a glass of water for cleaning her brushes, but she knocks it over by mistake. Blue paint spills everywhere, and the picture becomes a messy blur of colors. The maid cleans up the mess and says everything is okay. The princess wants her mom, but it is the maid beside her. Then her mom looks at the wet picture and says it is wonderful because it looks like a rainy day. She hangs it up. Later, when the rain stops, the princess goes outside to play on the seesaw. She hurts her knee and her teddy bear flies away. She goes to the doctor, who puts smelly medicine on her knee and bandages it. The princess cries for her mom while she waits to get better.

The painting looks ruined, and the colors run together. A maid comes and mops up the mess. The princess calls for her mom, but the woman next to her is the maid. Soon, her mom sees the soggy picture and says it is lovely because it looks like a rainy day. After the rain stops, the princess goes outside and plays on the seesaw. She bangs her knee, and her teddy bear flies away. She visits the doctor, who puts smelly medicine on the hurt knee and wraps it with bandages. The princess wants her mom while she rests.
