video_title: We don't eat our classmates  #backtoschool #getreadyforschool #bedtimestories #firstdayofschool

summaries.summary: Penelope Rex is a little T-Rex who feels nervous about starting school. She asks what her classmates will be like and worries about leaving home and her mommy. Her mom gives her a backpack with ponies on it, and her dad packs 300 tuna sandwiches and apple juice in a pony lunchbox. On the first day, Penelope is surprised to see that her classmates are children. She eats them because she thinks children are delicious. Mrs. Noodleman tells her, “We don’t eat our classmates!” and makes Penelope spit them out. Penelope feels sad because her classmates are dirty, scared, and do not want to play with her. At home, her dad asks if she ate her classmates and tells her that children are the same on the inside, but they should not be eaten. The next day Penelope tries again, but she keeps eating classmates until they run away from her. Then she meets Walter the goldfish and asks him to be her friend. After she learns what it feels like to be someone’s snack, she stops eating children. Penelope and the other children play together, have lunch together, and become friends.

Penelope Rex is worried about her first day of school. She practices teaching her dinosaur toys, and her mom watches happily from behind the door. Penelope gets a new backpack with ponies and a lunchbox full of sandwiches and juice. When school begins, she sees that her classmates are children, and she eats them because she thinks they look tasty. Mrs. Noodleman tells her not to eat classmates and makes the children come back out. Penelope tries to be friendly after that. She saves Griffin Emory a seat at lunch and tries to play at recess, but the children stay away from her because they are scared. At circle time, everyone sits far from Penelope, and she feels lonely. At home, her dad asks about school, and Penelope cries because she did not make any friends. He tells her that children are tasty, but friends should not be eaten. The next day Penelope eats more classmates, and they run away. Walter the goldfish does not run. Penelope talks to him, and when she feels what it is like to be a snack, she stops eating children. After that, she plays games with the class and makes friends.

video_title: My Teacher Is a Monster Read Aloud | Funny Kids' Story Time | Preschool kindergarten by Peter Brown

summaries.summary: Bobby had a big problem at school. His teacher, Miss Kirby, seemed like a monster to him. Bobby threw a paper airplane in class, and the other children saw him. Miss Kirby stomped, roared, and called him Robert, which was Bobby’s long name. Bobby spent his free time in the park, trying to forget school. One Saturday, he found Miss Kirby in the park wearing a hat. He wanted to hide, but he said hello. A wind blew her hat away, and Bobby jumped and caught it before it fell in the water. Then they sat by the ducks and quacked with them. Miss Kirby changed more and more as they spent time together. Bobby took her to his favorite spot on the rocks, and she gave him paper to make a paper airplane. Bobby flew it outside, and it soared high. By lunchtime, Miss Kirby looked normal again. Bobby was not scared anymore, and they said goodbye until Monday.

At school, Bobby called Miss Kirby a monster because she was loud and angry when he threw a paper airplane in class. She stomped and roared, and Bobby thought she had green skin, claws, and sharp teeth. Bobby went to the park on Saturday and found Miss Kirby there, reading a book and wearing a hat. He said hello to her, and when the wind blew her hat away, Bobby ran and caught it for her. Miss Kirby thanked him. Then they watched the ducks and quacked with them. Bobby showed Miss Kirby his favorite place in the park on the rocks. There, she gave him a sheet of paper, and he made a paper airplane. He threw it into the sky, and it flew very far. As Bobby and Miss Kirby spent time together, she looked less like a monster and more like a normal teacher. They said goodbye, and Bobby was no longer afraid of her at school.

Bobby thought his teacher, Miss Kirby, was a monster because she shouted when he was naughty in class. He had thrown a paper airplane, and Miss Kirby used his full name, Robert, to tell him to settle down. Bobby later went to the park, where he hoped to forget his teacher troubles. On a Saturday morning, he saw Miss Kirby there. He did not run away. He said hello, and she said hello back. Then a gust of wind blew away her favorite hat, which her granny had given her. Bobby jumped up and caught the hat before it reached the water. After that, Bobby and Miss Kirby listened to the ducks and quacked with them. Bobby then took her to his favorite spot on the rocks. Miss Kirby gave him paper, and he folded it into a paper airplane. Bobby threw it, and it flew far away. By the end of the day, Miss Kirby looked much less like a monster, and Bobby was happy to see her again.

summaries.summary: A boy finds dragons in his room and counts many of them. The dragons are on the dresser, the bookcase, the bed, the floor, the lamp, and in the sky. The boy and the dragons talk about why dragons love tacos. They look at taco ingredients like peppers, tomatoes, onions, cheese, beef, beans, tortillas, lettuce, and salsa. The dragons say they like tacos, but they hate spicy salsa. The boy reads a book about keeping salsa mild. The dragons also dress up for parties, go to pool parties, and dance with accordion music. The boy makes many tacos so there will be enough for a big taco party. Dragons come to Robbie’s house for the party and eat the tacos. Then they find spicy jalapeno salsa, and the dragons breathe fire. The fire burns the house. After that, the dragons help Robbie rebuild the house, and they celebrate with more non-spicy tacos.

video_title: OFFICER BUCKLE AND GLORIA - Caldecott Medal Book by Peggy Rathmann | Read-Aloud

summaries.summary: Officer Buckle knew many safety tips in Naville. He wrote them on his bulletin board and shared them at Naville School, but the children did not listen. Sometimes they even snored. Then the police department got a dog named Gloria. Gloria went with Officer Buckle to school, and he showed that she obeyed his commands. When he gave safety tips, the children began to watch Gloria and listen to him. They laughed, clapped, and cheered. Officer Buckle was surprised, and after that speech there were no accidents. The next day the students sent him a big envelope full of thank-you letters with drawings of Gloria. One letter from Claire said that he and Gloria made a good team. Soon many schools called and asked Officer Buckle to come with Gloria. He gave speeches at 313 schools, and children listened each time.

Officer Buckle gave safety speeches to many schools, and Gloria the police dog went with him. At first, the children at Naville School did not listen to him, but when Gloria sat and obeyed his commands, they paid attention. Officer Buckle gave safety tips like keeping shoelaces tied, wiping up spills, and never leaving a thumbtack where someone might sit on it. The children laughed and cheered, and Officer Buckle kept talking with more expression. After the speech, no accidents happened. The students sent letters with drawings of Gloria, and Claire wrote that Officer Buckle and Gloria made a good team. Soon schools all over called for the safety speech, and Officer Buckle and Gloria visited 313 schools. Later, a TV news team filmed him at State College, and the students applauded when he finished safety tip number 99. Officer Buckle watched himself on the news that night.

The next day, Mrs. Topple called Officer Buckle for another safety speech at Naville School. Officer Buckle was upset because he thought nobody looked at him, so he said he was not giving any more speeches. Mrs. Topple asked if Gloria could come instead. Gloria was brought to the school, and she sat on stage looking lonely. Then she fell asleep, and the audience fell asleep too. After Gloria left, Naville School had its biggest accident ever. A puddle of banana pudding caused everyone to slip and slide into Mrs. Topple, and she dropped her hammer. The next morning, the police station got many letters with drawings of the accident. At the bottom was a star-shaped note from Claire. She said Gloria missed Officer Buckle yesterday and reminded him that she always wore a helmet.

Officer Buckle read Claire’s note and smiled. Gloria gave him a big kiss on the nose, and he patted her back. Then he thought of a new safety tip: always stick with your buddy. This was his best safety tip yet. Officer Buckle had learned that Gloria helped people pay attention to his safety speeches. When Gloria was with him, children listened, no accidents happened, and many schools asked for his talks. When Gloria was not there, the children at Naville School became sleepy, and a big banana pudding accident happened. The letters from the students showed drawings of Gloria and told Officer Buckle that he and Gloria made a good team. After all of that, Officer Buckle stayed with Gloria and kept sharing safety tips.

summaries.summary: Mr. Willowby got a big, green Christmas tree by special delivery. He wanted it in the parlor corner, but it was so tall that it bent into the ceiling. Baxter the butler cut off the top. Mr. Willowby was happy and began trimming the tree. Baxter gave the top to Miss Adelaide, who liked it but cut off the top again. The little treetop was left outside, and Timm the gardener took it home. His wife thought their house was too small, so she cut off the top too. Barnaby Bear found it next and brought it home for Mama Bear. Little Bear said it would not hold a star, so Mama Bear cut off the top again. Later, Frisky Fox found the tree top, took it home, and then Benjamin Rabbit found it outside the fox den. Benjamin and his family celebrated around it, but Mrs. Rabbit saw it was too tall and cut off the top. At last, Mistletoe Mouse found the smallest piece and took it home. Mrs. Mouse put a cheese star on top, and it was just right.

summaries.summary: A child sets out on an epic quest to learn the truth about dragons. The child puts on a favorite cloak and sturdy boots and goes into a deep forest on a crisp day. The child follows a brook past gnarled groves, crunchy oak leaves, and tall trees. The child must be careful of hob goblins under mossy bridges and glowing Willow the Wisps that try to lead travelers away. The child finds a yellow cottage in a swamp and meets a wise woman. She serves a warm drink and says dragons are fearsome, fire breathing, and live deep underground with treasure. Then the child travels to another forest with green bamboo and misty mountains. The child follows nine-tailed fox footprints and, if lost, can ask the white rabbit on the moon for help. The child reaches an airy palace and another wise woman says dragons are majestic, live in the sky and rivers, and can bring rain and floods. In the end, the child learns both truths about dragons and that both journeys can be taken.

summaries.summary: Every spring, Rebecca Estelle planted carrots, beans, tomatoes, peas, corn, and rudabagas, but never pumpkins. When she was a girl, her family had been very poor, and she had eaten pumpkins for a whole month. After that, she never wanted to see a pumpkin again. One autumn day, a pumpkin fell from a truck and smashed in her yard. Rebecca Estelle covered it with dirt and tried to forget it. But in spring, pumpkin vines grew at the edge of her yard. She ignored them, cut them down, and shut her curtains, but the vines kept growing back. She stopped using the front door and did not look at the vines all spring and summer. Then, one autumn day, she saw that pumpkins had covered her whole yard. Rebecca Estelle decided to give them away. She made pumpkin pies and many pumpkin treats, carved jack-o-lanterns, and called the town to come. Everyone came, ate pumpkin food, and left with pumpkin gifts. Rebecca Estelle kept only a few seeds for next spring.

Years later, a pumpkin fell off a truck into her yard. She was angry and buried the pieces with dirt. In spring, she found pumpkin vines growing where the pumpkin had smashed. She would not water them, and she tried cutting them down. But the vines came back again and again. So Rebecca Estelle ignored the front yard all spring and summer and used the back door instead. In autumn, she finally saw that the vines had filled the yard with pumpkins. She thought about her old hard times and decided to give the pumpkins away. She made pies, tarts, muffins, cakes, bread, pudding, and cookies. Then she carved jack-o-lanterns, lit candles, and waited. The town came to see the pumpkins, and everyone shared the pumpkin treats before going home with gifts.

summaries.summary: Deep in the woods, an old white cabin held three friends: a cat, a squirrel, and a duck. The cat sliced the pumpkin, the squirrel stirred the water, and the duck added the salt to make pumpkin soup. They ate the soup, played music, and slept in a quilt made by all three. One morning, the duck woke early and wanted to be the head cook. He took the squirrel’s spoon and said he should stir the soup. The squirrel and cat said no, and they all had a big fight. The duck packed a wheelbarrow and left. The cat and squirrel looked for him in the pumpkin patch and in the dark woods, but they could not find him. Their soup became too salty, and they cried. At last they found the duck back at the cabin. They cooked together again, and the duck stirred while the others let him help. The soup was good, and peace returned to the cabin.

In an old white cabin in the woods, a cat, a squirrel, and a duck made pumpkin soup. Each one had a job. The cat cut the pumpkin, the squirrel stirred, and the duck put in the salt. They liked their work and lived peacefully. Then one morning the duck wanted to stir the soup. He climbed on a stool, took the squirrel’s spoon, and said it was his turn. The squirrel and cat argued with him, and the duck said he was leaving because no one let him help. He went away in a wheelbarrow. The cat and squirrel searched for him all day and through the dark woods, but they did not find him. Their soup was too salty, and they felt sad. Later they saw light in the cabin and rushed back inside. The duck was there, and they all made soup again. This time the duck stirred, and the squirrel showed him how to add the salt. The soup was the best ever, and the cabin was peaceful again.

summaries.summary: Wesley was unhappy because he did not fit in with the other people in his town. He did not like pizza, soda, or football, and he refused to shave half his head like the other boys. He had no friends and was often chased by tormentors. One week at school, he learned that wind can carry seeds far and that each civilization has a staple food crop. After school ended, he decided to use that knowledge for a summer project. He planted a patch of ground in his yard and waited. The wind helped plant the seeds, and soon seedlings grew. The plants grew very tall and made fruit, juice, roots, and leaves that Wesley used for food and drink. He also made a hat, robe, oil, games, and a new way of counting. He named his land Weslandia. By the end of summer, Wesley had created his own civilization, and when he returned to school in September, he had many friends.

Wesley lived in a town where he felt different from everyone else. His parents and neighbors noticed that he did not like the same things the other boys liked, and he had no friends. At school, he learned that wind carries seeds and that civilizations have staple food crops. Wesley thought he could use this knowledge for a summer project. He turned over a piece of ground in his yard, and the wind planted the seeds for him. Soon a strange plant began to grow. Wesley’s neighbors expected weeds, but Wesley said it was his crop. The plant made yellow fruit, purple centers, tubers, leaves, bark, and fibers. Wesley used these parts for food, drinks, a hat, a robe, oil, and new games. He also made his own counting system and told time with a sundial. He called his new land Weslandia. Later, he made a language, wrote the history of its founding, and went back to school in September with friends.

summaries.summary: When the sun slips down, bats wake up and fly out of their barn, cave, and rafter. They call to each other and say the moon is perfect for bats at the beach. Soon they pack buckets, towels, blankets, books, and other things, then fly over the dark trees to the ocean. They land on warm sand and set up their blankets. The bats play games, bury friends in sand, make sand caves, and race on the waves. At lunchtime, they eat beetles, ants, milkweed bugs, crickets, moths, and other bug treats. Later, their stomachs hurt, so they go to the snack bar for dessert. The old bats sing bat songs while the little bats rest. Then the sky turns purple and the sun begins to come up. The bats say goodbye, pack their things, and fly home before day. They curl up in their home and dream about the moon weather.

First they spread out their blankets and get ready for fun. The bats play in the sand, bury one another, build sand caves, and sail in wingboat races. They also surf on the summer tide. When it is time for lunch, they eat baskets full of bugs and other treats. Later, their stomachs hurt, so they visit the snack bar for dessert. The old bats sing songs, and the little bats climb into their laps. When morning comes, they pack up, say farewell to their new friends, and hurry home before day. Back in their crack and crevice, they snuggle close and go to sleep.

summaries.summary: Max wore his wolf suit and made mischief. His mother called him a wild thing, and Max said, "I'll eat you up." So she sent him to bed without supper. In his room, a forest grew. The walls turned into the world, and an ocean came by with a private boat. Max sailed far away to where the wild things are. The wild things roared, gnashed their teeth, rolled their eyes, and showed their claws. Max said, "Be still," and looked into their yellow eyes without blinking. The wild things became afraid and made Max king. Max said, "Let the wild rumpus start!" Then he sent the wild things to bed without supper, and he felt lonely. He smelled good things to eat far away, so he gave up being king. The wild things asked him to stay, but Max said no. He sailed home through the night and found his supper waiting, still hot.

summaries.summary: Deep in the Australian bush, two possums lived together. Their names were Hush and Grandma Poss. Grandma Poss could do bush magic. She made wombats blue, cucuras pink, dingo smile, and emus shrink. Her best magic made Hush invisible so snakes could not see her. But one day Hush said she wanted to know what she looked like, so she asked Grandma Poss to make her visible again. Grandma Poss looked in all her magic books, but she could not find that spell. The next day, she remembered that the magic had something to do with food, so they left the bush and traveled across Australia. They ate many foods, but Hush stayed invisible. In Darwin they ate a Vegemite sandwich and Hush got a tail. In Perth, pavlova made her legs and body appear. In Tasmania, a lamington made her visible from head to tail. After that, Hush stayed visible, and once a year she ate those foods again to keep it that way.

video_title: HELLO LIGHTHOUSE - Caldecott Medal Book by Sophie Blackall | Read-Aloud

summaries.summary: On a tiny island at the edge of the world, a lighthouse stands on a high rock and sends its light to the sea. A new keeper arrives to take the place of the old one. He polishes the lens, fills the oil, trims the wick, winds the clockwork, paints the rooms, writes in the log book, and listens to the wind. He drinks tea, fishes for cod, and writes letters to his wife. Soon the tender brings supplies and his wife comes too. He shows her the round rooms, and they set the table for two. Then thick fog comes, and a bell rings to warn ships. One dark night, a boat crashes on the rocks, and the keeper pulls three sailors from the water and wraps them in blankets.

The keeper becomes very sick after sneezing one dawn. By dusk, he is terribly ill. His wife runs up and down the spiral stairs, tends the light, gives him broth and chips, and writes in the log book while he rests. When his fever breaks, the icebergs pass by on their journey south, and the whales pass by on their journey north. Later, the woman walks around and around inside the lighthouse. Her husband boils water and helps her breathe in and out. He keeps tending the light and writes in the log book when their child is born. Then the sky swirls with green light.

After the child is born, the tender comes again with oil, flour, pork and beans, mail, fresh books, and news from the land. Inside one letter is a message with the Coast Guard seal. The keeper winds the clockwork and polishes the lens one more time. He tends the light and writes in the log book, but he knows his work will not last much longer. Together, he and his wife watch the horizon. Then the Coast Guard arrives with a brand new light and installs a machine to run it. There is no lamp to fill and no wick to trim. The keeper’s work is finished, and he climbs the spiral stairs and closes the log book for good.

The keeper and his wife pack their things into a boat. They wave goodbye to the gulls and leave the lighthouse behind. Beyond the breakers, they look up at the old tower one last time and say goodbye to the lighthouse. The story begins again with the lighthouse still standing on the high rock. Fog rolls in and out, waves rise and crash, and the wind blows and blows. Across the water, another light on the land shines back. The lighthouse still beams its light over the sea and calls out, 'hello hello hello hello Lighthouse.'

The lighthouse stands on a tiny island at the edge of the world and sends its light out to sea from dusk to dawn. A new keeper comes to care for it. He cleans the lens, fills the oil, trims the wick, winds the clockwork, paints the rooms, writes in the log book, and listens to the wind. He waits for his wife and writes letters to her. When she arrives on the tender, he shows her the lighthouse home. Later, fog covers the sea, a bell rings, and a boat is wrecked on the rocks. The keeper saves three sailors from the black water and wraps them in blankets. After that, he gets sick, and his wife cares for him. Their child is born, and the Coast Guard later brings a new light, so the keeper’s job ends. He and his wife leave by boat, and the lighthouse remains shining.

Every morning, children climbed in with pitter patter, giggle giggle, and patter sounds, and the bus felt happy. Then a new driver came and took the bus on unfamiliar roads. The children still climbed in with shuffle, clunk, and creak sounds, and the bus still carried them and felt joy. After a long time, another new person drove the yellow bus into the city, parked her in a quiet spot, and walked away. No one came for a while, and the bus stayed empty and still. One cold night, people climbed in and huddled together, making rustle and bump sounds. Later, the bus was taken by a truck across a bridge, through the country, and to a farm in a valley. There, more animals came in with clip clop and maaah sounds. Then the farmer gathered them and took them away. The farm became quiet. Soon the river rose, and then swimmers came in with swish and swoosh sounds, and they filled the yellow bus with joy.

After some time, another driver brought the bus into the city, parked her in a quiet place, and left. The bus had no riders and no sounds. Then, on a cold night, people came and climbed in. They made rustle, bump, and brr sounds and sat close together. They did not ride anywhere, but they filled the bus with joy. One morning, a truck moved the bus to a farm by a river in a valley. The bus heard loud noises like city machines. Then the farmer gathered the animals and took them away. The farm became quiet. After that, the river rose and rose. At last, swimmers came in, swishing and swooshing around the yellow bus, and she was happy again.

On the next days, Ronald made fun of her teeth, her voice, and her snowflake, but Molly Lou Melon smiled, sang, and showed her beautiful snowflake. The other children were happy to see what she could do. On the fifth day, Ronald was nice to her, and Molly Lou Melon wrote her grandma a letter to say her advice was right.

After counting to ten and opening eyes, the magic begins again with green leaves.

One day they decided to make a monster monster with tape, tacks, glue, gunk, gauze, bolts, wire, and a smelly old shoe. They lifted it into the stormy sky, and a lightning bolt hit it. The creature came alive. He roared, then said, “Thank you!” and hugged them. He opened a window, saw the morning light, and smiled. Grouch and the others wanted him to be scary, but he was kind. He went to the village bakery, said “Thank you” again, and took a white paper bag. Then he walked to the beach and gave each of them a warm powdered jelly donut. They sat on the shore, watched the sunrise, and giggled together.

Grouch Grump and Little Gloom and Doom thought they were monsters. They lived in a monster castle high on a mountain above a village. Every day they shouted, argued, and fought about who was the biggest and baddest. To end the fight, they made a new monster from tape, tacks, glue, goo, wire, and an old shoe. A lightning bolt made the monster wake up. He stood up, tore off the bandages, and said, “Thank you!” He hugged the little monsters and looked out into the bright morning. The others wanted him to smash the village, but he did not. He walked to the bakery, where the shop was just opening, and came out with a white paper bag. Then he went to the beach. There he gently gave Grouch Grump and Little Gloom and Doom a warm powdered jelly donut each. They all smiled, giggled, and watched the sunrise together.

In a dark castle on a dark mountain, Grouch Grump and Little Gloom and Doom argued every day about who was the most terrible monster. They tried to settle it by building a bigger monster with tape, tacks, glue, gunk, gauze, bolts, wire, and a smelly old shoe. They took their creation into the storm, and lightning made it alive. The monster twitched, roared, and then said, “Thank you!” He squeezed them in a hug and opened the window to the warm morning air. He greeted the bats, rats, spiders, and snakes, which made the others shout that he should be a monster. Instead, the monster smelled the sweet air, roared, and smashed through the dungeon wall. The little monsters thought he was going to make trouble in the village, but he went to the bakery, said “Thank you,” and carried away a white paper bag. At the beach, he gave them each a powdered jelly donut, and they sat together watching the sunrise.

Grouch Grump and Little Gloom and Doom were loud, grumpy little monsters who lived in a monster castle. They kept arguing and fighting about who could complain the most. One day they made a monster monster out of many things, and lightning brought it to life. The monster first roared, then said, “Thank you!” and hugged them. He looked out at the dawn, smiled, and said hello to the bats, rats, spiders, and snakes. The little monsters did not like this, because they wanted him to be mean. The monster then smashed through the dungeon wall and ran down the mountain. The three little monsters followed him to the village bakery and waited outside. They heard him say, “Thank you,” and saw him leave with a paper bag. At the beach, he gave them warm powdered jelly donuts. They all became quiet, smiled, and watched the sunrise and the ocean.

video_title: All Ages Storytime: Maybe Something Beautiful

summaries.summary: Mira lived in a gray city and loved to doodle, draw, color, and paint. When she saw blank paper, she thought, “Hmm… maybe.” She gave little gifts to people on her way to school, like an apple for Mr. Henry, a flower for Ms. Lopez, a songbird for Mr. Sax, and a red heart for the policemen. On the way home, she taped a glowing sun on a wall, and the city became a little less gray. The next day, Mira met a muralist with paintbrushes. He asked what she saw, and he said, “Maybe something beautiful.” He painted the wall, and Mira joined in with bright colors. Soon Mr. Sax and many others came to paint, dance, and make music. Even the policeman asked to paint too. They colored walls, benches, utility boxes, and sidewalks. At the end, everyone rested, and the artist said they were all artists and the world was their canvas.

One day she gave a round apple to Mr. Henry, a flower to Ms. Lopez, a songbird to Mr. Sax, and a red heart to the policemen. Later she taped a glowing sun on a wall, which made the city a little brighter. The next day, Mira saw a man with paintbrushes looking at the wall. He said he saw “maybe something beautiful,” then painted the wall sky blue. Mira learned he was a muralist, and he gave her a brush. Mira painted too, and the wall became full of color. Soon Mr. Sax and other neighbors joined in. Music, dancing, and painting spread through the streets until a policeman stopped and asked to paint with them. Everyone shared brushes and covered walls, benches, boxes, and sidewalks with art. In the end, the artist said they were all artists and the world was their canvas.

summaries.summary: Maisie wants to play outside, eat a cookie, and stay up late, but Dad keeps saying no because it is getting dark and bedtime is near. Maisie feels grumpy and tells Dad she cannot go where she wants, have what she wants, or do what she wants. Dad tells her that tomorrow they will have a celebration. He says they will celebrate her great great great grandpa Mose and Juneteenth. Dad explains that Grandpa Mose worked in the fields until sunset and had to keep going because the masters would not let the slaves quit. The slaves thought about freedom, prayed for it, and made plans for a better future. Later, a brave president’s proclamation was read in Galveston, Texas, and Grandpa Mose heard cheers, saw happiness, and felt pride. The people danced and celebrated into the night because they had found freedom.

Maisie wants to go outside, have a cookie, and stay awake, but it is too late and she must stay inside and go to bed. She feels upset and tells her dad that she cannot do what she wants. Dad says that tomorrow they will celebrate Juneteenth. He tells Maisie about her great great great grandpa Mose, who worked in the fields until sunset with other slaves. They were very tired, but they still dreamed about freedom, prayed at night, and hoped for change. Some slaves ran north to freedom, and later a brave president’s proclamation brought freedom to many more people. In Galveston, Texas, Grandpa Mose heard the proclamation, and people cheered, danced, and celebrated all night. After that, he and the others kept working, but now they were paid. Even though Black people still were not treated as equals, they kept going. Every year on Juneteenth, they remembered, marched, lobbied, learned, and celebrated.

The slaves were tired, but they thought about freedom, prayed before sleep, and hoped for a better future. Some ran north following a bright star. Later, a proclamation from a brave president was read in Galveston, Texas, and Grandpa Mose heard cheers and felt pride. The people danced and celebrated into the night. After freedom, they kept working for pay and saved their money. Black people still faced unfair treatment, but they did not give up. Every year on Juneteenth, they remembered, marched, and celebrated.

Black people still faced unfair treatment, but every year on Juneteenth they remembered, marched, lobbied for schools and voting rights, and celebrated.

summaries.summary: Three bears lived in a house in the woods. Papa Bear was big, Mama Bear was middle-sized, and Baby Bear was wee little. One morning, Mama Bear made porridge and put it in three bowls. The porridge was too hot, so the bears went for a walk. While they were away, Goldilocks came to the house. She tasted each bowl. Papa Bear’s porridge was too hot, Mama Bear’s was too cold, and Baby Bear’s was just right, so she ate it all. Then she sat in three chairs. Papa Bear’s chair was too hard, Mama Bear’s was too soft, and Baby Bear’s chair was just right, but it broke. Goldilocks went upstairs and tried three beds. Baby Bear’s bed was just right, so she fell asleep. When the bears came home, they saw the porridge was eaten, the chair was broken, and Goldilocks was in Baby Bear’s bed. Goldilocks woke up, saw the bears, and ran away.

summaries.summary: Little Nick was very happy when summer vacation began. He went to his grandparents’ farm and hugged Grandma and Grandpa. After breakfast, Nick asked to go outside to play. Soon he saw Duck, Sheep, Cow, and Pig having a loud argument. They were upset because they would not share toys, a ball, or mud, and they were saying unkind things to each other. Nick asked them to stop and said it was rude. He told them that kindness means doing nice things, helping others, respecting older and younger people, waiting your turn, and not mocking others. He gave examples from his own life, like helping his sister, giving up a seat, and helping a boy get his ball. The animals listened, apologized, and promised to be kind and polite. They said hello, smiled, and said sorry when needed. By the end of the day, everyone was happier, and Duck thanked Nick for being a good friend.

summaries.summary: Many years ago, an emperor loved fine clothes more than anything else. He did not care about hunting, plays, food, or wine. One day, two swindlers came to town and said they were master weavers. They told the emperor they could make a magical cloth that only intelligent people could see. The emperor gave them gold and sent his prime minister to check on their work. The prime minister saw nothing, but he lied and said the cloth was beautiful. He even gave the swindlers more money. Then the emperor visited the room himself and also saw nothing. Afraid of seeming stupid, he praised the cloth and ordered a suit. Soon the swindlers pretended to dress him, and he marched through town while everyone pretended to admire his clothes. At last, a child shouted that the emperor had nothing on. The crowd agreed, and the emperor knew he had been tricked.

He also paid the swindlers more money. Later the emperor went himself and saw nothing either. He still said the cloth was magnificent and ordered a suit. The swindlers kept pretending to make invisible clothes, and other noblemen also said they could see them. On the day of the parade, the emperor wore nothing, but everyone acted as if he was dressed well. The people in the street praised the clothes until a young child shouted that the emperor had nothing on. Then the crowd laughed, and the emperor understood that he had been fooled.

The inchworm measured the flamingo’s neck, the toucan’s beak, the heron’s legs, the pheasant’s tail, and the whole hummingbird. The inchworm tried, and while the nightingale sang, he measured and measured until he inched away out of sight.

summaries.summary: Summer brings many things. It brings the sun, the heat, and cold things to eat. The children ride way out of town, up hills and down, and then they stop to eat. They like fireworks at night with red, yellow, blue, and white lights. On hot days they ride in a car and feel too warm, so cold water cools them off. Summer also brings swings, hay, and things with wings that they catch with a net. They say hello to the fish, go to a summer fair, and water the garden so it can grow. Most monsters prefer brownies, and they eat them in many ways, such as with gooey centers, crispy sides, peanut fudge, and walnuts. Monsters with two heads like double chocolate chip brownies, and monsters with big claws use sticky syrup so they can grip their treats. Even more than brownies, monsters love playing hide and seek. They hide under beds and in wardrobes at night so they can scare children by surprise. The story explains that dark brownies help them stay hidden. Then a child bakes huge brownies for the monsters and brings milk too. The milk scares the monsters, so they hide it at first. But one monster gets covered in milk and learns that milk tastes good with brownies. In the end, the monsters stop fearing milk, move their games to the barns, and no longer hide in children’s rooms.

video_title: SPOOKLEY THE SQUARE PUMPKIN 🎃 A Halloween Story About Courage & Kindness Kid's Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: In a pumpkin patch, a little pumpkin named Spooky was born. He was not round like the other pumpkins. He was square, and the other pumpkins teased him because he could not roll. Spooky wished he could be like them. Then Halloween was almost here, and a big storm came. The wind tossed the round pumpkins around and broke their vines. Spooky stayed safe because he was square. When the fence broke, three pumpkins rolled into the bay. Spooky tipped and flipped until he fit in the gap and stopped the pumpkins from going farther. The pumpkins shouted hooray. After the storm, the farmer saw Spooky holding the broken fence. He knew Spooky had saved the day. The next year, the farmer planted Spookley’s seeds, and many pumpkins grew in many shapes and colors. Every Halloween, people come to see the special pumpkins and remember not to judge by how something looks.

The other pumpkins cheered because he saved them. More pumpkins bumped into him, and the pile grew big. When morning came, the farmer found Spooky wedged in the broken fence. He saw that Spooky had protected the patch. After that, he planted Spookley’s seeds everywhere, and the patch grew pumpkins in many shapes, sizes, and colors.

summaries.summary: On Saturday, Fergus and his baby brother Dink looked for treasures at the beach. The waves brought things to shore, and they collected seaweed, a pebble that looked like an eyeball, and a shell that might have been a shark’s tooth. Then a surfboard washed up. They waited for 15 minutes, but no one came for it, so they made it part of their treasure pile and named it Dave. Fergus did not want to go into the water because he thought there was murky ickiness there. Later, Fergus went to get ice cream. While he was away, Dink looked at Dave and tried to drag him into the water. Fergus saw this and ran into the water to save Dave. A wave picked them up and carried Fergus and Dave back to shore. After that, Fergus and Dink kept looking for more treasures and found another one.

summaries.summary: One happy gray stone lived in a pile with many other stones. He waited while the other stones were picked for different jobs, and he hoped he would have a purpose too. At last, he was chosen and placed on a desk beside a big cup. He thought he might help, but he was only a paperweight. Then bright scribbles came by and made art on the paper. The paper stack got taller and taller, and the scribbles cried because they had used all the paper. Stone did not want them to be sad, so he rolled down and asked if they could use red, yellow, and blue. The scribbles liked his idea and painted on him. More stones came, and soon Stone was picked again. He became a small gift that could brighten someone’s day. After that, scribble stones traveled everywhere and helped many people feel happy.

summaries.summary: Peral P. Pumpkin was very excited for October 24th, the big day for the Pick a Pumpkin for Your Porch event. He cleaned himself until he was bright orange and made his stem straight. He chose his special smile and went to sleep early. When he woke up, his smile was gone. Peral tried to get it back, but it did not return, so he had to go with a frown. At the event, the patch was full of pumpkins. Other pumpkins and people called him a grumpy pumpkin, and no one picked him. Peral became angry and shouted that he was happy and had only lost his smile. Then a little girl named Panie sat next to him. She said she had a crooked smile too and understood him. Panie showed Peral how to breathe, count backwards, and talk to a friend. With practice, Peral learned to show his feelings without yelling. Panie and Peral liked each other and liked themselves just as they were.

video_title: ⛄ SNOWMEN AT NIGHT What Do Snowmen Do When No One is Watching? Funny Kids Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: One wintry day, a child made a snowman that was very round and tall. The next day, the snowman looked different. His hat had slipped, and his arms drooped down. This made the child wonder what snowmen do at night. The child thought snowmen might slide off the lawn, down the street, and into the park when it gets dark. In the park, snowmen gather in a circle and wait for the others. They drink ice-cold cocoa made by snowman mothers. Then the snowman games begin. They race, skate on the pond, and do tricks on the ice. Sometimes they giggle, act like clowns, and bump into each other until they all fall down. They gather snowballs and play baseball under the moonlit sky. Then they have a big snowball fight. After that, they go sledding down the hill. At the end, they are tired and sleepy, so they gather their things and go home.

video_title: My First Chinese New Year. By:  Karen Katz. Read Aloud kids book.

summaries.summary: The family gets ready for Chinese New Year. They decorate the walls with red paper cutouts and say red brings good luck and happiness in China. The sister and child push away the bad luck from last year so good luck can come in. Dad and the child buy plum and Christmas pumps, and the candy bars remind them that new things have grown. Grandpa and the child make headholsters to honor their ancestors. They add boats filled with tangerines and oranges, which stand for money and good luck. Mom buys brand new clothes, and the child adds a little dress to the bucket. Then everyone gets a haircut so they can start the year fresh and green. After that, the family begins cooking for the big feast. Grandma and the child make a special soup for good health, and later the child will put out the dumplings on New Year’s Eve. Girlfriends, cousins, uncles, and everyone else come to the big round table. They eat soup, chicken, whole fish, parmesan, and sweet rice pudding. On New Year’s day, the family shares more good luck. Then they go to the Chinese New Year parade in Chinatown. They watch the lion dancers, drummers, symbol clashes, clothes, paper launchers, and finally the dragon, which is a sign of good luck. At the start of spring, they hug and wish each other happy new year.

The people watch and like what he does. At the end, they say he should not be in the zoo. They tell him the circus is the right place for him, and he is happy to go there.

The bird gave him a name tag and taught him letters, sounds, and words. Each day he learned more, and each afternoon she read stories. When the weather turned cold, she flew away and told him not to forget that words are built one letter at a time. Rocket practiced all winter. When spring returned, the bird came back. Rocket learned more words, read more stories, and heard the story of Buster finding his bone.

She read about Buster, an unlucky dog who lost his favorite bone. Rocket listened, then waited for the end of the story. The next morning he came back early to hear more. summaries.summary: In the Jingle Jangle Jungle, on a cold and rainy day, Moose, Lion, Zebra, and Sheep looked for a warm place to play. The bear woke up, stomped his feet, gnashed his teeth, and chased them out. The animals wanted to help him feel better so they could go back inside. Zebra thought stripes would help, Moose wanted antlers, and Lion wanted a golden mane. But the bear stayed cranky. Then Sheep saw that the bear only wanted a quiet place to sleep. Sheep used clippers to cut off some wool, put it in a bag, and made a soft pillow. She gave the pillow to the bear in the cave. The bear said thank you and soon fell asleep.

After that, the witch and her friends made a new broom with seats and a nest, and they all flew away together.

A dog found the hat and politely returned it, then asked, “Is there Room on the Broom for a dog like me?” The witch said yes, and he joined them. Soon the wind blew off the witch’s bow, and a green bird found it and asked to come too. The witch agreed. Then the witch dropped her wand, and a frog brought it back and asked for a place on the broom. The witch said yes again. After that, the broom snapped in two, and the cat, dog, and frog fell into a bog. A dragon came and tried to eat the witch, but a strange beast with four heads scared him away. The witch thanked her helpers and made a new, bigger broom for all of them.

The story begins with a witch and her cat riding a broomstick through strong wind. The wind blows away the witch’s hat, so they land and look for it, but they cannot find it. A dog appears with the hat, gives it back, and asks, “Is there Room on the Broom for a dog like me?” The witch says yes, and the dog climbs on. Then the wind blows away the bow from the witch’s braid, and a green bird brings it back and joins them too. Next, the witch loses her wand, and a frog returns it and asks to come along. The witch agrees again. After that, the broom breaks in two, and everyone falls into a bog. A dragon comes, but before he can eat the witch, a huge beast with four heads tells him to go away. The dragon leaves, and the witch makes a new broom with seats and places for all her friends.

video_title: Fly Guy vs. The Flyswatter! By Tedd Arnold. Book#10: Fly Guy. Kids Book Read Aloud.

summaries.summary: Buzz had a pet fly named Fly Guy, and Fly Guy could say Buzz’s name. One day, Fly Guy ate breakfast in Buzz’s backpack. Buzz took his backpack to school, and Fly Guy flew out in class. Then the teacher said the class would go on a field trip to tour a factory. Buzz told Fly Guy to stay in his pocket, and the children rode the bus to the factory. Inside, the tour guide showed them a fly swatter museum and the place where fly swatters were made. She said each child could have one, and then Fred the fly came out to talk. Fred said flies play in slime, eat garbage, and are nasty. Fly Guy got mad. Fred then showed the super swatter 6000 and said it was the fly swatter of the future. When a tiny fly was brought out, the machine started swatting. Fly Guy rescued the little fly by flying it to an open window. Fred shouted for everyone to stop and end the tour. Later, back at school, the class made an art project and said it was the best field trip ever.

The narrator tastes Eugene’s Bib and Bop, Farah’s tajin with chicken and apricots, Dakota’s red beans and rice, and Ronnie and Donnie’s dumplings. Each food tastes good, and the narrator keeps asking if it is better than pizza. After more tasting, the narrator asks Mr. Gonzalez, who says pizza is the best. At the end, the narrator plans another experiment and asks for green puzle soup for dinner tomorrow.

summaries.summary: Nick was happy when summer vacation began, and he went to visit his grandparents at the farm. He hugged Grandma and Grandpa, ate breakfast, and then asked to go outside to play. Outside, he found Duck, Sheep, Pig, and Cow having a loud fight. Duck said Cow would not share toys. Sheep said Pig took her ball. Cow and Duck teased each other, and everyone shouted. Nick asked them to stop and told them to show kindness. He explained that kindness means doing nice things, helping others, sharing, waiting your turn, and being grateful. The animals listened and began to talk about kind things they had done, like helping family, teachers, neighbors, and older people. They apologized for being rude and mean. By the end of the day, the animals were polite and kind, and Nick was glad he had helped his friends.

People work for money and choose their own jobs, and together they help make the pizza.

After lunch, some classmates talked about a video game, but Zayn did not know how to join in. He talked about the game, but the others did not hear him, and they left for science class. In science, the teacher gave each student a planet to draw, but Zayn made his own. Later, he looked for a boat in the classroom after the teacher said, “Whatever floats your boat.” Zayn cried and asked why people only saw his autism stripe. Mama showed him many other stripes he had, like pilot, caring, honest, and curious. Zayn felt better and loved himself again.

summaries.summary: At school, Blue is writing a story when Chloe says it is time for a story with Calypso. Everyone sits up straight and listens. Calypso tells a story about an old dog who sits on a chest by the road and begs for treats. A gnome asks him to open the chest, and the old dog says it is empty. But when he opens it, the chest is full of treats. Blue does not think the story makes sense, so she wants to write a new one with a better ending. Then she sees that the real typewriter is gone. Blue goes to find Calypso because she needs the typewriter to write. On the way, Blue meets Snickers, who is sad because he cannot sit like everyone else, and Winton, who is sad because people run away from him. Blue asks them to come with her to see Calypso.

Blue, Snickers, and Winton walk together to find Calypso. They meet the Terriers, who are playing a game and pretend to shoot bows and arrows at them. The three friends do not fall over, so they keep going. Snickers hides in skinny trees and sneaks around the Terriers. Winton asks a Terrier a question, and the Terrier runs away. The last Terrier traps them, but Winton gives Blue a pretend real shield. Blue uses the shield, and they escape when it makes a loud ping. Snickers then says he is a sausage roll, and Blue and Winton laugh. Blue notices that Winton is standing close, so he is not being a space invader anymore. The friends keep going to Calypso.

Blue asks Calypso where the real typewriter has gone. Calypso says it is around there somewhere. Blue tells Calypso how she got past the Terriers by using a shield. Calypso then asks Blue to show her a typewriter. Blue shows Calypso a pretend real typewriter, just like she used a pretend real shield. Calypso smiles and says it is a lovely typewriter. Blue thanks Calypso and runs off to write her story. The story ends with the lovely typewriter, and Blue keeps it with her.

summaries.summary: Franklin could do many things by himself, but he was not allowed to go into the woods alone. One day he went to play at Bear’s house. His mother said he must be home for dinner by 6:00 and warned him not to go into the woods alone. Franklin played hide and seek with Bear, Fox, Goose, and Otter. He found Bear, Goose, and Otter, but he could not find Fox. While searching, Franklin walked into the woods without thinking. Fox was not there. Fox was hiding inside Bear’s house. The others waited, then went home when it was almost 6:00. Franklin’s parents looked for him too. It got dark, and Franklin could not find the path. He was lost and scared. Then he heard his parents calling. They found him, hugged him, and took him home. Franklin said he was sorry and promised never to go into the woods alone again.

In the next spring, everyone in the neighborhood planted Chinese vegetables, and the whole street smelled like soup.

summaries.summary: A boy had a pet fly named Fly Guy. Fly Guy could say the boy’s name: “Buzz.” One day, Buzz was at school, and Mom and Dad were at work, so Fly Guy went out by himself. He looked for breakfast and ate a little, then more, but he was still hungry. He followed a smell and found a strange garbage can. He tasted the garbage and felt sick. Fly Guy flew home and fell asleep on Buzz’s bed. Later, Buzz came home from school and found that his bed was between two trees, because Fly Guy had grown so big that Buzz’s house was on his head. Buzz told Fly Guy to put the house down and give him a ride. Buzz then asked what Fly Guy had done that day. Fly Guy had eaten at different places, and Buzz followed him. They went to the garbage can, where a scientist was taking out trash. The scientist helped, and then the army arrived looking for a 50-foot monster. Buzz said there was only his pet fly. Everyone went home, and Buzz asked Fly Guy what he wanted to do next. Fly Guy said, “Eat.”

summaries.summary: Joy says she is in charge of being joyful. She likes dinosaurs, cupcakes with sprinkles, monkeys, bouncy balls, goofy faces, twirling, sunshine, rain, shiny red bicycles, and new adventures. She says the best thing of all is being with friends and family. Then Joy steps on Sadness’s foot. Sadness says she feels blue and does not always understand the world. She likes rain, but many things bother her, like broken ice cream cones, broken pencils, and losing things. She says crying helps her slow down and feel better for a little while. After that, Anger speaks. He does not like strange sayings, traffic jams, timeout, or vegetables in the wrong place, like broccoli on pizza. Then Disgust talks about gross things like feet, crabs, cows, road trips, dirty ground, sweating, no water, and camping. Last, Fear says he tries to keep everyone safe from scary things like basement stairs, vacuum cleaners, clowns, and sliding on banisters. He likes soft things, tea, and peaceful nature shows.

She learned to talk, share, help, and play with others. In the end, she woke up, went to the park, and made many friends.

summaries.summary: The child has a tiny temper that follows everywhere and grows when parents say no. In the morning, the parents say there is no breakfast until teeth are brushed, and the child says okay. Then Dad says no playing until homework is done, so the child puts the game away. Later, before dinner, the child sneaks for a sugary snack, but Mom catches the child and asks for the popsicle to be put back. By dinner, the temper is very big, red hot, and angry. It does not want broccoli or greens and shouts about not liking being told what to do. Then the child takes a deep breath and counts to ten. As the counting goes on, the temper gets smaller. The child brushes teeth, does the work, and tries the broccoli. At the end, the child eats all the greens, and the temper goes to sleep.

summaries.summary:
Stacy loved words. She liked reading, writing, spelling, and learning unusual words from the dictionary. She kept a special notebook for extraordinary words and practiced them carefully. Words made her feel understood, especially when she felt quiet, clumsy, grumpy, or anxious. One day her teacher, Mrs. Blakesly, asked her to stay after class and gave her a spelling test with a big red 100. Then Mrs. Blakesly told Stacy that she would be in the spelling bee with Jake. Stacy knew Jake was a bully who used words to hurt other students, and she hoped she could be braver at the contest.

Stacy studied all week. At the county library, she took her place onstage and spelled word after word correctly. Soon only Stacy, Jake, and one other girl were left. The other girl missed her word, and then Jake kept spelling correctly too. Stacy finally misspelled instantaneous and lost. Jake won first place, and Stacy got second. Jake was rude, but Stacy told him he should be courteous. Her mother reminded her, "Only fail if you stop," and Stacy remembered perseverance. She decided she would keep learning words and try again tomorrow.

It made the house rustle, scratch, flicker, and howl through the roof. When the wind stopped, the house was quiet again, but it still felt lonely. The house decided it needed people who would like a spooky house. Soon, a family came up the hill and went inside. They made themselves at home, and the house was happy to be haunted.

summaries.summary: If you give a moose a muffin, he will want jam too. Then he will eat the muffin and ask for another, and another, until they are all gone. He will ask for more muffins, so you must go to the store for muffin mix. He will go with you and feel the chilly air, so he will ask to borrow a sweater. When he puts on the sweater, he will see a loose button and ask for a needle and thread. Sewing the button will make him think of puppets, so he will ask for old socks and make sock puppets. Then he will want a puppet show and need cardboard and paints. After that, he will hide behind the couch, and his antlers will stick out, so he will ask for a sheet. The sheet will make him think of being a ghost, and he will use it to clean paint spills. He will wash the sheet, hang it outside, and see the blackberry bushes. Then he will want blackberry jam again.

summaries.summary: In Spain, there was a little bull named Ferdinand. While the other young bulls ran, jumped, and played, Ferdinand liked to sit quietly under his favorite cork tree and smell the flowers. His mother worried that he might be lonely, but Ferdinand was happy where he was, so she let him stay. As Ferdinand grew bigger and stronger, the other bulls fought each other and wanted to go to the bullfights in Madrid. Ferdinand did not want to fight. One day, five men came to choose a bull. Ferdinand sat on a bumblebee by mistake, and the bee stung him. Ferdinand jumped, snorted, and ran around, so the men thought he was fierce and took him to Madrid. At the bullring, Ferdinand saw the flowers and sat down to smell them. He would not fight, so the men had to take him home.

summaries.summary: Otis was a friendly little tractor who worked on the farm with his farmer every day. After work, he liked to play on the hills, by the mud pond, and near the haystacks. At night, he slept in his little stall in the barn. One night, the farmer brought home a baby calf. The calf cried for her mother, but Otis’s soft putt-putt sound helped her fall asleep. Soon, the calf followed Otis everywhere. They played together and sat under the apple tree. Then the farmer got a big yellow tractor and moved Otis out of his stall. The big tractor made loud noises, and the calf did not like him. Later, the calf got stuck in the mud pond. The farmhands, the big tractor, and the fire truck could not help. Then Otis came, circled the pond, and freed the calf. Everyone was happy, and Otis and the calf stayed best friends.

They played together and spent time side by side. Then the farmer got a new yellow tractor and moved Otis out of the stall. The calf did not like the loud tractor. Later, the calf wandered to mud pond and sank into the mud. The farmhands tried to pull her out, then the big tractor and the fire truck came, but nothing worked. When Otis arrived, he drove around and around the pond. The mud loosened, and the calf got out. The farm celebrated, and Otis and the calf stayed together.

summaries.summary: On a cold winter morning, Dexter ran downstairs to eat his mom’s bacon and cheese bread pudding, but his twin sister Leah got the first bite again. Later, when Mama and Papa were busy cooking for a big dinner, Dexter and Leah helped in the kitchen. Papa found out they had no eggs, so he sent the twins to Ms. Marvis’s house to get some. At Ms. Marvis’s home, Dexter noticed it felt very quiet and lonely. On the way back, he and Leah talked about how their house was always full of people, and they asked their parents to invite Ms. Marvis to dinner. That night, Ms. Marvis shared stories about living in Poland and making punchki, jelly donuts made in winter. The next day, Papa used her recipe, and the twins helped make punchki to give to Ms. Marvis. They later built a snow family in her yard, and Ms. Marvis wrote a thank-you letter saying their kindness made her feel special.

summaries.summary: A girl sees another girl being bullied. She stops and thinks about how the hurt girl might feel. Then she decides to do something kind. She can be extra friendly, include the girl in games, and not join in when others are mean. The story says that even small actions can help a lot. If the bullying is still happening, the girl can tell a trusted grown-up. The story explains that telling is not tattling. Tattling is getting someone in trouble, but telling is getting someone out of trouble. The story also says kindness can spread. When one person does a kind thing, other people may do kind things too. The girl shares her ideas with others and invites them to help.

video_title: I Spy Fly Guy! (exciting adventure with Fly Guy & his friend, Buzz) Kids Picture Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Buzz had a pet fly named Fly Guy. Fly Guy could say Buzz’s name. One day Buzz and Fly Guy went outside to play hide and seek. Fly Guy hid in the garbage can, where he liked to eat while Buzz looked for him. Then Buzz hid in the garden shed, and Fly Guy found him. After that, Fly Guy hid in the garbage can again. Just then, the garbage man came and dumped the can into the truck. The truck drove away with Fly Guy inside.

Buzz’s dad was going to work, and Buzz told him, “Follow that truck!” Buzz followed the garbage truck all the way to the town dump. He ran into the dump and called, “Fly Guy, where are you, Fly Guy?” Many flies answered him because they could all say Buzz’s name. Buzz looked and looked, but he could not find Fly Guy. He kept trying to spot him as flies flew away from him.

At the town dump, Buzz kept searching for Fly Guy. He looked at a fly hiding, a fly eating, and a fly landing on his hand. Each time Buzz asked, “Do I spy Fly Guy?” the fly flew away. One fly even bit Buzz and then flew away. Buzz still could not find his pet fly. He felt sad and wondered if Fly Guy was gone forever.

Buzz kicked a can and then kicked a jar. After that, he remembered that he and Fly Guy were still playing a game. Then he heard Fly Guy from above. Fly Guy said, “Buzz, I give up, you win!” Buzz looked up and cried, “Buzz, I spy Fly Guy!” Fly Guy answered, “Buzz, laws.” Buzz found Fly Guy, and the game ended.

summaries.summary: When the child gets home, Penny the dog jumps all over them, and they realize Penny can be used for homework about measuring. Penny is a Boston terrier, and the child compares her size with other dogs at the park. They measure noses with inches, tails with dog biscuits, ears with cotton swabs, paw prints with centimeters, and height with inches, feet, and yards. Penny is one inch long in the nose, one dog biscuit long in the tail, one swab long in the ears, three centimeters wide in the paw print, and 18 inches tall. Then the child checks how high the dogs can jump, and Penny jumps as high as the child’s waist. The child also uses a seesaw to compare weight and later weighs Penny on a scale at home. Penny weighs 16 pounds.

The child spends the day measuring Penny in many ways. At the park, they use standard units like inches and centimeters to measure Penny’s nose, paw prints, and height. They also use non-standard units like dog biscuits and cotton swabs to measure Penny’s tail and ears. Penny is smaller than some dogs and bigger than others, and her jump is measured by using the child’s body as a unit. When they cannot find a scale in the park, they use a seesaw to compare Penny’s weight with other dogs. After that, they go home, where Penny is weighed at 16 pounds. The child also learns about volume, food, water, and the cost of taking care of Penny. At the end, the child says Penny is expensive but very valuable.

The child says the Earth is big enough for all kinds of people, and that if people change the way they see, they will find Wonder in everyone.

video_title: Construction Site: Farming Strong, All Year Long (teamwork, perseverance) Kids Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: In early spring, six big trucks wake up with the sun and look down at the farm. Big tractor says hello, and pickup truck says hello too. The farm is busy, and there is work to do. Dozer fills a cracked road with dirt, and dump truck carries the broken pieces away. Big tractor pulls a chisel plow to turn the soil and pull up weeds. Then little tractor plants the crop, and corn seeds drop into the ground row by row. Little skid steers fix pens and clean floors while cows, horses, chicks, chickens, a lamb, and mother sheep stay nearby. In summer, the sun is hot, and the crops grow tall with rain and care. Later, the trucks help make a new barn by digging, moving dirt, setting posts, pouring concrete, and putting in stalls. The cows come in at night, and the barn is finished.

summaries.summary: Once there were two tall towers in New York City. Philippe was a young street performer. He rode a unicycle, juggled balls and torches, and loved to walk on a rope. When he saw the two towers, he wanted to stretch a wire between them and walk on it. He knew people would say no, so he made a secret plan. One August evening, Philippe and friends brought rope and cable into the South Tower and waited until night. At midnight, they shot a line across to the other tower and tied the strong cable between the roofs. When the sun came up, Philippe put on black clothes and took his balancing pole. He stepped onto the wire and walked high above the city. Police came and shouted, but Philippe kept walking back and forth for almost an hour. Then he returned to the roof and gave himself up. The judge later told him to perform in the park for children.

Because the towers were not finished, he and friends went in secretly one August evening. They took cable and equipment up many stairs to the roof of the South Tower. At midnight, friends on the other tower shot a line across with an arrow. The first try missed, so Philippe climbed down and fixed it. Then the stronger cable was pulled across and tied tight. The cable slipped once and almost fell, but Philippe held it in time. In the morning he put on black clothes, took his long pole, and stepped onto the wire. He walked and danced in the air while people below looked up in surprise. Police came, but he kept going for nearly an hour. Afterward he walked back and was arrested. The judge made him perform in the park for children.

In spring, apple blossoms bloom and must be pollinated before apples can grow. The apples develop through summer, ripen in fall, and are picked at harvest time. In winter, the trees become dormant until the next spring. Apples are used in many foods and drinks, come in many varieties and colors, and are stored in cool, dry places so they can last for months.

summaries.summary: A few days before Halloween, a shopkeeper put pumpkins on the shelves outside a little shop in a big city. A girl came to look at them. She picked up one pumpkin and carried it away. The other pumpkins worried about their friend, then saw him across the street, high up as a Jacko Lantern. He had triangle eyes, a nose, and a big smile. The pumpkins were happy for him and dreamed that they might become jackolanterns too. Then one pumpkin saw something sad. He had lost his stem and was now just stumpkin, a stemless pumpkin with a little stump. Still, stumpkin was a nice pumpkin, orange like a traffic cone and round like a basketball. More people came over the next days. Some pumpkins left and some stayed. Stumpkin waited for a home. A cat sat on his top, and then a baby chose him, but a bad dog ruined it. On Halloween night, the shop closed, and the shopkeeper carried stumpkin away. He did not get a window, but he did already have a home, and that made him very happy.

summaries.summary: Mac was a good apple who shared toys, helped Granny Smith after art class, and liked to dive into the watering hole. One day, rain fell while Mac was sleeping. Small creatures looked for higher ground, and a little worm came near Mac. When Mac woke up, he saw the worm and met Will. Will showed Mac how to fly a kite, play in the dirt, and make a mess. Mac took Will to the watering hole to get clean. They went to the orchard, but other apples saw Will and shouted that Mac had worms and was rotten. Mac and Will left. Will read stories to Mac, and Mac liked the adventure books. The next day, the apples teased them again, and no one would play with them. That night they sat alone, and in the morning Will was gone. Mac searched everywhere for Will. At last, Mac looked up in the sky and found him. Mac said he would rather be a bad apple with Will than a sad apple without him, and Will helped Mac turn the pages.

Mom said they were too creepy, but Jasper said he was a big rabbit now, so Mom bought one pair. That night Jasper wore them to bed. In the dark, the underwear glowed a ghoulish greenish glow, and Jasper could not sleep. He changed into plain white underwear and hid the creepy pair in the laundry hamper. The next day the creepy underwear were back on him, so he threw them in the garbage. After school, Jasper heard scratching at his dresser and found the underwear back again. He mailed them to China, but the next morning they returned with chopsticks. Jasper used his mom’s sewing scissors, then later buried the underwear deep in a hole at Creek hanger Hill. At the end, Jasper bought creepy underwear again all by himself and was not scared.

summaries.summary: Voting is a way people choose something and use their own voice. People vote for a class president, a snack, a class trip, or a class pet. They can vote with a raised hand, on paper, or with thumbs up or thumbs down. If people do not vote, they lose their say. In big elections, people choose the President and Vice President every four years. They also elect senators, Congress people, mayors, and sheriffs. The story explains that the United States is a democracy, so the people help govern the country. It also tells how voting rights changed over time. Black men could vote in 1870, women in 1920, Native Americans in 1924, and 18-year-olds in 1971. Adults 18 and older must register to vote. Political parties, like Democrats and Republicans, help choose candidates. Candidates campaign, give speeches, and try to win voters’ trust.

The story says voters should follow the news and learn what candidates believe before Election Day. Candidates try to win support with speeches, ads, town hall meetings, handshakes, rallies, phone calls, door-to-door visits, and campaign stickers. In primary elections, party members vote for the candidate they want on the ballot. Debates are shown on live TV so people can hear the candidates answer questions. Election Day comes on the Tuesday after the first Monday in November, after the harvesting season. On that day, voters go to their assigned poll, which may be a school or firehouse, or they may mail an absentee ballot if they are away. Voting is private, and a curtain or screen keeps each vote secret. People vote on machines, computers, or paper ballots. This privacy helps make sure only the voter knows the choice.

After the polls close, the votes are counted. Some results are scanned by computer, and some are counted by hand. The results are sent to the Board of Elections, which carefully checks them and declares the winner. The loser accepts defeat, and the winner announces victory. The winner also says they will serve everyone in the country, not only the people who supported them. The story explains that voting is an important responsibility because it helps choose leaders and lets people have a voice. It also reminds readers that voting rights were won through brave struggles over time. At the end, the story says it hopes readers will cast their first vote for The Cat in the Hat. The whole story shows how voting starts with learning, continues with casting a ballot, and ends with the winner being chosen.

Voting lets people make choices together. The story says people can vote for class things, like a president, a snack, a trip, or a pet. They may vote by raising a hand, marking paper, or using thumbs up or thumbs down. Voting gives people a voice, and not voting means losing that voice. In the United States, people vote for President and Vice President every four years. They also vote for senators, Congress people, mayors, and sheriffs. The story says the country is a democracy, which means the people help run it. It also tells that voting rights grew over time for Black men, women, Native Americans, and 18-year-olds. Adults who are 18 or older must register with their name, address, and birth date before they can vote. Political parties, candidates, and elections all help people make these choices.

Candidates try to win voters during the campaign. They speak at town halls, give speeches, wave at people, and visit rallies. Supporters call people and go door to door to ask them to vote for their party. They also collect money and sell stickers. Before Election Day, people watch debates on TV and listen to what the candidates say. Voters are told to read, watch, and listen carefully so they can learn what each candidate believes and plans to do. Election Day is set for the Tuesday after the first Monday in November because it comes after harvest time. People vote at polling places like schools or firehouses, and some mail in ballots if they are away. Their votes stay private behind a curtain or screen. After the polls close, the votes are counted and the Board of Elections names the winner.

summaries.summary: It snowed all night on Sodor, and in the morning everything was white. Sir Topham Hat asked Thomas to take firewood to the stations. He asked Gordon to take trucks to the docks. Sir Topham Hat told Gordon that the snow was slippery and said to take the long way around the hills. Gordon did not listen. He said he was strong and could go over any hill. Thomas was careful, but Gordon went straight on. On one hill, Gordon slid fast. Then he came to a bigger hill, and a giant snowball grew behind him. Thomas came up the hill and was pushed back by the snowball. Gordon could not stop it. Thomas was knocked off the rails. Gordon felt sorry and asked Rocky to help. Rocky lifted Thomas back on the tracks. Then Thomas and Gordon delivered the firewood to all the stations, and they went around the hills together.

He warned Gordon that snow was slippery and told him to take the long way around the hills. Gordon said he was strong and went straight ahead. He went up one hill, but on the way down he slipped and sped along. Spencer shouted for him to slow down. Gordon kept going. At the biggest hill, snow gathered on Gordon and turned into a huge snowball. Thomas came behind him and thanked him for clearing the tracks, but the snowball pushed Gordon back down the hill and hit Thomas, knocking him off the rails. Gordon could not help, so he found Rocky. Rocky lifted Thomas back onto the track. Then Gordon helped Thomas deliver the firewood to all the stations.

summaries.summary: On a sunny day, Thomas was taking freight cars on the island of Sodor. He saw an old, overgrown track and went down it. Soon he found a very old station with crumbling platforms and ivy on the building. Thomas was amazed and told everyone he had found a hidden town. The next day, Sir Topham Hat said the place was Great Waterton, a town that had once helped give water to Sodor. The springs had run dry, so people had left, and the town was thought lost. Now it was found again. Everyone worked to fix it up for Sodor Day, and Sir Topham Hat put Thomas in charge.

Thomas liked being in charge at Great Waterton. He checked the old tracks and tried to do everything himself. One day he went too fast on the old line and toppled off the track. Harvey helped lift him back, but Thomas was hurt and had to go to the works. While Thomas was away, a new engine named Stanley took charge of the work. When Thomas returned, Sir Topham Hat said Stanley would stay in charge and Thomas would help him. Thomas felt sad, but Stanley asked him to shunt freight cars. Thomas did the job well, but he still wanted to prove himself.

Thomas saw an old freight car near Morgan's mine and tried to bring it in. He bumped it too hard, and it rolled into the mine. Thomas went after it and followed it down a dark tunnel with his bright lamp. The freight car sped away, and Thomas rushed after it. He did not notice a junction ahead, and he crashed through a blocked tunnel and jumped the track. Then he was stuck deep in the mine. His fire went out, and he could not move or whistle. The next morning the engines searched everywhere for Thomas, but they could not find him.

Stanley thought Thomas might be near Great Waterton, so he went to look. He heard Thomas's whistle in Morgan's mine and found him in the dark. Thomas had almost no puff left. Stanley coupled up to Thomas and pulled hard. At last he got Thomas back onto the track, but then Stanley's boiler valve burst, and he could not move. Thomas then helped Stanley. He found an open siding, got behind him, and pushed Stanley out of the mine and back to Great Waterton Junction. The other engines were glad to see them, and Sir Topham Hat said Thomas had been found and Stanley had saved Thomas and Thomas had saved Stanley.

After that, everyone worked hard to get Great Waterton ready for Sodor Day. Thomas was happy that Stanley had come to Sodor, because Stanley was now his friend. The weather was perfect for the day. Sir Topham Hat and Lady Hat came to open the town. They stood by the red ribbon, and Lady Hat cut it with big scissors. Sir Topham Hat said it was the grandest Sodor Day ever and welcomed everyone to Great Waterton. Great Waterton was no longer lost, and the work was finished on time. Thomas was tired, but he was very proud as all the engines puffed happily.

Cranky felt better and promised to be kind. He worked carefully and said please and thank you, but later he became cranky again.

summaries.summary: One morning Sir Topham Hat spoke to James and said that if he could not behave, his red coat would be taken away and he would be painted blue. James felt cross. He was rough with the coaches and called, “Come along, come along!” The coaches grumbled and squealed. James had to fetch his own coaches, and he thought this was unfair. He bumped the coaches hard onto the train and made them groan. Then he had to take them to a different platform where people stayed far away. James felt lonely and wanted to show that he could pull the coaches well. When the guard blew his whistle, James started off with a big jerk. He went too fast, and then the train began to slow down because the brake pipe was leaking. The driver and guard found a hole. They fixed it with newspapers and a leather bootlace from Jeremiah Jobling. After that, James pulled the train safely and was careful never to bump coaches again.

Sir Topham Hat was stern with James and warned him about his bad behavior. James became cross and rude to the coaches. He shouted at them, bumped them, and pulled them to a different platform. No one came close to him there, and James felt lonely. He thought Gordon was the only engine who could pull coaches, but he wanted to prove he could do it too. When the guard blew the whistle, James rushed off with a strong jerk. The coaches swayed and cried out because they were going too fast. Soon James slowed down because the brake pipe had a leak. The driver and the guard looked along the train and found a loose joint. They asked the passengers for help and needed a leather bootlace to mend it. Jeremiah Jobling did not want to give up his bootlace at first, but he did. The driver wrapped newspapers around the hole, and James was able to go on. James learned to take care and not bump the coaches again.
