video_title: 'Velma Gratch and the Way Cool Butterfly' read by Kyra Sedgwick

summaries.summary: Velma Gratch was the youngest of three sisters, and when she started first grade, everyone remembered Frieda and Fiona but not her. Frieda was known for her singing, and Fiona for running and spelling. Velma felt left out, so she tried to get noticed by singing too loud, running too slow, and doing badly in class. Then she learned about butterflies in science and loved the word metamorphosis. Her class visited the Butterfly Conservatory, where she saw many butterflies and learned about migration. One monarch butterfly landed on Velma’s finger and would not leave. It stayed with her all day, through school and even at home. Because of this, everyone finally knew Velma well. Later, Velma took the butterfly to the park with her class and sisters. When the monarch’s friends were released, it flew away with them to Mexico. At last, everyone remembered Velma.

Velma Gratch wanted people to notice her when she began first grade, because her older sisters, Frieda and Fiona, were already famous at school. People remembered Frieda’s beautiful singing and Fiona’s fast running and good spelling, but they hardly remembered Velma at all. Velma tried to make herself stand out by acting badly in class, and she was sent to the principal’s office. Then science class became exciting when Mr. Plexipuss taught the children about butterflies and the word metamorphosis. Velma read many books about butterflies and was happy when her class went to the Butterfly Conservatory. There she learned about butterfly wings and migration. A monarch butterfly landed on her finger and stayed there for a very long time. It followed her through school, so everyone learned her name. In the end, Velma brought the butterfly to the park, where it flew away with other monarchs heading to Mexico.

Frieda had an angelic voice, Fiona ran very fast, and both were known for their school work. Velma wanted to be noticed too, so she sang too loudly, ran too slowly, and did not do her classwork well. After that, she became excited about science, especially butterflies. She learned the word metamorphosis and studied butterfly names and facts. When her class went to the Butterfly Conservatory, Velma learned about butterfly wings and migration. A monarch butterfly landed on her finger and would not leave, even after school was over. Because of this, everyone at school and at home knew about Velma. Later, the butterfly was taken to the park, where a guide released monarchs to fly to Mexico. Velma’s butterfly flew away, and everyone said it was way cool.

It stayed with her at school, at home, and in every class. Everyone learned her name because of the butterfly. video_title: 'The Sound of Silence' read by Simu Liu

summaries.summary: Little Yoshio ran out into Tokyo and listened to many sounds. He heard his boots splash in puddles, rain on his umbrella, and a koto player tuning her instrument. The koto player played beautiful music and told Yoshio that the most beautiful sound was ma, or silence. Yoshio went to school wondering where silence could be. He listened all day, but there was always noise. At recess he sat in the bamboo grove, but the wind and bamboo still made sound. On the way home he heard buses, trains, and traffic lights. At home he heard chopsticks, slurping, and bathwater dripping. That night he tried to stay awake to find silence, but he fell asleep. The next morning, he got up early and went to school before anyone else. In the empty classroom, while reading a book, he suddenly found silence. He learned that silence was there between sounds all along.

Yoshio loved listening to the sounds of Tokyo. One rainy day he heard his boots, the rain, and a koto player tuning and then playing her instrument. He told the koto player he had never heard a sound like that. She asked if he had a favorite sound and said that the most beautiful sound was ma, or silence. Yoshio spent the day searching for silence at school, in the bamboo grove, on the way home, in the dining room, and in the bath. He even tried to stay awake at night to hear it, but he fell asleep before he found it. The next morning he woke to a barking dog and went to school early. His sisters ran past him, and he opened the school gate when no one was there yet. In the quiet classroom, while reading, he heard no other sounds at all. Yoshio then understood that silence had been there between the sounds all along.

One day Yoshio stepped outside and listened to the busy city of Tokyo. He heard rain, puddles, and a koto player making strange, lovely music. When the music stopped, Yoshio asked the koto player about her favorite sound. She said the most beautiful sound was ma, or silence. Yoshio wanted to find silence, so he looked for it everywhere. At school he heard other children making noise. In the bamboo grove he heard the wind and the bamboo. On the way home he heard buses, trains, and traffic lights. At dinner he heard his family eating, and in the bath he heard dripping water. That night he tried to wait for silence, but he fell asleep. The next morning, after hearing his neighbor’s dog and his sisters, he went to school early. In an empty classroom, while reading a book, he finally found a still, quiet moment and understood that silence had always been around him.

As he read a book, the room became very still, and he heard no sounds at all for a moment. Yoshio realized that silence was not missing. It had been in the spaces between all the sounds from the very beginning.

video_title: 'My Brother Charlie' read by Holly Robinson Peete

summaries.summary: Callie and her twin brother Charlie have always been together, even in Mommy’s tummy. They share curly hair, brown eyes, hot chocolate with marshmallows, their dog Harriett, music, football, and names that start with C. Callie is two minutes younger and loves to talk and watch the sky. Charlie is skinnier, goofier, and quieter. As babies, Callie showed love by talking, snuggling, and kissing Mommy, but Charlie did not. Mommy saw that Charlie was different and later learned that he has autism. This makes it harder for him to make friends, show feelings, and stay safe. Sometimes Charlie is hard to understand and can ruin playdates, but he also shows love in his own ways. He smiles, plays hand games, helps with Harriett, and runs to comfort Callie when she gets hurt. One day, after Callie hurt her toe, Charlie said, “Don’t cry, Callie, I love you.” Callie said it back, and she knows their love is shown in many ways.

Callie tells about her twin brother, Charlie. They have the same curly hair and brown eyes, and they both love hot chocolate, Harriett the dog, music, football, and things that start with C. Callie is younger by two minutes. She likes to talk and look at the moon and the Big Dipper. Charlie is quieter, does not like math, and sees jets and helicopters in the sky. When they were little, Callie said “I love you” a lot, but Charlie did not say those words. Mommy worried and watched Charlie closely. Then she learned that Charlie has autism. Because of this, it is harder for him to make friends, say how he feels, and stay safe. Some days are hard, but Callie also sees Charlie’s good side. He knows many presidents, swims well, loves animals, and can play piano. He cares for Callie when she is hurt. At last, when Callie hurt her toe, Charlie said, “I love you,” and Callie answered, “I love you, too, Charlie.”

Charlie did not kiss Mommy or say “I love you.” Mommy knew something was different and later found out Charlie has autism. This makes it harder for him to make friends, show feelings, and stay safe. Callie says love is not only in words but also in actions. Charlie shows love by smiling, holding hands, helping Harriett, sharing his shells and sneakers, and playing piano. He also comes to help when Callie gets hurt. One day, after Callie banged her toe, Charlie comforted her and said, “Don’t cry, Callie, I love you.” Callie said it back, and she remembers that love is shown in many ways.

summaries.summary: Before Julius was born, Lilly was happy to be a big sister. She gave him things, shared secrets, and sang lullabies to him every night. After Julius was born, Lilly did not like sharing. She took her things back and said, “These are mine!” She pinched his tail and said mean things into his crib. Her parents loved Julius very much. They kissed his wet pink nose, looked at his small black eyes, and stroked his sweet white fur. Lilly thought this was disgusting. Julius stayed in her room, and Lilly had to be quiet while he slept. Her parents told Julius he was beautiful and special, and they also sang him letters and numbers. Lilly tried to scare Julius with disguises and magic, and then she pretended he was not there. Nothing changed. Lilly got upset, but her parents still loved Julius and praised him. One day, Lilly told Julius a story that called him a germ, and she was sent to the uncooperative chair. Later, at a family party, Cousin Garland said mean things about Julius. Lilly defended her brother, showed how to kiss, admire, and stroke him, and made everyone repeat that Julius was the baby of the world.

She read scary stories, slept with her door open, and brushed her teeth while hanging from a tree branch by her ears. One day, Rabbit said they were going on an adventure. Bear wanted to read about adventures instead, but Rabbit kept asking if he was scared. Bear said no and went with her. They crossed a stream, went around a dark forest by bus, rode a train and helicopter over a mountain, and came to a rope bridge. Bear finally said he was scared of the bridge and went home. Then Rabbit fell through the bridge, and Bird woke Bear. Bear rushed out, crossed the stream, forest, and mountain quickly, and saved Rabbit. After that, Bear admitted he was scared, Rabbit said she was too, and Bear learned that sometimes it is okay to be scared.

Then the conductor became very upset because wild animals were storming the stage. The lions, elephants, bears, raccoons, monkeys, bison, camel, yak, bonobo, ferret, jackal, hippo, tigers, and goats took the instruments and played them. The audience stayed calm, but the boy was frightened. After the animals finished, they bowed, left the stage, took off their fancy clothes, and went back to their cages. Then the boy’s sister told him to wake up or they would leave him behind. The story says never play music next to the zoo and do not fall asleep when an orchestra plays.

His big brother, James, plays the trumpet, and the boy and his friends pretend to be in the band. During Mardi Gras, brass bands parade past his house, and people dance in the streets. The boy loves the music and says he wants his own music to sound like gumbo, with many different sounds mixed together. He and his friends make their own instruments and play like real musicians. One day he finds a broken trombone and takes it outside when a parade passes. James sees him and calls him Trombone Shorty, and that name stays with him. He practices hard, carries his trombone everywhere, and learns songs by listening to James. Later, his mother takes him to the New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival, where he plays with Bo Diddley onstage. After that, he starts his own band, joins James’s band, and keeps playing music in New Orleans and around the world.

In Tremé, a neighborhood in New Orleans, a boy grows up hearing music all around him. His brother James plays trumpet in a band, and the boy and his friends follow along and pretend to play too. On Mardi Gras, brass bands march through the streets, and the boy loves watching the parades and the dancing people. He thinks of music like gumbo, with many different things mixed together. Before he has a real instrument, he and his friends make music with things they can find. Then he discovers a broken trombone that is still good enough to play. He goes into the street with it, and James gives him the name Trombone Shorty because the trombone is so big on him. The boy practices all the time, even falling down sometimes because the trombone is heavy. His mother later takes him to hear Bo Diddley at the New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival. Bo Diddley invites him onstage, and the boy plays with him. After that, he starts the 5 O'Clock Band and keeps growing as a musician.

summaries.summary: Mo was a zombie who loved vegetables. He grew many kinds in a hidden garden and cooked them in his secret kitchen. He liked celery, tomatoes, carrots, spinach, cucumbers, kale, peppers, onions, garlic, and cilantro. His mom and dad did not like vegetables at all. They wanted Mo to eat zombie food like brain cakes, brain stew, and brain-and-bean tortillas. Mo tried to get them to try veggies, but they would not listen. He began to wonder if he was really a zombie because he did not like zombie cuisine. Then Mo had an idea. He made a tomato-and-veggie soup that would look like zombie food. He hoped his parents would eat it and want more. At dinner, his parents tasted the soup, but they said it tasted like vegetables and did not like it. Mo felt sad, but he told them he was still Mo, still a Romero, and still a zombie who loved vegetables.

Mo Romero was a zombie with a secret. He loved vegetables more than zombie food. He grew veggies in a hidden garden and made tasty meals in his secret kitchen. His parents thought vegetables were yucky and told him zombies should eat brain cakes, brain stew, and other zombie dishes. Mo kept trying to show them he liked peas, spinach, cucumbers, and kale, but they would not change their minds. He wondered if he was not really a zombie after all. Later, Mo found a recipe for tomato-and-veggie soup. He chopped, blended, and poured until it was ready. He brought it home for dinner, and his parents served their own strange zombie foods too. When they tasted Mo’s soup, they were upset because it tasted like vegetables. Mo told them he liked vegetables and was still their son. His parents then accepted that he was different and promised to eat a little more veggies for him.

summaries.summary: Snappsy the alligator did not feel like himself. His feet felt draggy, his skin felt baggy, his tail would not swish, and his jaw would not SNAP. He went looking for food by the pond, up a hill, and through the forest. The narrator kept saying Snappsy was a big, mean alligator hunting for tiny birds and fuzzy bunnies, but Snappsy said he was just going to the grocery store to buy food. He filled his cart with pudding, peanut butter, pita bread, popcorn, and other foods. Then he carried his groceries back past the pond and hill to his crooked little house. Inside, he made a peanut butter sandwich and read a book. The narrator kept guessing what he was doing, so Snappsy said he was planning a party. He cleaned, made the house festive, and waited for friends to come. His friends arrived, danced, and had a good time. Snappsy offered pudding, and everyone did the Chicken Dance.

summaries.summary: When you build a perfect sandcastle, a dragon moves in. He sits inside the castle and keeps you company. He can help by toasting marshmallows, pulling a raft, and making a kite fly. He also keeps beach bullies away. But you must hide his smoke from the lifeguard and wipe away his dragon prints. Later, you want to tell your family. You tell your mom about the dragon, but she hears the ocean. You show your dad a feather and sharp teeth, but he thinks they are a seagull feather and broken shells. The dragon is real, though. Then he gets hungry and eats the peanut butter sandwiches. He makes the lemonade sizzle and takes brownies from the cooler. He snickers and sprays sand on your sister. Your family says they have had enough. You tell the dragon to leave until he learns manners, and you say you will never build a perfect sandcastle again, at least until tomorrow.

summaries.summary: There was once a good shoemaker who became very poor. He and his wife had only enough leather to make one last pair of shoes. The shoemaker planned to cut the leather at night and sew the shoes in the morning. But when they came to the workshop, they found two finished shoes on the table. A dandy gentleman came to the shop, tried the shoes on, and paid double. The shoemaker bought leather for more shoes. Again, each night, he cut the leather, and each morning the shoes were finished. Soon the shoes were famous, and the shoemaker and his wife were no longer poor. Near Christmas, they stayed up and watched. At midnight, two tiny elves came in and made the shoes. The next day the couple made warm clothes and shoes for the elves. That night the elves found the gifts, put them on, danced, sang, and ran away. After that, they were never seen again, and the shoemaker and his wife lived happily.

The shoes sold well, and soon the couple were no longer poor. One night before Christmas, the wife asked who was helping them, so they stayed awake to watch. At midnight, two tiny elves came through the window. They were small, barefoot, and wearing ragged sacks. The elves worked fast, stitching and hammering until all the shoes were done. The next morning, the wife made warm clothes and stockings, and the shoemaker made shoes for the elves. That night the elves found the gifts, dressed up, sang, danced, and left the shop. After that, they never came back.

summaries.summary: Clark the Shark went to Theodore Roosterfish Elementary and loved school, lunch, and recess. He was the biggest and strongest fish, but he was also too loud and too wild. He shouted, munched too much lunch, and played too rough, so the other fish stopped sitting with him, eating with him, and playing with him. Clark asked Mrs. Inkydink what was wrong. She told him he needed to stay cool and remember that there is a time and a place for everything. Clark tried, but he kept forgetting. Then he made rhymes to help himself remember. He said, “When teacher’s talking, don’t go walking,” “Only munch your own lunch,” and “Easy does it, that’s the way.” These helped him behave better. Later, a scary new kid, Sid the Squid, came to school and made a mess. Clark helped him play safely and taught him to stay cool. Everyone cheered for Clark, and he told his mother what he learned.

After three tries, Gabe stayed with Emma. Then Stella, Gabe’s little sister, arrived with a snack and hiccups. Emma was scared of Stella’s hiccups and toes, so Stella became the perfect monster for Emma. Emma stayed in bed, the child went back to his room, and Gabe returned to his own bed.

A long time ago, in a town in Calabria, there lived Strega Nona, the “Grandma Witch.” People whispered about her, but they still came to her for help. She could heal headaches, help girls find husbands, and remove warts. As she got older, she needed help in her house and garden, so she hired Big Anthony. She told him to sweep, wash dishes, weed the garden, feed and milk the goat, and fetch water. She also told him never to touch the magic pasta pot.

One day, Big Anthony saw Strega Nona make pasta by singing to the pot and blowing three kisses to stop it. Later, after she left to visit Strega Amelia, he tried the spell himself. Pasta poured out and filled the house, then the town, and people ran for plates and bowls. Big Anthony forgot the three kisses, so the pasta would not stop. At last Strega Nona returned, sang the song, blew the kisses, and stopped it. She made Big Anthony eat the pasta for his punishment.

summaries.summary: Chester Raccoon stood at the edge of the forest and cried because he did not want to go to school. He wanted to stay home with his mother, his friends, his toys, his books, and his swing. Mrs. Raccoon held his hand and told him that sometimes people must do things that feel strange and scary at first. She said Chester would like school and make new friends. She also said she knew a special secret called the Kissing Hand. She showed him by kissing the middle of his left palm. Chester felt the kiss go from his hand to his heart. Mrs. Raccoon told him to press his hand to his cheek when he felt lonely and think, “Mommy loves you.” That night, Chester went to school. Before he went in, he kissed his mother’s hand and gave her a Kissing Hand too. Then he danced away to school, and Mrs. Raccoon smiled and felt his love in her heart.

Irene was very upset, but she kept going with the empty box until she got lost in the dark snow. She fell into a hole, then found the glowing palace. The wind helped her by turning the box into a sled, and the gown was caught in a tree nearby. Irene put the dress back in the box, took it to the palace, and gave the duchess the story. The duchess welcomed her, and later Irene was taken home in a sleigh while her mother was preparing for the morning.

The boy made an enemy list and kept it in his tree house. His dad said he knew how to get rid of enemies and showed him a secret recipe called Enemy Pie. While Dad mixed ingredients, the boy imagined something awful, but the pie smelled and looked good. Dad explained that the pie only worked if the boy spent a day with his enemy and was nice to him. The boy visited Jeremy, played bikes, trampoline, water balloons, and games, and slowly found that Jeremy was not so bad. When Dad served Enemy Pie, the boy stopped Jeremy from eating it because Jeremy was his friend now. Then he tasted the pie and found it delicious. Jeremy went home after inviting him to play again the next morning.

At the start of summer, the boy had a new tree house, his sister was at camp, and he was on a strong baseball team. But the summer changed when Jeremy Ross moved in next door to Stanley. Jeremy laughed when he struck the boy out, and he invited Stanley to a party the boy was not invited to. The boy decided Jeremy was his only enemy and wrote an enemy list. His dad remembered having enemies when he was young and offered to help with a secret recipe called Enemy Pie. Dad would not explain the recipe, but he said it was the fastest way to get rid of enemies. The boy brought strange things like weeds, worms, rocks, and gum, but Dad did not use them. Instead, Dad baked a pie that smelled delicious. He told the boy the pie would only work if he spent one full day with Jeremy and was nice to him. The boy did that, and the two boys biked, played, ate lunch, and went to the tree house. By dinner, the boy realized Jeremy was becoming a friend. When Dad served the pie, the boy warned Jeremy not to eat it, then learned Dad had already eaten some. The pie was good, and Jeremy invited him over again.

summaries.summary: An egg rolled through the trees, across the meadow, and down the hill. It rolled into Mother Duck’s nest. Mother Duck did not see it because she was reading. Soon the eggs cracked. One duckling had blue spots, so Mother Duck named him Crayon. The next had brown stripes, so she named him Zebra. The third was yellow, so she named him Moonlight. The fourth duckling looked very odd and said, “Guji Guji,” so that became his name. Mother Duck taught all four ducklings to swim, dive, and waddle. Guji Guji learned fast and was bigger and stronger, but Mother Duck loved all her ducklings the same. Then three crocodiles came from the lake. They looked like Guji Guji and told him he was a crocodile too. They said to bring the ducks to the bridge. Guji Guji thought hard, made a plan, and took the ducks to the bridge the next day. The crocodiles waited below, but Guji Guji dropped rocks on them. The crocodiles ran away. Guji Guji saved the ducks, and everyone danced and celebrated.

summaries.summary: Harry was a white dog with black spots, and he liked almost everything except baths. One day, when he heard the water running in the tub, he took the scrubbing brush and buried it in the backyard. Then he ran away from home. Harry played in the street where people were fixing it, and he got dirty. He played at the railroad and got dirtier. He played tag with other dogs and became dirtier still. Then he slid down a coal chute and became the dirtiest of all. He changed from a white dog with black spots into a black dog with white spots. After a while, Harry felt tired and hungry and wondered if his family thought he had really run away, so he ran back home. At the house, no one knew he was Harry until he found the scrubbing brush, took it into the bathtub, and let the children scrub him. Then his family knew him, and Harry became clean again and very happy.

Harry was a white dog with black spots who did not like baths. When he heard the water running, he hid the scrubbing brush in the backyard and ran away. He had many dirty adventures. He played where the street was being fixed, ran around the railroad, played tag with other dogs, and slid down a coal chute. Each time, he got dirtier and dirtier until he looked like a black dog with white spots. Later, Harry felt tired and hungry, and he ran home. He sat by the back door, but his family did not know him. Harry tried to show them who he was by doing his tricks, like flip-flopping, flop-flipping, rolling over, playing dead, dancing, and singing. Still, they said he was not Harry. Then Harry dug in the garden and found the scrubbing brush. He carried it inside, jumped into the bathtub, and got his bath. After the children scrubbed him, everyone knew he was Harry, and he was white with black spots again.

summaries.summary: Mr. Hatch was a quiet man who lived alone and did the same things every day. He walked to the shoelace factory, ate lunch by himself, bought a turkey wing, read the paper, and went to bed early. One Valentine’s Day, he found a package on his porch. Inside was a heart-shaped box of candy and a card that said, “Somebody loves you.” Mr. Hatch was surprised and happy. He laughed, danced, and put on a tie and aftershave. After that, he began smiling and talking to people. He shared candy at work, helped Mr. Smith at the newsstand, and found little Melanie Todd when she was lost. He baked brownies, and the neighborhood children came to his house for a picnic. Later, Mr. Goober the postman said the valentine had been delivered to the wrong house. Mr. Hatch gave back the box and card and felt sad again. But the next Saturday, everyone in the neighborhood came to his house with hearts, candy, streamers, and a sign that said, “Everybody loves Mr. Hatch.”

Mr. Hatch kept to himself and lived a very plain life. Every morning he went to work, ate alone, and came home to the same supper. Then, on Valentine’s Day, Mr. Goober the postman brought him a brown package. Inside was a red heart-shaped box full of candy and a card that said, “Somebody loves you.” Mr. Hatch wondered who had sent it, but he was so happy that he laughed, dressed up, and went for a walk. After that, he became friendly with people in his neighborhood. He shared chocolates at lunch, helped Mr. Smith at the newsstand when he was sick, and found Mr. Todd’s little girl at school. He baked brownies and made lemonade, and children and parents came to his yard for a party. Later, Mr. Goober told him the valentine had been sent to the wrong address. Mr. Hatch gave back the box and card and became lonely again. But his neighbors remembered how kind he had been. They filled his porch and yard with decorations and a sign that said, “Everybody loves Mr. Hatch.”

On the first day of school, she worried about what to wear and tried on forty-two outfits. When she looked in the mirror, she found that she was covered with stripes from head to toe. Then many people brought her strange cures, and Camilla changed into even more unusual things. At last a kind old woman offered her plain lima beans. Camilla admitted she loved them, ate them, and all the strange changes disappeared. After that, she ate lima beans whenever she wanted and never had stripes again.

He is actually a wizard named Howl, who is looking for a new apprentice. Before Sophie can speak to him, a witch named Madame Sulleman appears and casts a spell on her, turning her into an old woman. The spell can only be broken if Howl confesses his undying love for her, but there is a problem because he will only do that if the curse is broken first. With help from a talking fire demon named Calcifer, Sophie finds a way into Howl’s moving castle and becomes his apprentice. As she works there, she grows more confident, and Howl begins to care for her. Madame Sulleman later tries to destroy Sophie, but Sophie uses all of her power to break the curse and become young again. Howl confesses his love, they kiss, and together they defeat Madame Suliman and free Calcifer from the castle.

video_title: Tangled: Princess Rapunzel

summaries.summary: A drop of sunlight made a magic flower. Mother Gothol kept the flower and used it to stay young. In a far kingdom, the queen got very sick before her baby was born. People found the flower and made medicine for the queen. She became well and gave birth to a baby girl named Rapunzel with golden hair. Mother Gothol saw the hair and stole Rapunzel. She hid her in a tall tower in the forest. Every year, the king and queen sent lanterns into the sky and hoped their lost child would come home. Rapunzel grew up in the tower. She was kind and curious. On her 18th birthday, she asked to see the floating lights, but Mother Gothol said no. Then Flynn Ryder came to the tower, and Rapunzel hit him with a frying pan. She made him take her to the lights, and they began a big adventure.

Flynn Ryder and the Stabington brothers stole a crown and ran from the guards through the forest. Flynn found Rapunzel's tower and climbed inside. Rapunzel hit him with a frying pan and hid him in a closet. When he woke up, she made a deal with him. He would take her to see the floating lights, and she would give him the crown. Rapunzel left the tower for the first time. She saw the world outside and went with Flynn to the Snuggly Duckling, where rough men helped them escape. They ran from the guards, swung on her long hair, and got out of a flooding cave. Rapunzel used her glowing hair to light the dark and heal Flynn's hand. Then they went to the kingdom and watched the lanterns rise into the sky from a little boat.

Rapunzel gave Flynn the satchel with the crown, and he wanted to stay with her. But the Stabington brothers came, and Mother Gothol used them to cause trouble. Flynn was tied up and sent away, and Rapunzel thought he had left her. Mother Gothol took Rapunzel back to the tower. In jail, Flynn learned that Mother Gothol was behind everything. Maximus the horse and the thugs helped Flynn escape. Flynn rode back to the tower and found Rapunzel tied up. Mother Gothol tried to take Rapunzel away again. Rapunzel said she would heal Flynn if Mother Gothol let her go. Mother Gothol agreed, but Flynn cut Rapunzel's hair with a broken mirror shard so Mother Gothol could not keep her prisoner. Mother Gothol turned to dust, and Rapunzel's hair turned brown.

Rapunzel cried over Flynn, and one tear fell on his cheek. The magic from the tear healed him. Flynn woke up, and he and Rapunzel kissed. They went back to the palace together. Rapunzel met the king and queen, who were her real parents. They knew she was their lost princess and hugged her. The kingdom was happy that Rapunzel had come home. Flynn asked Rapunzel to marry him, and she said yes. Rapunzel was no longer in the tower, and she was with the people who loved her.

Their baby girl, Rapunzel, was born with golden hair, but Mother Gothol stole her and hid her in a tower. Rapunzel watched lanterns rise every year and wanted to see them. When Flynn Ryder came to the tower, Rapunzel hit him, then made him take her to the lights. They traveled outside, met many people, and saw the lanterns from a boat. After that, the Stabington brothers and Mother Gothol caused trouble. Rapunzel went back to the tower, but Flynn came to save her. He cut her hair so Mother Gothol lost her power and turned to dust. Rapunzel healed Flynn with a tear, and they returned to the palace, where she met her parents again and said yes when Flynn asked to marry her.

But before they could kiss, the Stabington brothers came back, and Flynn went to face them.

There she met a wolf, and she told him she was going to her grandmother’s house. The wolf went on ahead to the old woman’s house. When Little Red Riding Hood came, the wolf answered her at the door and let her in. He spoke to her with his big arms, ears, eyes, and teeth. A hunter heard the wolf, came to the hut, and shot him. Then the wolf was gone.

Next he met a bear and then a wolf, and he outran them too. At last he met a fox, who asked him to come closer. The gingerbread man did, and the fox snapped him up.

summaries.summary: Snow White lived in a far away land as a princess, but she did not want to act like a perfect royal girl. She wished she could run in the forest, climb trees, and eat snacks. One day, while walking in the castle gardens, she met a little bird. The bird told her that the woodland creatures were having a picnic and asked her to come live in the forest. Snow White packed bread and cheese and ran away from the castle. In the forest, she found a little cottage made of twigs and leaves. A family of deer invited her inside and showed her a room with flower walls and a soft moss bed. Snow White told them about the castle, and they told her about the forest. She felt happy and like she belonged. The next day, she explored the forest with her new friends. At sunset, she returned to the castle, smiling. After that, she often went back to the forest to stay with the deer.

summaries.summary: Scaredy Squirrel never leaves his nut tree. He thinks the world outside is full of danger, like germs, poison ivy, tarantulas, killer bees, green martians, and sharks. He stays in his tree where he has nuts, a safe place, and the same view every day. He follows the same routine each day: wake up, eat a nut, look at the view, eat more nuts, and go to sleep. He also keeps an emergency kit ready with things like a parachute, bug spray, gloves, a hard hat, soap, lotion, a net, a band-aid, and sardines. He has a plan for danger: panic, run, get the kit, put it on, check the exit plan, and leave the tree. One Thursday at 9:37 a.m., a killer bee appears, and Scaredy Squirrel jumps so hard that his kit falls out of the tree.

Scaredy Squirrel tries to catch his emergency kit after it falls, but this makes something surprising happen. The parachute is inside the kit, and Scaredy Squirrel starts to glide through the air. He learns that he is a flying squirrel. While he is flying, he forgets about the killer bee and all the other things he fears. He feels happy, brave, and free. Then he lands in a bush, gives himself a 5.7 for the dive, and plays dead. He stays still for a long time, first for 30 minutes, then for one hour, and then for two hours. After waiting, he sees that nothing bad is happening in the unknown. So he goes back to his nut tree.

summaries.summary: Captain Swashby loved the sea and moved to a small house near the beach when he retired. He liked being alone and did not want neighbors. Then a girl and her granny moved into the house next door. They brought umbrellas, beach chairs, and fun noises. Swashby wrote messages in the sand to make them go away, but the sea changed the words a little. The girl read the words and played or sang instead. She and Granny invited Swashby for tea, but he said no. Later, the girl played with shells, buckets, and shovels, and Swashby showed her how to use the wet sand and clam shells. Then the sea moved in, tickled the girl’s toes, and washed away her sculpture. Swashby helped when the girl drifted away in a bucket, and everyone laughed and hugged. After that, Swashby shared tea, food, and sea glass with them. He learned that neighbors could be friends, and he wrote, “Thank ye friend,” to the sea.

Swashby came out and taught her how to use wet sand and clam shells. Then the sea moved up the beach, damaged the sculptures, and carried the girl in a bucket. Granny shouted, and Swashby rescued the girl. After that, Swashby shared tea, beach treats, and sea glass with them, and he thanked the sea for helping him make friends.

After retiring, Captain Swashby lived in a small house beside the sea, which he loved very much. His quiet life changed when a girl and her granny moved next door. They set up beach chairs and umbrellas and used the shore in ways Swashby did not like. He tried to keep them away by writing messages in the sand, first “No trespassing,” then “vanish,” and later “Please go away.” But the sea kept changing his words, and the girl turned them into singing, wishing, and playing. Granny invited him to tea, but he stayed indoors. Even so, he came out to teach the girl about wet sand and clam shells, and she made beautiful sculptures. Then the sea rose, washed away the sculptures, and carried the girl off in a bucket. Swashby hurried to help and brought her safely back with a wave. After that, he laughed and shared tea, ice cream, lobster, s’mores, and sea glass with the girl and her granny, and he wrote a message of thanks to the sea.

summaries.summary: A regular girl and her best friend do many things together. She makes things, and he unmakes things. One day the girl decides to make the most magnificent thing. She knows exactly what she wants it to be, so she hires an assistant, gathers supplies, and starts work. She tinkers, hammers, and measures, while her assistant helps in his own way. But when they look at the first thing, it is all wrong. The girl tries again and again. She saws, glues, adjusts, twists, and adds new parts. She makes things square, round, long, short, rough, smooth, big, and small. Still, none of them are magnificent. She gets more and more upset and finally quits. Her assistant takes her for a walk. As they walk, she notices that some parts of the wrong things are actually right. She goes back and makes a new version carefully. At last, they look at it, ride it, and see that it is the most magnificent thing.

summaries.summary: Max says goodbye to Grandpa and gives him a big hug. Behind Grandpa, the big moon shines in the sky. Max and Grandpa look at it together. Max gets into the car and says, "Bye bye, Grandpa! Bye bye, moon!" As the car drives away, Max keeps watching Grandpa until he is gone and only the moon is left. summaries.summary: Princess Pinecone lived in a kingdom of warriors and was very happy for her birthday. Most warriors got battle gifts, but she received cozy sweaters. This year she asked for a big, fast, strong horse, a real warrior’s horse. Her family tried, but they gave her a tiny pony instead. Pinecone said it was too small and too round, and the pony even ate the curtains in her room. A great battle was coming, so Pinecone tried to teach the pony to be a warrior horse, but it did not work. On the day of the battle, the warriors fought with dodge balls, spit balls, hair balls, and square balls. Then Otto the Awful stopped when he saw the pony and said it was cute. Other warriors also paused to admire it. Pinecone realized the warriors could show their cuddly sides. She gave them cozy sweaters, and everyone voted Pinecone and the pony the most valuable warriors.

summaries.summary: Anansi was a spider in Ashanti land. He had six sons: See Trouble, Road Builder, River Drinker, Game Skinner, Stone Thrower, and Cushion. One day Anansi went far from home and got lost. Back home, See Trouble saw that his father was in danger and told his brothers. Road Builder made a road, and the six brothers hurried to help. They found that a fish had swallowed Anansi. River Drinker drank all the river water, and Game Skinner split open the fish so Anansi could come out. Then a falcon carried Anansi high in the sky. Stone Thrower hit the falcon with a stone, and Anansi fell down safely. Cushion came next and helped him land softly. The spider family was happy to be together again. Later, Anansi found a beautiful globe of light in the forest. He wanted to give it to the son who saved him, but he could not choose. He asked Nyame to hold it, and because the sons argued all night, Nyame took the light into the sky, where it still shines.

summaries.summary: Leonardo was a monster, but he was not very scary. He was not big like Eleanor, did not have 1,642 teeth like Tony, and was not weird like Hector. Leonardo tried hard to scare people, but he could not do it. One day, he had an idea. He wanted to find the most scaredy-cat kid in the whole world and scare him. Leonardo looked and looked until he found Sam. He sneaked up on Sam and made loud monster sounds like "Grrr" and "Roar". Sam started to cry, and Leonardo thought he had done it. He shouted that he had scared the tuna salad out of someone. But Sam said, "No you didn't!" Leonardo asked why Sam was crying. Sam told him a long story about his big mean brother, a broken action figure, a hurt toe, soap in his eyes, bird poop on his head, no friends, and a tummy ache. After that, Leonardo decided to become a wonderful friend instead of a terrible monster. He still tried to scare his friend a little sometimes, saying, "Boo!"

summaries.summary: Mirha had waited a long time for her first day of school. Mama, Baba, and Nani said goodbye in the morning, and Mirha went to class feeling excited. But when she told the class her name, many children and even some teachers said it wrong. Some called her Mina, Miriam, Murha, Mero, Me, Mirha, Nera, or Yara. Hayden even asked if he could call her Mayo. Mirha wanted to say, “That’s not my name,” but she stayed quiet and felt sad. At home, she told Mama she wanted to change her name to something easier. Mama told her that Mirha was a beautiful name and that it meant happiness in Arabic. Mama said her name was special and should not be changed. The next day, Mirha told Hayden her real name and showed him how to say it. Hayden said sorry, and they played together. Mirha made her first friend.

video_title: Do Not Open This Book Read Aloud 🛑 | What Happens When You Do Open It? [English] 2025

summaries.summary: The book tells the reader not to open it, but the reader opens it anyway. Then it says not to turn the page, but the page is turned again and again. The voice in the book gets more and more worried and keeps warning that something bad will happen. It says a young boy once saw the next page and his hair turned white, but then it says that was not true. The voice also says it will not speak again, tell the parents, and even offer gold or a flying car if the reader stops. At the end, the voice says to turn the page on purpose, but then admits it was trying to trick the reader. The last warning says a terrible witch turned the voice into a frog if anyone reached the last page. summaries.summary: A grape tells how he used to be sweet, kind, and thankful when he lived in a big bunch with his family. He planned a big party with a fair, a magician, hay rides, snacks, and fireworks. He waited for everyone to come, but nobody arrived. After that, he became angry and started holding grudges against others. Later, he tried to meet his friend Lenny, but bad luck made him late. Lenny got upset and would not listen, and the grape saw how much their anger looked alike. On the way home, he found an old photo of himself and the wrong invitation date. He learned the party had been planned for the wrong day. After that, he began talking things out, letting go of grudges, and becoming sweet again.

This story is about a grape who calls himself a sour grape because he remembers every small hurt. Later, he was late to meet Lenny because of many problems on the way. Lenny stayed angry, and the grape realized he was acting the same way. He found the mistake in the invitation, understood what had happened, and began to let go of his grudges.

Then the panda starts acting silly by playing a banjo badly, hanging upside down, and singing the bamboo Burp song. The narrator decides the panda is a problem. The panda then says jelly beans are raining, aliens might land, and a boat could sail to Antarctica. Soon a second panda appears, and both pandas feel very hungry. They discover the real problem: they are in Antarctica and there is no bamboo. The alien helps them, and together they spell help with jelly beans. The alien ship takes everyone back to the Bamboo Grove, where they eat a bamboo and jelly bean feast.

Later, there are two pandas, and both are very hungry. They realize they are in Antarctica and there is no bamboo there. The alien helps solve the problem. The pandas and aliens spell help with jelly beans, and the alien ship brings everyone back to the Bamboo Grove. At the end, they all enjoy a bamboo and jelly bean feast.

summaries.summary: Allan was a very scary alligator. Every day he polished his scales, sharpened his nails, and brushed his big teeth. Then he went into the jungle and scared the frogs, monkeys, and parrots. Allan loved being scary. At night he went back to the swamp, did his crossword, and took out his false teeth. He kept his false teeth in a secret place, and no one knew about them. One morning Barry the beaver saw Allan and got very frightened. Barry hid behind a bush, and Allan’s false teeth fell out. When Allan woke up, his teeth were gone. He went into the jungle anyway, but without his teeth he was not very scary. Allan went home feeling sad and cried until the next morning. Then the jungle animals came to his swamp and brought back his teeth. They told Allan to stop scaring them. Allan agreed, and after that he became Allan the Gardener, Allan the Hairdresser, Snappy Cuts, and Allan the Dentist. Sometimes he even let Barry borrow his teeth.

Allan came from a family of scary alligators. Each morning he got ready by polishing his scales, sharpening his nails, and brushing his teeth. He practiced scary faces and then went into the jungle to frighten the animals. The frogs jumped, the monkeys fell from the trees, and the parrots screeched. Allan liked this. After his long day, he returned to the swamp, solved the crossword in the Jungle Times, and took out his false teeth. He hid them in a secret place. One morning Barry the beaver saw Allan and became so scared that he hid behind a bush. Then Allan’s false teeth fell out of the bush. Allan woke up and found that his teeth were missing. He tried to scare the jungle animals again, but without his teeth he was not very scary. He went home and cried. The next morning the animals came back with his teeth and said he must stop scaring them. Allan said he did not know how to do anything else. The animals had an idea, and Allan became a gardener, hairdresser, dentist, and more.

summaries.summary: It is time for the octopus to go to school. He wants to stay home and play, but he must get ready. First, he hides, so you have to find him. Then you give him a hug and tell him school will be fun. He holds on tight with his strong suction cups, so tickling helps him let go. Next, you help him get dressed. He tries on many outfits until he finds a perfect ensemble. He gets nervous about school and inks, so he needs to be cleaned up. Then it is time for breakfast, but he may hide again if you turn away. He also wants to bring eight stuffed animals. At school, he is excited and plays hide-and-seek with new friends. His teacher says he looks great. At the end, he gives you one last hug goodbye.

When he hears about school, he gets nervous and inks, so he must be cleaned up. After that, he eats breakfast. You must not turn away, because he might disappear while you spread the mystery mollusk on toast. He does not like hearing about new octopuses, so he may jet away and hide in a tiny hole. When it is time to leave, he chooses eight stuffed animals. At school, he is happy, plays hide-and-seek, and gets a compliment from his teacher. Finally, he hugs you goodbye.

summaries.summary: At the zoo, Chip was the monkey who watched over the animals at night. Most nights, he knew what would happen: the mice would sneak out, the elephants would get scared, the birds would fly out, and the tigers would try to escape. Chip had plans for this. He gave the tigers food, sent the birds back to their aviary, used a pillow to calm the elephants, and brought the mice back with cheese. But one night was much worse. A grumpy pirate penguin named Pete wanted to escape the zoo. Pete wore an eye patch and led an army of alligators. He made a plan to let snakes scare the gorillas, use alligators to scare flamingos, and roll a giant snowball toward the hippo pool. Chip stopped each part of the plan. He brought help for the snakes, fish for the alligators, and bananas to make the snowball miss. Pete’s escape failed, and Chip kept the zoo safe.

summaries.summary: The book says it has no story and tells the reader there will be no elves, pirates, frogs, dogs in cars, rockets, or other wild things. The book keeps saying there will be no pictures, no thrills, and no happy ending. Then the other pages ask why it will not tell a story. They try to help by making up a silly opening about Prince Porkchop Lover and Princess Sleeping Pickle, but the book stops them. The pages and reader give the book a big hug, and then they shake it three times. After that, words start coming out. The book first tells a small story about itself, then begins to imagine more stories with polar bears, pirates, elves, and flying adventures. In the end, the book becomes full of stories and says to imagine a story, a poem, or a play, and never think you have nothing to say.

summaries.summary: Martin Luther King Jr. was a boy who often got hurt, but he always got back up. He loved books even before he could read and said he wanted to get big words when he grew up. When he was 6, he had a white friend and they played together every day. Then they had to go to different schools, and his friend said they could not play anymore because his father said so. Martin learned this was because Martin was Black and his friend was white. His parents told him to choose love instead of hate and taught him that he was as good as anyone else. As he grew older, he saw unfair rules everywhere. Black people had worse schools and had to use different fountains, bathrooms, and lunch places. When he was 14, he was forced to give up his bus seat. Later, he studied religion and learned about nonviolent resistance from Henry David Thoreau and Mahatma Gandhi. He used peaceful protests, speeches, and marches to fight unfair treatment and help change the laws.

Rosa Parks was told to give up her bus seat to a white man in Alabama, but she refused and was arrested. After that, Martin Luther King Jr. helped lead a bus boycott in Montgomery. Black people and some white people stopped riding the buses, even though it meant walking far. Martin gave a powerful speech about justice and was later put in jail and had his house bombed, but he stayed calm and nonviolent. The boycott lasted more than a year, and in the end the bus rules changed so people could not be separated by skin color. After that, more peaceful protests began, including lunch counter sit-ins. Martin was invited to the White House, but he still saw unfairness at home when his daughter could not go to Funtown Amusement Park because it was not open to Black people. He kept working for change. In Birmingham, he was jailed again and wrote his Letter from Birmingham Jail, which was shared with many people. Then children joined marches and helped bring more change.

In Birmingham, more than 1,000 children joined a march and shouted, “Freedom.” The police arrested many of them on the first day, and even more children came the next day. Police used water hoses and dogs to try to stop them, but people across the country saw what was happening and wanted to help. Ninety days later, the rules in Birmingham began to change, and Black people and white people could use the same lunch counters, water fountains, and restrooms. Soon many Americans took part in protests across the country. A. Philip Randolph suggested a big march in Washington, DC, so people from many states came together. They traveled in all kinds of ways and missed work to be there. On August 28, 1963, Martin Luther King Jr. gave his famous “I Have a Dream” speech. He said he dreamed that children would be judged by their character, not by skin color, and that black and white children would join hands as brothers and sisters. After the march, new civil rights laws were passed.

Martin Luther King Jr. kept fighting for voting rights after the civil rights laws were passed. In Selma, Alabama, 600 activists tried to walk 54 miles to Montgomery to tell the governor that Black people should be able to vote. The police attacked them with billy clubs and tear gas, but they stayed peaceful. Two days later, 2,500 people tried again and still could not get through. On the third try, on March 21, 1965, 8,000 people marched with Martin. They walked for two days in the rain while the world watched. President Johnson even sent troops to protect them. When they reached Montgomery, people cried tears of joy. Martin said that when people show hate, we should show love, and when people show violence, we should show kindness. He taught that people must walk the path of peace, march together, and stand united so freedom can ring.

Martin Luther King Jr. was born into a world where Black people were treated unfairly, but he kept moving forward. As a child, he loved books and words, and he learned to get back up after accidents and hard times. He grew up to become a minister and studied ideas about peaceful protest. He used those ideas to help lead the Montgomery bus boycott after Rosa Parks was arrested. He also wrote important words in jail, spoke at many rallies, and led marches with grown-ups and children. In Birmingham, children marched for freedom, and their bravery helped change unfair rules. In Washington, DC, people from many places joined the March on Washington, and Martin shared his dream of fairness for all children. Later, he led marches in Selma to win voting rights. The marches were attacked, but the people stayed peaceful and kept going. Over time, new laws were passed, and Martin’s work helped bring more justice and freedom.

In America, he saw that England ruled the colonies and taxed many things. He became a patriot and gave speeches against British rule. He led a charge against a weak British barrier and helped win the battle. After the war, he worked to build the new nation, helped write the Federalist Papers, and became Secretary of the Treasury. He later died in a duel with Aaron Burr.

In the morning, Nudles was awake and smiling, and he made a new list for us.

summaries.summary: In the Arabian Desert, the evil sorcerer Jafar put together an enchanted scarab. It flew away and led him to the Cave of Wonders. A tiger head told him that only a person of great worth could enter and find the magic lamp. Jafar wanted to find this person, the diamond in the rough. In Agrabah, Aladdin and his monkey Abu ran from palace guards after stealing bread. Aladdin gave the bread to two hungry children. Princess Jasmine was tired of being told to marry a prince, so she left the palace in disguise. Jafar used his snake staff to trick the sultan and learn that Aladdin could enter the cave. He ordered guards to bring Aladdin to the palace. Jasmine met Aladdin in the marketplace, and he helped her escape an angry vendor. Later, Aladdin was taken to the dungeon, but an old man offered him a deal to get the lamp from the cave.

The old man led Aladdin and Abu to the Cave of Wonders. The tiger head opened, and Aladdin was told to touch nothing but the lamp. Inside, they saw piles of treasure. A Magic Carpet helped them find the lamp on a rocky altar. Abu touched a red ruby, and the cave began to shake. Lava rose, rocks fell, and the bridge turned into a slippery ramp. Aladdin and Abu ran for the exit, but a rock trapped the Magic Carpet. Aladdin gave the lamp to the old man, who turned out to be Jafar. Jafar pushed them back into the cave, but the Magic Carpet saved them and helped them escape. Abu pulled the lamp from Aladdin's turban, and when Aladdin rubbed it, a genie came out. The genie promised wishes, and Aladdin made his first wish: he wanted to be a prince. The genie changed him into Prince Ali, and Aladdin rode into Agrabah in a big parade.

As Prince Ali, Aladdin went to the palace and asked the sultan for Jasmine's hand in marriage. Jasmine came in and said she was not a prize to be won. That night, Aladdin visited Jasmine on the magic carpet and told her she should be free to choose. Jasmine saw the carpet and took Aladdin's hand as they flew through the sky. Later, Jafar waited for Aladdin, had his guards throw him into the sea, and thought he was gone. But Aladdin had hidden the lamp and used a wish to escape. He hurried back to the palace to show the sultan and Jasmine who Jafar really was. Before he could do that, Iago stole the lamp and gave it to Jafar. Jafar rubbed the lamp, wished to rule as sultan, and then wished to become the most powerful sorcerer in the world. He trapped Jasmine in an hourglass, turned the sultan into a puppet, and changed Abu into a toy.

Aladdin rushed toward the lamp, but Jafar trapped him behind a wall of swords. Aladdin said Jafar was still second best, and Jafar made one last wish to become an all-powerful genie. A new lamp appeared, and Aladdin used it to trap Jafar inside his own lamp forever. The sultan was impressed by Aladdin's bravery and changed the law so Jasmine could choose her husband. Jasmine chose Aladdin. Aladdin still had one wish left, and he wished for the genie to be free. The shackles fell away, and the genie flew into the sky after saying goodbye. Aladdin and Jasmine held hands and rode the magic carpet into the clouds together.

One night, Jafar found the Cave of Wonders and learned that only one person could enter and get the magic lamp. In Agrabah, Aladdin and Abu escaped guards, and Aladdin shared stolen bread with hungry children. Jasmine left the palace in disguise because she did not want to be forced to marry a prince. Jafar used the sultan's ring and the Mystic Blue Diamond to find that Aladdin was the one who could enter the cave. Jasmine met Aladdin in the marketplace, and he helped her when a vendor got angry. Aladdin was later taken to the dungeon, where an old man offered him a deal. Aladdin, Abu, and the old man went to the Cave of Wonders, found the lamp, and escaped after Jafar revealed himself. The genie came from the lamp, Aladdin became Prince Ali, and he tried to win Jasmine's hand. Jafar later stole the lamp, made cruel wishes, and caused trouble for Jasmine, the sultan, and Abu. In the end, Aladdin trapped Jafar, freed the genie, and married Jasmine.

They hurried back to the castle, safe at home, and Merida hugged Angus because they had saved each other by trusting one another.

summaries.summary: Melvin did not like disappointment. If his cookie had fewer chocolate chips, if he lost a turn in a game, or if he did not get the backpack he wanted, he wanted to throw a fit. At school, his teacher had a rule: "you get what you get and you don't throw a fit." This meant Melvin had to stay calm when he got crayons instead of markers, when he was last in line, or when his napkin was pink instead of green. Melvin thought he could still throw a fit at home. But one night, when it was his turn to choose the movie, he picked Dinosaur Rumble, and his sister wanted to watch a pony movie called Trouble. Melvin told her the rule. Then his family said the same words to him about cookies, games, and backpacks. Melvin wanted to cry and shout, but he did not. He learned the rule was for home too.

Melvin had a hard time when things did not go his way. He got upset about cookies with too few chocolate chips, losing turns, and not getting exactly what he wanted. Dad, Mom, and his sister all repeated it back to him and gave examples from cookies, games, and the sold-out dinosaur backpacks. Melvin realized everyone knew the rule now. He felt like crying and shouting, but he stayed quiet. He did not throw a fit.

The story ends by reminding readers to use school supplies gently so they will last and be ready when needed.

summaries.summary: Every fall, the park rangers invited all the animals to a big woodland party. Boomer the moose was excited and brought his special salad of young branches, maple leaves, and slug slime dressing. But when he saw the humans eating pasta, he wanted noodles instead. That night, after helping with the dishes, Boomer hid under a rug and waited. When everyone was asleep, he sneaked to the dining room, opened the refrigerator, and ate a lot of pasta. He was happy, but he was also noisy, and the park rangers found him and sent him away. Boomer tried to get noodles again by wearing a blue hat and a moustache and going to a restaurant. When his hat fell off, the people saw he was an animal and pushed him out. Sad and hungry, Boomer looked for noodles, but he only found a picture in a magazine. Then he decided to go to Italy, but the airline said he was too tall to fly. After that, Boomer made his own noodles, shared them at his own party, and everyone had a wonderful time. At the end, he added his maple leaf salad too.

summaries.summary: Meg was a box attack who loved to make things from boxes. She built tiny houses, tall towers, and twisty tunnels. Her mother was proud of her and sent her to maker school. There Meg met many makers, like blanketeers, spaghetti texts, tin foilers, and egg cartoneers. Meg was the first box attack in class, and she learned how to make box structures useful, strong, and beautiful. Then Simone arrived. Simone was also a box attack, and she made things Meg had never seen before. The two girls started to argue about how to build. On maker match day, they had to work as a team, but they did not want to. Meg wanted a tree house, and Simone wanted a ship. They built on the same big box and kept making their sides bigger and bigger until the whole thing was used up. Their work almost crashed. Then they stopped arguing, joined the last pieces together, and made one new creation. They did not win first place, but they became friends.

Clifford can sit up and beg, and he can help when they camp out because he does not need a tent. Clifford is not always good. He runs after cars and cats, digs up flowers, and chews shoes. He eats and drinks a lot, and his house is hard to keep. But Clifford is a good watchdog, and bad boys do not come around anymore. One day, the child gives Clifford a bath, combs his hair, and takes him to the dog show. Clifford does not win first prize, but the child still keeps Clifford and likes him best.

summaries.summary: At the big construction site, five trucks wake up in the morning and get ready for work. They see a brand new job: a giant building plan. The job is too big for only five trucks, so Cement mixer blows his horn. More mighty trucks come fast, and soon ten big trucks are in the yard. Skid steer breaks rocks, and Bulldozer clears the land. Excavator digs trenches, and buckhoe sets down drainage pipe. Crane truck lifts a beam, but he runs out of supplies. Then a mighty flatbed arrives with more supplies, and the work starts again. Front end loader and dump truck move dirt and gravel. Cement mixer pours concrete, and pumper sends it up high into the building. The team works hard together, finishes the job, and drives away at night to rest.

Then Sonic heard someone crying for help from Uncle Chuck’s workshop. He stopped the game and rushed there in a blue blur. Sonic saw Uncle Chuck and Robotnik trapped by the tractor. He tried to push the tractor, but it was too heavy. Then he remembered Uncle Chuck’s magic power ring. Sonic ran into the workshop, got the ring, and came back glowing bright yellow. With the ring’s power, he lifted the tractor with one hand and freed them. Sonic carried Uncle Chuck and Robotnik to the hospital.

summaries.summary: It was hot and dry in the land. The red soil was cracked, and the porcupine knew rain was coming because she could smell it. She whispered, “The rain is coming,” and told the zebras. The zebras saw the lightning and told the baboons. The baboons heard the thunder and told the rhino. Then the first raindrop splashed down, and the rhino felt the rain and told the lion. The lion said he could smell, see, hear, feel, and taste the rain. Soon it rained and rained until the rivers flowed fast and the water holes were full. After the rain stopped, tall grasses grew, and the trees made fresh green leaves. The lion rested in the shade, dino lay in the cool mud, the baboons ate fruit, the zebras drank water, and the porcupine said the rain would come back again when it was time.

When a raindrop falls, the rhino feels the rain and tells the lion. The lion knows the rain is here because he can smell it, see it, hear it, feel it, and taste it. Then the rain falls hard and long. Rivers gush, and water holes fill up. When the rain stops, new grass grows, and the trees get green leaves. The animals enjoy the changes: the lion sits in the shade, dino lies in mud, the baboons eat fruit, the zebras drink water, and porcupine waits, knowing rain will come again.

summaries.summary: The sky turns gray, and dark clouds gather over the hill hollow. One by one, animals hurry there to stay safe. First bird comes in, then mouse, squirrel, rabbit, chipmunk, woodchuck, raccoon, possum, red fox, and skunk. Each new animal makes the count grow until ten critters are huddled together in the hill hollow. All night long, the storm keeps going. The wind blows, the leaves swirl, lightning cracks, rain falls, and thunder rumbles and grumbles. In the morning, the sky is clear again. But Alton and the others hear a new rumble and grumble. They turn around and find two sleeping bears making the sound. Before the bears get their scent, the animals fly away, counting backward from ten to one. Then they see that the big storm has changed into a very big beautiful day.

summaries.summary: On hot summer days at Grandma’s farm in Michigan, the sky grew dark and thunder scared the child, who hid under the bed. Grandma, called babushka, told the child it was “thunder cake-baking weather” and said they must make a Thunder cake before the storm came. She explained that the child should count the seconds between lightning and thunder to know how far away the storm was. They found the recipe, wrote down the ingredients, and hurried outside. As the storm moved closer, they gathered eggs from Nellie Peck hen, milk from the kick cow, chocolate, sugar, flour, three overripe tomatoes, and strawberries. Grandma stayed calm and helped the child keep going. They mixed the batter, put the cake in the oven, and finished just as the storm reached the house. They ate the cake together, and after that, the child was no longer afraid of thunder.

Together they find the recipe and collect the ingredients. They get eggs from Nellie Peck hen, milk from the kick cow, and then go through tangle weed woods to the dry shed for chocolate, sugar, and flour. They also pick three overripe tomatoes and strawberries from the trellis. Grandma keeps telling the child to hurry. They return to the kitchen, mix the batter, and bake the cake just before the storm arrives. When the rain falls and thunder shakes the house, they eat the Thunder cake, and the child stops being afraid of thunder.

Inside the cat’s belly, everyone was crowded together. The stable boy used a piece of straw to tickle the cat’s throat. The cat sneezed and threw everyone back out, in reverse order. summaries.summary: A man and a woman lived in a cottage in the forest and had a baby boy. They took him to a fortuneteller, who said that when he was 16, he would marry a princess and become a king. Later, a king in disguise visited their cottage. He did not want the fortune to happen, so he took the baby away, put him in a wooden box, and threw him into the river. But the baby was found by the Miller's young assistant at a mill. The Miller and his wife raised the child as their own. When the boy grew up, the king gave him a letter to take to the castle. Robbers changed the letter, so the queen married him to the princess instead of harming him. The king then sent him to fetch three golden hairs from the devil. The young man found answers to three other problems on the way, got the golden hairs from the devil's granny, and returned home. In the end, the king went to the river fairman, became the new fairman, and the young man became king after marrying the princess.

The Miller and his wife raised him. When he was 16, the king sent him with a letter to the castle, but robbers changed the message. So the queen read that he should marry the princess, and the wedding was held. The king was angry and sent him to get three golden hairs from the devil. On the journey, the young man helped a town with a dead tree, another town with a broken fountain, and a ferryman who needed a helper. At the devil's house, the devil's granny helped him get the hairs. He returned, told the king the answers, and shared the news. Then the king went to the river and became the ferryman, and the luck child became king with the princess.

While the devil slept, she plucked out one golden hair, then another, then a third. Each time the devil complained, she asked him about the strange problems he had heard of in dreams. The devil explained that a mouse under a tree’s roots had stopped golden apples from growing, a toad under a stone had stopped a fountain from flowing with wine, and a ferry pole would make the next person who held it take over the ferryman’s work forever. The granny changed the young man back and gave him the three golden hairs. She told him to leave before the devil returned. The young man then went back on his journey, carrying the hairs and the answers to the three questions.

On the way back, the young man first told the ferryman the answer to his problem after crossing the river. He said that if the ferryman handed over his pole, the next person would have to take the job forever. The ferryman thanked him, and the young man saw jewels on the riverbank and filled his pockets. Next, he returned to the town with the fountain and told the soldiers that a toad under a stone was blocking it. They lifted the stone, removed the toad, and took it outside the town. At once, the fountain began flowing with red wine again, and the mayor gave him a large sack of gold coins. Then he reached the town with the tree that had once borne golden apples. He said a mouse was eating the roots, and when the mouse was taken away, the tree grew leaves, blossoms, and golden apples again. The mayor also gave him gold coins.

The young man returned to the castle with the three golden hairs, two sacks of gold coins, and pockets full of jewels. He told the king how he had found the answers to the town, fountain, and ferryman problems. The king became interested in the jewels and asked where they came from. The young man explained that they could be found on the riverbanks after crossing the river. The greedy king hurried there to get them. When he reached the ferryman, the ferryman handed him the ferry pole, and the king had to take over the job forever. Because the king did not return, the princess became queen, and the young man became king, just as the fortuneteller had said. The princess and the young man lived happily ever after after all the adventures and dangers.

summaries.summary: Kia was a little girl in southern Africa. Her mother died, and her father took Kia to work with the cows. Kia learned how to care for cows and grew strong. Later, her father married a new woman who had a daughter. The stepmother did not like Kia and gave most of the food to her own daughter. Kia became very thin and hungry. One day, by the lake, a shining purple fish came up and asked why she was crying. Kia told the fish her sad story. The fish took her to a watery world with green grass, fat cows, fruit trees, cream, and honey. Kia ate there, then returned home full. She went every day, and the fish sang, “KIA KIA, please be brave.”

Kia kept going to the lake to eat with the purple fish. Her body grew big and strong again. One day her stepmother saw that Kia looked healthy and asked where she got her food. Kia did not answer. The stepmother made Kia’s father follow her, and he saw the purple fish. The stepmother wanted fish stew, so he speared the purple fish and brought it home. The next day Kia waited at the lake, but no fish came. Her stepmother gave her fish stew, but Kia would not eat it. The stepmother and her daughter ate the stew and spat the fish bones on the floor. Kia dreamed of the fish singing, “KIA KIA, please be brave.” In the morning, she gathered the bones and buried them gently in her mother’s grave.

After Kia buried the fish bones, a beautiful purple flower grew from the red earth near her mother’s grave. Beside the flower, a feast appeared on a bright cloth. Kia ate the food and went home. The next day the King’s Men saw Kia sitting by the flower and told the king. The king sent his men to bring the flower, but they could not pluck it. That evening Kia returned, and the feast appeared again. This time a pair of leather sandals was there too. Kia ate, but when she heard the king coming, she ran away and left one sandal behind. The king said he would marry the girl who could pluck the flower and fit the sandal.

The king called all the girls in the kingdom. They tried to pluck the purple flower, but none could do it. They tried to fit the sandal, but none could fit it. The king asked if all the girls were there. Kia’s stepsister said Kia was asleep at home after her work with the cattle, and she said Kia smelled like cow dung. The king told them to fetch Kia. Kia woke up and came to the king. To everyone’s surprise, she picked the flower at once. Then she put her foot into the sandal, and it fit perfectly. The king saw Kia, and soon they were married. There was a great feast and singing. The story says the feast may still be going on.

Kia then buried the fish bones in her mother’s grave. A purple flower grew there, and a feast appeared beside it. The king saw the flower, found the flower and sandal test, and married Kia when she alone could pluck the flower and wear the sandal.

summaries.summary: A mother fox lived with her cubs in a cozy den. In the daytime they played, roamed, hunted, and explored. At night they curled up together, and the mother told them stories. One night she told a story about a fox who walked on a sunny day and smelled cheese in a tree. He saw a crow with cheese in its beak. The fox said kind words and asked the crow to sing. The crow opened his beak to sing, and the cheese fell into the fox’s mouth. The cubs laughed and giggled at the story. The youngest cub liked it best. She thought about it all night and the next day went out alone. She found a crow with cheese and used the same kind words. Then she asked the crow to tell her how he became so wise. The crow began to talk, and the cheese fell down. The little fox caught it and went home. That night, she told the story to the others.

The crow liked the praise and opened his beak, so the cheese fell down and the fox ate it. The cubs thought this was very funny. The youngest cub remembered the story the most. The next day she went out alone and thought about cheese and crows. Soon she saw a crow with cheese in its beak. She spoke politely and said the crow had a beautiful singing voice. When that did not work, she said she was a silly young fox and asked the crow how he learned to be so clever and wise. The crow began to speak, and the cheese dropped into her mouth. She took it and returned home. That night, she told the story herself.

summaries.summary: Anansi, his wife Asu, and their children had very little food because the rains did not come and the harvest failed. Anansi went to the farm with his hoe and dug in the dry ground for root vegetables. Instead of vegetables, he found a buried pot. The pot spoke to him and sang, “Do not wash me” and “Wrap me, tap me, and I will cook.” Anansi asked for chicken stew, and the pot filled with stew. He ate it all, then hid the magic pot in the bushes and went home. He told Asu he had found nothing, and she gave him only hot water with salt and pepper. Later, Anansi returned to the farm many times and used the pot to make porridge and more stew. He kept the pot secret and did not share. One day Asu followed him, saw the pot, washed it at the river, and the magic went away. When Anansi came home and asked the pot to sing, it would not cook anymore.

There was a hard time in Anansi’s home because food was scarce. Anansi told Asu he would go to the farm and dig for root vegetables. On the farm he found a buried pot. The pot talked and sang that it should not be washed and that if someone wrapped and tapped it, it would cook. Anansi asked for chicken stew, and the pot filled up with stew. He ate it all by himself and hid the pot in the bushes. At home, he told Asu he had found nothing, so she gave him only hot water with salt and pepper. The next day and after that, Anansi kept going back to the farm. Each time he used the pot, it made food like porridge and stew. He never shared it. His son noticed that Anansi’s belly was getting big, and Asu became suspicious. She followed Anansi, saw him use the pot, and then washed it in the river. After that, the pot lost its magic, and Anansi could not get any more food from it.

summaries.summary: The child says he is not an ordinary kid. He does ordinary things like riding a bike, eating ice cream, and playing ball, but he does not look like other kids. His mom says he is unique and a wonder, and his dog Daisy agrees. Some people do not see that. They stare, point, laugh, and say mean things behind his back. This hurts his feelings, and it hurts Daisy’s feelings too. When this happens, the child and Daisy put on their helmets and blast off up through the clouds and across the galaxy to Pluto. They say hello to old friends and to the martians. From far away, the child sees that Earth is small, but he knows it is full of billions of different people. He realizes the Earth is big enough for everyone. He cannot change how he looks, but he hopes people will change how they see him. Then they may see that he is a wonder, and that they are wonders too. The story ends by saying, "We’re all wonders. Look with kindness and you will always find wonder."
