summaries.summary: The girl in the story loved watching a TV show about a boy with a magic pencil. He could draw food when he was hungry and draw a police officer when people were in danger. She wished for a magic pencil too. She wanted to draw a lock for her door, stop time so she could sleep longer, erase the smell from the garbage dump, and make her family happy. She wanted beautiful dresses for her mother, schools for her father to build, and a proper ball for her brothers and herself. Every night she hoped for the pencil, but it never came. One day at the dump, she saw a girl her age sorting trash and boys collecting metal scraps. Her father explained that some children had to work and some girls did not go to school. This made her think about unfairness. Later, when girls were told they could not go to school, she began to write and speak out for them. Her voice grew strong, and people around the world listened.

As a child, Malala dreamed of having a magic pencil like the boy on TV. She imagined using it to protect herself, help her family, and make the world better. She wanted to give her mother beautiful dresses, help her father build schools, and make a real ball for her brothers. But each morning, the pencil was not in her cupboard. One day she saw children at the dump sorting trash and gathering metal, and she asked her father why a girl from her area was not in her class. He told her that in their country, some girls did not go to school and some children had to work so their families could eat. Malala felt sad and thought about how girls were not always allowed to follow their dreams. After that, she decided she would use her words instead of a magic pencil. She wrote about her life, traveled to share her story, and spoke for girls who could not speak for themselves. Even when dangerous men tried to silence her, she kept speaking, and many people listened.

When Malala asked her father why the girl was not in her class, he explained that in their country some girls did not go to school and some children had to work so their families could eat. Malala then understood that many girls were not allowed to follow their dreams. She decided she would use words, not a magic pencil, to make the world better.

She decided that if she had a magic pencil, she would erase war, poverty, and hunger, and draw a world where girls and boys were equal. Instead of only wishing, Malala worked hard in school for the next few years. Then dangerous men announced that girls were forbidden to attend school, and they walked through the city with weapons. One by one, girls stopped coming to class. Malala asked her father where the students had gone, and he said they did not feel safe anymore. Malala realized that someone had to speak out, and she decided it should be her.

Malala began writing about what it felt like to be afraid on the way to school and about friends who had moved away because of the danger in her city. She wrote about how much she loved school and how proud she was of her uniform. After that, she kept writing and did not stop. She wrote speeches and traveled around her country to share her story. She also spoke with a reporter from a famous international newspaper, and people wanted to know about her life. Malala said she was speaking for all the girls in her valley who could not speak for themselves. Her voice became very powerful, and the dangerous men tried to silence her, but they failed. Signs appeared saying, “Stand with Malala,” and she was shown with the words, “I am Malala. Hope.”

As more people joined her, Malala’s voice became even louder. She said that together they made a chorus and stood up for what they believed. They raised their voices for people in need and helped people in danger, even if they were far away across the ocean. Malala explained that they should think of the world as a family. She asked again if the reader still believed in magic. This time she answered that she did, because her story was being read by people all over the world and millions now knew it. Those people helped her spread her message of hope. Malala said that she had finally found the magic she was looking for in her words and her work. She ended by saying that one child, one teacher, one book, and one pen can change the world.

summaries.summary: The story begins with a child explaining many things Black people could not do, like play in white playgrounds, go to white schools, or drink from white water fountains. One spring night, the family goes to church to hear Dr. King. He tells everyone it is time to march for freedom, and he asks for peaceful protestors. The parents worry about jobs and safety, but the children say they can march. On May 2nd, many boys and girls meet at church and walk together, singing freedom songs. Police warn them to stop, spray them with water, and threaten dogs, but the children do not leave. Many are arrested and taken to jail. Inside the crowded jail, they sing “We shall overcome.” The marches continue for seven days. The jails fill up, President Kennedy notices, and leaders make a deal. Desegregation begins, and the child finally plays on a playground and eats in a diner that had once been closed to them.

Police try to stop them on different days by threatening jail, water hoses, and dogs. The marchers do not disperse, and many children are jailed, including the narrator. video_title: Read Aloud- The Tree Lady By: H. Joseph Hawkins

summaries.summary: Catherine Olivia Sessions, called Kate, grew up in the woods of Northern California. She liked gathering leaves, pine needles, and flowers to make necklaces and bracelets. At school, she learned to read, write, and count, but she loved science most of all, especially trees. Kate felt the trees were her friends. She studied them in college and learned about soil, insects, plants, and how trees grow. In 1881, she became the first woman to graduate from the University of California with a science degree. After college, Kate moved to San Diego and saw that it was a dry desert town with very few trees. She worked as a teacher and vice principal for two years, then left to become a gardener. Kate searched for trees that could live in hot, dry places. She found many kinds and planted them all over San Diego.

Kate thought San Diego needed trees. She wrote to gardeners around the world and asked for seeds that could grow in the desert. She also traveled to places like South and Mexico to look for trees that liked dry weather, steep hills, and canyons. She found trees such as yucca, Italian Cypress, palm trees, and quiver trees. Kate’s nursery sold trees to people who planted them in yards, streets, schools, parks, and plazas. By the turn of the century, young trees from her nursery were growing all over San Diego. Many people did not believe a desert city could have so many trees, but Kate kept planting them. Her work changed the city little by little, and more trees grew in many parts of town.

In 1909, city leaders said that the Panama California Exposition would come to San Diego in 1915. The fair would be held in City Park, which was later called Balboa Park. Kate saw that the park still needed thousands more trees. She wanted the park to look beautiful and give visitors shade. Kate knew she could not plant all the trees alone, so she asked friends to bring more friends and help in tree-planting parties. Many volunteers came to work with her. They planted enough trees and plants to fill Balboa Park. When the fair opened, San Diego was ready. People came from near and far, walked through the cool shade, and admired the gardens. The fair was so popular that it stayed open for two years instead of one.

After the fair, many people gave Kate awards for her work. They began to call her the mother of Balboa Park. Kate kept gardening and planting trees for many years. She worked until she died in 1940. Because of all her planting, San Diego became the leafy city it is today. Kate had loved trees since she was a child, and she spent her life helping them grow in a place where many people thought they could not live. Her work changed the city and left behind parks, streets, and gardens full of trees.

First, Cupcake wants a beach party with sprinkle castles and sun play, but Muffin says the beach is very hot and some friends might get drippy. Next, Cupcake thinks of a floating boat party, but Muffin says the ship might rock and soup could lose lunch. Cupcake then suggests makeovers with frosting and sprinkles, but Muffin says some friends might think that is icky. Cupcake tries musical chills, but Muffin says someone sitting down fast could get squished. Cupcake runs out of ideas and suggests the lambo with prizes. At last, she decides to rest in her garden. When she opens the gate, all her friends are there. They dance, some get a little drippy, and Cupcake gets a little squished during limbo. Still, it becomes the best birthday party anyone can remember.

summaries.summary: Rosie was a small girl who loved to dream about having superpowers. Every night she went to sleep with her soft toy, Foy meow. One night, a mysterious Force carried Rosie and meow away to a secret garden. Rosie woke up and saw beautiful plants and flowers all around her. Mia told Rosie that they had been chosen by The Secret Garden to help save it from pretend monsters that came at night and hurt the garden with their big footprints and swinging tails. Rosie felt unsure at first, but Mia told her she did not need special powers, only courage and faith in herself. Rosie agreed and went with Mia to find the monsters. They faced many obstacles, but Rosie stayed brave. At last, they reached the monster’s lair. Rosie held meow tightly, a bright light shone around her, and her superpowers awakened. Rosie and meow defeated the monster. When the sun rose, the garden was safe again, and Rosie learned that her true superpower was courage and faith in herself.

summaries.summary: On a very hot first Tuesday of seventh grade, Christy Thomas gets in trouble at school and must write a 100-word essay about decorum. After school, she helps with her younger brother David Michael and talks with her friends Marianne Speer and Claudia Kishi about babysitting. Christy has an idea to make a babysitters club so the girls can work together, answer one phone number, and get more jobs. Marianne says they can meet at her house, and Claudia suggests inviting Stacey Mcgill, a girl from New York. Stacey joins the group, and the girls plan rules, flyers, and a symbol. Christy also has trouble with Watson, her mother’s boyfriend, because she does not want to babysit his children. Later, the club starts getting calls, and the girls begin taking jobs. They learn from each babysitting job and write about their work in a notebook.

The Babysitters Club grows as Christy, Marianne, Claudia, and Stacey make flyers, choose officers, and take phone calls from families. Christy becomes president, Claudia vice president, Stacey secretary, and Marianne treasurer. The girls start getting jobs with the Pikes, the Newtons, and other families. Christy babysits Jamie Newton and his cousins, and Claudia watches the children at another house. Marianne babysits at Watson’s big house, where Andrew and Karen live, and she must keep Booboo the cat away from Mrs. Porter next door. Christy also babysits for Watson’s children and learns more about them. At the same time, Christy’s mother tells her that Watson wants to marry her. Christy feels upset at first, but later she writes a note to Watson saying the fondue was fun and that it is okay if he and her mother get married.

The club has some problems, but the girls keep working together. Their notebook helps them remember each babysitting job. Christy gets calls from the Babysitters Club phone, and the girls take more jobs. One day they plan a pizza party when they see they have earned money, but the party must wait when Stacey goes to New York and Marianne and Claudia cannot pay at first. Christy also has a fight with Stacey because Christy thinks Stacey lied about being in New York. Later, the girls make up. Stacey tells them she has diabetes, not a diet, and that she sometimes goes to New York for doctor visits. The others listen and understand. They agree that Stacey does not have to hide it from them, and the club stays together. They plan more meetings, more jobs, and a sleepover, and Christy feels happy that the club is working.

Christy’s family changes when Watson asks her mother to marry him. Christy is surprised, but she slowly gets used to the idea. She goes to Watson’s house for dinner and sees how he and his children, Andrew and Karen, live. At first Christy is rude about Watson, but later she apologizes in a note and says she will babysit for Andrew and Karen when needed. Christy also learns more about divorce and stepfamilies from talking with the children. Andrew and Karen say they want their parents back together, and Christy understands that they are unhappy too. Christy’s mother says the wedding is still far away and that the children may not all live together. Christy does not know what will happen yet, but she keeps talking with her mother and with Watson. The story ends with Christy still part of her family and still part of the Babysitters Club.

By the end of the story, the Babysitters Club is busy, successful, and close. Christy, Marianne, Claudia, and Stacey answer calls, keep records, and help many families. They babysit Jamie Newton, the Pike children, Pinky and Buffy McKeever, and Watson’s children, Andrew and Karen. They also learn to work through problems. Christy and Stacey stop arguing, Claudia and Christy say sorry to each other, and the girls make new plans for a pizza party and a sleepover. Stacey tells the club that she has diabetes, and the girls accept the truth and support her. Christy’s mother gets engaged to Watson, and Christy begins to accept that change too. In the end, the girls are friends again, the club is still working, and Christy feels proud that their idea has become real.

summaries.summary: The day before Christmas, the PAW Patrol pups decorated the Big Pine Tree outside the lookout. Ryder hung popcorn, Rocky put up lights, Marshall placed ornaments on the high branches, and Rubble helped with the decorations. Skye said the tree needed a star, so she flew up and put the star on top. That night, Ryder watched Santa on the Santa tracker and saw a big blizzard. Then Santa called the lookout. He said his sleigh crashed, he lost gifts, and his magic Christmas star was gone. He needed help to save Christmas. Ryder told the pups to get to work. Rubble dug out the sleigh, Rocky fixed it with a ski, Skye, Marshall, Zuma, and Chase helped find gifts and reindeer, and the pups worked fast in the snow.

The PAW Patrol pups helped Santa after his sleigh crashed in the snow. Rubble dug the sleigh out, and Rocky used his forklift and some recycled parts to repair it. Skye searched the dark sky for lost presents and found one in a tree. Marshall climbed his ladder, Chase used his net, and they caught the falling gift bag. Ryder sent the pups to deliver the presents, and Chase found the reindeer by following tracks in the snow. Skye dropped gifts down chimneys, and Marshall delivered gifts too, even to Mayor Goodway and Chickaletta. Zuma went over the water and gave Wally a fish snack so he could keep going. The pups kept searching for Santa’s missing magic Christmas star.

Ryder used the Santa tracker to find where the magic Christmas star had fallen. He, Rocky, and Rubble went to Farmer Yumi’s yard and found Bettina flying in the air with the star stuck to her side. Rocky called her down with fresh hay, and when she stopped to eat it, he used a mechanical claw to take the star. Ryder then called Santa and told him the good news. Chase found all eight reindeer, but they would not line up, so he used his loudspeaker and guided them back to Santa’s sleigh. Santa was waiting there, and the pups gave him the star. Santa put it back on the sleigh, and the gifts were loaded.

Santa got his magic Christmas star back, and the sleigh was ready again. Skye held the reins for a moment and said she always wanted to do that. The reindeer took off and pulled the sleigh and the pups into the air. Santa whistled, and the reindeer landed back on the ground. He thanked Ryder and the pups for saving Christmas. One day, a new cheese named Wedge came to Tiny Village. Wedge was quiet and shy, while the Big Cheese was loud and proud. Soon the village held its yearly cheese cathlon. The Big Cheese won the first race at first, but he slipped on a pebble and Wedge beat him. Wedge kept winning every event, including chess, and never bragged. In the end, Wedge was named first place. The Big Cheese felt upset at first, but then he calmed down, went home, and talked with Wedge. He learned that losing can teach humility, empathy, and joy in taking part.

If someone catches a leprechaun, he may grant a wish, but if he gets away, there is no wish, no luck, and no gold. To try to catch one, children need a plan and the right gear. They build a trap with a box, a bottle cap, glitter glue, tape, gold paint, rocks, and glue. They make the rocks look like real gold and add a rainbow slide inside the box. Then they close the drapes, dim the light, and wait quietly. A sound is heard, but when they check, the leprechaun has escaped. He leaves behind a shoe and a note signed by Liam the leprechaun. The note says the trap was clever, but he cannot be trapped by a cardboard box. The story ends by saying to enjoy St Patrick’s Day and try again next year.

A rainbow slide is made inside the box, and the children wait in the dark with the drapes closed. Then they hear a crinkle snap and rush to look. The leprechaun has escaped. He leaves one shoe behind, and inside it is a note from Liam the leprechaun. He thanks the children for the shiny things and says their trap was clever, but it was not enough. The story ends with a reminder to enjoy St Patrick’s Day and try again next year.

Then they woke up and found the real parade beginning, with marching bands, dancers, pipers, the mayor, police, fire fighters, and bears dressed as leprechauns.

video_title: 🧜‍♀️ All About MERMAIDS! Read Aloud Book for Kids | Mermaid Book for Kids

summaries.summary: Some stories say mermaids sing to sailors and cause storms, but this book says those ideas come from mistakes and superstition. It explains that mermaids are close relatives to humans and live in family groups called pods. They live in many places around the world, in seas, rivers, lakes, mountain streams, and desert water holes. Mermaids are built for speed and have tails, webbed fingers, and smooth skin with markings that help them hide in water. Their hair can be many colors, and they spend time grooming and braiding one another’s hair. Mermaids love music and shiny things. They usually stay near the water’s surface in warm sunlight and dive only to hunt for food. They eat plants, small animals, fish, and other sea life. They also make things like nets, hooks, hair pins, and combs. Mermaids sleep on rocks or float upright in the ocean, often near sperm whales.

The story explains that mermaids are not fish from storybooks, but real sea creatures with smooth tails, webbed fingers, and many kinds of hair and skin colors. They swim by moving their tails up and down, and their markings help them blend into the water. Most mermaids live in family pods, while mermen often live alone. Baby mermaids are called welps, and they are born knowing how to swim. As they grow, they play hiding games, peeking out and swimming away fast. This helps them learn speed and stealth. Grown mermaids eat algae, plants, snails, turtle legs, crustations, and fish. They use their nimble fingers to hunt and to make useful things like lobster pots, fishing nets, hooks, horns, harps, and hair pins. If someone finds a shell comb or a mermaid’s purse on the beach, it may have come from a mermaid.

Mermaids are found in many waters around the world, except the coldest, wildest, and most dangerous places. Some stay near shore, and others live in the open ocean. Freshwater mermaids also live in rivers and lakes, and they were once seen in busy port towns. Now they are harder to spot. Mermaids are known for their beautiful singing, and humans hear it but do not understand it. The book says sailors used to think mermaids sang to bring storms, but they are more likely warning others that bad weather is coming. When a mermaid leaps from the water by moonlight, twirling through the air, it means the weather will stay calm and the skies will be clear. Mermaids are friends with dolphins and swim and hunt with them. Welps like to play with seal pups, but mermaids fear great white sharks, orcas, and humans.

summaries.summary: Sylvian was visiting her grandmummy in Connecticut on Halloween. She put on her bonnet and went with Wiggy to the cornfield on the hill to find the biggest pumpkin for a pumpkin moonshine. The hill was steep, so they puffed like steam engines. In the field, Sylvie found a very large pumpkin, but she could not lift it, so she rolled it along like a snowball. When the pumpkin reached the sloping edge, it began to run away down the hill. It bumped over stones and bushes and rushed into the barnyard. The goats, hens, and geese were frightened, and the pumpkin hit Mr. Hemelscamp, who was carrying a pail of white wash. Sylvie helped him up and said sorry to the animals. Then she told Grandpop, who cut the top off the pumpkin, took out the seeds and pulp, and made a face in it. They put a candle inside and placed the pumpkin moonshine on the front gate post. Sylvie saved the seeds, planted them next spring, and many pumpkins grew.

summaries.summary: Laura lived in the Big Woods of Wisconsin in a little log house with her pa, ma, Mary, Carrie, and their dog Jack. Paw said that after he finished planting the crops, they could all go to town. Laura and Mary were excited, but they did not know much about town because they had never seen a store. When Paw said, “We’ll go to town tomorrow,” Ma washed Laura and Mary and put rags in their wet hair so it would curl. In the morning, they wore their best dresses and got into the wagon with Ma, Paw, and baby Carrie. They rode through the woods, saw rabbits and deer, and then Paw showed them Pepin. In town, they went into the big store, where Laura saw many things. After the trading, the storekeeper gave Laura and Mary candy. Then the family ate lunch by the lake and rode home tired. Paw sang that there is no place like home.

summaries.summary: One fine morning, a young click beetle went for a walk. At noon it climbed up and down a flower. In the afternoon it rummaged through pebbles. In the evening it crawled among tall grass. At night it climbed a tree, got tired, and fell to the ground on its back. It tried to turn over, but it could not, so it cried, “HELP.” A wise old click beetle had been watching. The old beetle said it would teach the young beetle how to click, flip through the air, and land on its feet the next morning. The young beetle slept. The next day the old beetle showed how to do it. Then the young beetle tried many times, but it kept landing on its back. Earthworm, turtle, snail, and mouse all passed by and spoke to it. Then something very big appeared, and the young beetle was scared. The old beetle called, “QUICK, CLICK and FLIP!” The young beetle clicked, flipped, did three somersaults, and landed on its feet.

In the kitchen, he baked seed cookies for the birds from mashed bananas and sesame seeds. His mom asked what he was doing, and George said the birds would love them. Then he loaded the warm cookies into his trailer and drove back to the snowman. Mr. Snowman thanked him and said George had a heart full of kindness. George laughed and said the birds had tummies full of seeds. The next morning, George saw that the snow was gone and the birds could find food again. After that, whenever it snowed, George brought seed cookies so the birds never went hungry.

summaries.summary: A very clever dingo sat by a billabong and decided to make wombat stew. He put a billy on the fire and said he needed the fat wombat for his stew. Platypus came by first and said mud would be good in a stew, so dingo let him tip in big blobs of mud. Then emu came and said feathers would help, so dingo dropped in feathers. Blue-tongue lizard came next and said flies were good, so he caught many flies and added them too. Echidna arrived and said a stew needed slugs, bugs, and creepy crawlies, so he put those in as well. Koala came down from the gum tree and said nuts would be nice, so he added nuts. At last dingo said only the wombat was missing. When he bent down to taste the stew, he found it was bad and rushed away into the bush. The others had tricked him, and the wombat was safe.

Koala came down from a scribbly gum tree and said nuts would help, so nuts were added. Dingo kept dancing and singing as the stew bubbled. At the end, he said the stew still needed the wombat. When he tasted the stew, he cried that it was poisoned and ran off into the bush. The other animals had fooled him, and he never came back for the wombat.

His friends came around him, and he said that sometimes all you have to do is be brave and jump.

Detective Dog found a cap on the shelf, then followed the smell of the thief through the town, past the traffic lights, the farm, the zoo, and the takeaway shop, and on into the woods. She found a man with a sack full of books. He said his name was Ted and that he had only meant to borrow them. Peter took Ted to the library, where Ted got a library card and could borrow books for free. After that, Ted read books in his backyard, and Detective Dog kept visiting the school on Mondays.

summaries.summary: Monty the manate was shy on his first day at Sea school near the ocean’s Gates. He waved goodbye to his mommy and slowly paddled to school. Monty tried to make friends with the jellyfish in the sea grass, but they told him to leave them alone. He met Sydney the shrimp, who shouted at him, and Monty said sorry. At lunch, Monty offered food to Sammy Seal, but Sammy said he liked fast and cool creatures and did not want to play. Then other fish laughed at Monty and said mean things about manatees. Suddenly, a big shark came racing toward them with open jaws. Monty stayed very still like a rock, just as his mommy taught him, and tucked the others under his tummy. The shark swam away, and the other sea creatures cheered for Monty. They said sorry for being mean, and Monty said they should all be friends and stop the bullying. From then on, they played nicely, and Monty shared a message about being kind and seeing what is on the inside.

He keeps dancing and joins Gish Grace and then Franken Stein. The Big Bus takes the monsters through town, and everyone does the Halloween Hustle. The bus stops, and Skeleton gets off to go to the shops. He buys a snazzy hat and a jazzy jacket, but a big black cat makes his bones scatter again. He tapes himself back together and goes to the party in fancy clothes. Inside, the ghost greets the guests and the dance contest begins. Skeleton dances until zombie foot gets in the way and his bones scatter once more. A skeleton girl sweeps up his bones and fixes him with strong glue. Then she asks him to dance, and all the monsters cheer and clap.

summaries.summary: It was New Year’s Eve, the last day of December. The family was excited, and the puppy was excited too. The child asked to stay up until midnight, and the parents said yes. They drove to the store to buy party hats, horns, poppers, streamers, balloons, glitter, and stars. At home, they decorated the rooms and hung a banner for baby New Year. Then they ate a late dinner with family favorites and cupcakes. They made a toast and talked about New Year’s resolutions, but the child could not think of one. Mom said that was okay. After dinner, they played games and shared happy memories. As midnight got close, they watched the countdown on TV. They cheered, used horns and poppers, and then the puppy and the children got very busy in the house. Soon the children went upstairs for a short nap. In the morning, the child saw that they had missed the new year and decided to stay awake next New Year’s Eve.

On New Year’s Eve, the family was ready to celebrate. The child begged to stay up until midnight, and the parents agreed. The family went to the store and bought hats, horns, and poppers. Back home, they put up streamers, balloons, silver glitter, gold stars, and a banner for baby New Year. They ate a big late-night dinner with their favorite foods. After dinner, they made a toast and talked about New Year’s resolutions. Dad had many, but the child had none, and Mom said that was fine. Then the family played Checkers and cards and remembered old holidays, camping trips, and new baby cousins. Later, they watched the crowd in Time Square and counted down from 10. When midnight came, they blew horns and popped poppers. The puppy, the brother, and the child got active in the house, and then everyone became quiet. The children went upstairs for a short nap. In the morning, they woke up to sunny light and saw they had missed the new year. The child then made a resolution to stay up next New Year’s Eve.

summaries.summary: Naughty Ninja came home from jungle training covered in mud, leaves, and flies. He went into his secret ninja training camp in the backyard and said he needed food. Dad said he must take a bath first, and Mom said they would have Ninja nuggets for lunch. Dad warned him not to say “ninja to the rescue,” because something bad always happened. But Naughty Ninja did not listen. The flies came to Dad, and Naughty Ninja thought they were wild poisonous flies. He shouted “ninja to the rescue,” and Dad ended up in the bathtub with his clothes on. Then Naughty Ninja thought Dad might be in trouble with invading Samurai Warriors, so he shouted it again and poured in bubble bath. The tub filled with bubbles, and the bathroom became a mess. Naughty Ninja ran, Dad slipped and slid, and Naughty Ninja slid too. Mom came in, saw the mess, and then said the soapy water had cleaned the house. Naughty Ninja and Dad looked around and saw everything was spotless.

summaries.summary: Mrs. Millie is a silly teacher who says funny wrong words all day. In the morning, she tells the children to hang up their goats, and they remind her that they mean coats. At 8:00, she says, “Please rise for the Frog salute,” but the children know she means the flag salute. At 9:00, she asks them to get out paper and Penguins, and they say she means pencils. At 10:00, it is recess time. Mrs. Millie says it stopped raining cats and dogs and tells them not to step in a poodle. The children laugh and say she means a puddle. After recess, she says it is time to chameleon, and they tell her she means come in. The day goes on with more silly mistakes at lunch, story time, art, and home time. At the end, the children put on their hats and mittens, say goodbye, and wave as they go home.

Mr Rex asked how she felt and told her it was okay to feel angry, but throwing things could hurt someone. video_title: 📚 Kids Read-Aloud Book 📚 A Tiger Like Me By Michael Engler.

summaries.summary: A little tiger wakes up in the Tiger’s Den when the sun comes up. He stretches, breathes in deeply, and roars loudly because he is wide awake. He does not want cold water, soap, brushes, or combs, so he runs away from the bathroom and slips past Mom at the door. Then he eats a big breakfast of Tiger Flakes and blood orange juice. After that, he sees a hiding place in the forest and sneaks inside. But it is not a game. A trap snaps shut and holds him tight. He calls for help and struggles, but that only makes it worse. Tiger mom comes quickly, grabs his paws, and pulls him out. The little tiger is safe again and ready for more tiger adventures.

The tiger goes outside into the snow wearing his winter tiger coat and soft tiger hat. He runs across the plains, and snow sprays under his paws. He roars, breathes out warm air, and catches snowflakes with his tongue. He jumps, pounces, rolls, and falls, but he does not get hurt. Later, when his stomach rumbles, he goes back into the house to look for food. He moves quietly through the kitchen shadows and jumps onto a chair. On the table, he finds a big, tasty tiger cake. He smiles because he is very hungry. The tiger enjoys the snowy play and then finds a good treat to eat inside the house.

Later, the tiger paints his face black and orange and creeps up on Dad, who is hiding behind his newspaper and asking for peace and quiet. The tiger stalks from the door to the sofa, takes a deep breath, and jumps with a big roar. The newspaper rips, and Dad jumps up in surprise. Dad tries to catch the tiger, but the tiger is too fast and escapes. Dad sends him to his room. There, the tiger builds a den from chairs and blankets. It is soft, dark, and safe, and he says it is a perfect hideaway for tigers. After that, tiger mom, tiger dad, and the tiger sit together on the carpet and make things with paper, glue, pencils, ribbons, clay, scissors, folding, tying, sticking, painting, and cutting.

The tiger says he does not need to brush his teeth, because that is for human children, not tigers. He shakes his head and digs in his claws. Later, it gets dark very quickly, and Dad sends him to his sleeping place. The tiger is still full of energy, so he listens to the sounds in the hall and the big bedroom. He hears floorboards creak, shadows move, and sheets rustle. Then he sneaks into his tiger parents’ den and snuggles between them. Tiger dad strokes his fur, and tiger mom rests her paw on his tummy. The tiger feels warm and cozy and falls asleep. He thinks about how good it is to be a tiger.

At the end of the day, the little tiger returns to his den after a long, exciting day. He lies down worn out after all his adventures in the forest and on the plain. Everything becomes quiet. The little tiger shuts his eyes and dreams. The story shows his day from morning to night, with roaring, running, snow play, a trapped moment, a scare for Dad, play with his parents, and finally sleep in the tiger den.

video_title: 📚 Kid's Read-Aloud Book 📚 Angry Ninja  By Mary Nhin.

summaries.summary: One day, the little sister used the jump rope without asking, and the child got very angry. The child felt a tight throat, a fast heart, and heavy breathing, and then exploded with anger. Later, Positive Ninja came over, and they played pig. When the child started losing, the child got upset again. Positive Ninja said anger is normal, but the way you handle it matters. Positive Ninja showed the 1 + 3 + 10 strategy. First, say one word like “relax” or “breathe.” Then take three slow, deep breaths. Last, count to 10. Positive Ninja also said to use an “I am” statement, like “I’m mad at you for breaking my toy.” After that, the child went inside for chocolate cake and found that the sister had eaten the last slice. The child felt angry again, but remembered the strategy. The child said “Breathe,” took three deep breaths, counted to 10, and said, “I’m upset that there’s no more chocolate cake.” It worked.

summaries.summary: The dinos love donuts. They dip them in jelly, add sprinkles, and eat the glazed and cake-crumb ones. They eat donuts because they are good for prey and help dinos see danger far away while they eat sweet dough all day. The dinos also like the holes, because the holes fit on horns and spikes, and a stick can help reach them. But the dinos love dancing even more than donuts. They dance from dawn to dusk and all through the night. Triceratops, raptors, Stegosaurus, Brontosaurus, and Pterodactyl all dance in different ways. Their dancing makes the palm trees shake, their footprints make pools, and dust floats like wigs around their heads. The dinos wait in line for donuts because they need a lot of food. A child makes a giant donut for the dino dance. The dinos love it, but they do not like the center hole, because they fear rocks. First, children open their eyes and notice all skin colors. Second, they use their words to talk about race, because silence does not stop racism. Third, they point to unfair policies instead of blaming people. Fourth, they say there is nothing wrong with people, even when people are treated differently. Fifth, they celebrate all differences. Sixth, they knock down the stack of cultural blocks and welcome each group’s own ways of speaking, dancing, and creating. Seventh, they confess when they say racist things and learn from mistakes. The story also says anti-racist babies keep learning and growing. In the end, they believe racism can be overcome and they do not judge a book by its cover.

summaries.summary: Julian goes on a subway ride with his abuela. He sees three ladies dressed like mermaids and dreams about being in the ocean as a mermaid too. When they get off the train, Julian asks if abuela saw the mermaids. Abuela says she did. Julian then says, “I am also a mermaid.” At home, he gets ready to make a mermaid look. He uses a plant for a headdress and curtains for a mermaid tail. When abuela gets out of the shower, Julian feels scared because she looks unhappy. But abuela calls him over and gives him a necklace to go with his outfit. Then she takes him outside and says, “You’ll see.” Julian whispers, “Mermaids,” and abuela answers, “Like you, mijo.” Then they join the mermaids together.

But baby did not stay in bed. He boogie woogied with a frisky little goat, then chance the cha-cha with a chocolate colored cow. Each time, mama and papa asked baby to listen and rest. Then baby danced with a shaggy little sheep. Mama said she gave up, and papa said baby was not sleepy. At last, mama said to get the fiddles, and they had a big pokefest in Arkansas. They danced until night came. Papa got tired. Then mama and papa kissed baby and put him to bed, with dance dreams in his head.

video_title: Virtual Storytime: 'Radiant Child: the Story of Jean-Michel Basquiat' by Javaka Steptoe

summaries.summary: Jean-Michel grows up in Brooklyn and dreams of becoming a famous artist. At home, he draws all day at a table covered with pencils and papers. His mother, Matilde, draws with him on his father Gerard’s old work papers and teaches him that art can be found in city streets, games, clothes, words, books, theaters, and museums. When they visit a museum, Jean-Michel studies the art and learns about artists like Picasso. At home, he draws while Gerard plays jazz and Matilde cooks arroz con pollo. After a car accident, Jean-Michel is frightened, but Matilde gives him a book about bones and body parts. He studies it until he is no longer afraid. Later, Matilde becomes ill and cannot stay at home. Jean-Michel keeps visiting her and shows her his artwork, telling her it will one day be in a museum.

As a teenager, Jean-Michel tells his father that he will be a very, very famous person one day. He leaves Brooklyn for New York City and begins living in the Lower East Side with friends, sleeping on couches and floors. During the day, he wears a green paint-splattered jumpsuit and makes collages and drawings everywhere he goes. At night, he spray paints poems and pictures on downtown walls. He signs his work with the name Samo, and people start wondering who Samo is. His art moves from street corners to gallery walls. Jean-Michel uses strong colors, lines, collages, and paint on anything he can find. His art is messy and not inside the lines, but it still stands out. He likes to work with the radio and TV on loud while he paints for long hours.

Jean-Michel becomes known as a bright and creative artist. People call him wild and a genius child, and he keeps drawing crowns for himself and the people he admires. He often flips through magazines and books and paints late into the night, sometimes for days. Sounds and images fill his head while he works. Even though many people watch him and admire his art, he keeps making his own kind of pictures. As a grown man, he still visits his mother when he can. At his biggest shows, he saves the place of honor for Matilde and puts her there like a queen on a throne. In the end, Jean-Michel is a famous artist, and his mother is honored at the center of his success.

At home, he draws while his father Gerard plays jazz and his mother cooks. He continues visiting her and bringing his artwork, hoping to show her how far he will go.

video_title: Virtual Storytime with Ms. Andrea: What Do You Say Dear

summaries.summary: A child learns many polite things to say in different funny situations. First, the child meets a baby elephant and says, “How do you do?” Then a fierce dragon appears outside the castle and blows red smoke, but a brave knight rides up and cuts off the dragon’s head, and the child says, “Thank you very much.” Next, a nurse helps a patient who was bitten by a dinosaur and says, “You’re welcome.” Later, the child bumps into a crocodile while walking backwards downtown and says, “Excuse me.” At a wedding, the bride is very hungry and asks, “Would you please pass the cake?”

The story continues with more polite words. At the princess’s ball, the princess tells a secret, but the bears in her orchestra make so much noise that the child cannot hear it, so the child says, “I beg your pardon.” Then the child goes to London to visit the queen. The queen invites the child to dinner, and there is spaghetti for the appetizer, the main dish, and a salad. When spaghetti is also served for dessert and the child cannot fit in the chair anymore, the child says, “May I please be excused?”

Next, the child flies an airplane and remembers that the duchess said, “Do drop in for tea sometime.” The child drops in, but the airplane makes a large hole in the duchess’s roof. The child says, “Uh oh! I’m sorry.” After that, the child becomes a dangerous pirate and captures a fine lady on the ship. Every morning, when she is untied for breakfast, she says, “Good morning. How are you?” The pirate answers politely too.

At the end, all the child’s friends come to the house for a party. The princess brings her orchestra of bears, and they play two dances. Then the bears want to eat everybody up. The child says, “This is the end. Goodbye.” The story shows many times when the right polite words are said in different places, like the castle, downtown, London, the duchess’s house, and the pirate ship.

Later, the child is a pirate with a captured lady who keeps speaking politely at breakfast. In the last scene, friends come for a party, the bears play music, and then they try to eat everyone, so the child ends the party and says goodbye.

Then they spread the feast on a quilt in the cave and sit together, eating, chatting, and saying thanks.

They saw a tiny farm and met Farmer Mac Nugget, who wore denim and called to his turkeys by name. The turkeys ran, flapped, and greeted the children. Then one child saw an axe by the door and asked about it. Farmer Nugget said the turkeys might be chopped up and roasted for Thanksgiving. The children became upset and cried. Farmer Nugget and the teacher went to the well and brought back water for everyone. After the children drank, they felt calmer and were mysteriously fatter. They thanked Farmer Nugget and left on the bus, huffing because they felt stuffed. When the bus drove away, no turkeys were left on the farm. The next evening, eight families had eight fluffy turkeys as guests, and everyone ate vegetables, jelly, and toast. They gave thanks for love and living and had a happy Thanksgiving.

The first two chairs were too big, and the last chair was just right, but it broke. Goldilocks went upstairs and tried three beds. The first bed was too hard, the second bed was too soft, and the third bed was just right. She fell asleep in that bed. Then the three bears came home. They saw that someone had eaten their soup, sat in their chair, and slept in their bed. Goldilocks woke up, saw the bears, ran down the stairs, and hurried back into the forest.

summaries.summary: Three white mice hide on a white piece of paper because of the cat this morning. Then they find three cans of paint and begin to play. One mouse jumps into red paint and comes out red. Another mouse jumps into blue paint and comes out blue. The third mouse jumps into yellow paint and comes out yellow. Next, the yellow mouse jumps into the red paint and becomes orange. The red mouse and blue mouse mix their colors and make purple. The blue mouse and yellow mouse mix their colors and make green. Soon the paint gets sticky, so the mice wash themselves in the sea. After that, they paint the paper instead of their bodies. They make blue, yellow, red, purple, green, and orange colors on the paper. They leave some paper white so they can still hide from the cat.

summaries.summary: In a cave in the woods, a great brown bear sleeps through the long cold winter. He snores in his deep dark lair while the snow falls outside. A mouse creeps into the cave and makes a small fire. The mouse and the bear do not wake up. Then a badger comes in, and they share honey nuts. More friends come too, like a wren, a raven, and a mole. They all go into the bear’s den, make food, and talk and chatter. The bear keeps sleeping through all the noise. At last, the fire stirs the bear awake. He grumbles because everyone had fun while he slept. The friends share more corn and tea with him. Bear eats and drinks, and then he tells tall tales through the night. When the sun comes up, the bear cannot sleep, but his friends snore.

The animals give him more popcorn and tea. Bear gulps, gobbles, and then tells tall tales through the blustery night. When morning comes, the bear cannot sleep, but his friends are snoring.

Froggy said he was awake and wanted to go out. His mother told him to look down because he had forgotten something to wear. Froggy took off his hat and boots, then put them back on and went outside. Soon his mother told him to look down again. Froggy saw he had forgotten his shirt, so he went back inside. Then he took off his mittens, untied his scarf, and took off his hat, but he kept on his pants, boots, and socks. He put on his shirt and went out again. His mother asked if he forgot anything else. Froggy had on a scarf, coat, shirt, pants, boots, and socks, but he was missing his underwear. Froggy went back inside, took off some clothes, got too tired, and went back to sleep.

summaries.summary: Little green said his first word: "go." He liked the word and practiced it in a quiet voice, a medium voice, and then a very loud voice. He could not wait to share it, so he bounced into town and shouted "go" for everyone to hear. Naptime was ending, and bulldozer woke up first. He said he was going to surprise dumptruck, and he pushed dirt up the hill. Then everyone woke up and started building a new bridge. They lifted, carried, drove, scooped, pushed, mixed, and held. Little green kept shouting "go-go-go," and the workers moved faster and faster. Soon things got too wild, and no one knew what to do. Little green tried whispering, but that did not help. Then a stranger rolled into town and shouted "stop." That word helped everyone rest and get organized.

After the stranger said "stop," little green and little red worked together. They were opposites, so they said many words back and forth: go, stop, stop, go, go, stop, go, stop, go. At first it was hard. Too much go made everyone crash into each other. Too much stop made everyone stay too far apart. They kept trying different ways to work until they found the right pattern: go, go, go, stop. That was the perfect amount for getting work done. Little green and little red liked working together, and they became good at it. The new bridge was finished just in time. Everyone was happy. Then the cars raced across the bridge.

summaries.summary: In the morning, the big trucks got ready to work. Crane said, “Let’s hoist.” Doza said, “Let’s push.” Digger said, “Let’s dig.” They built tall buildings, roads, and bridges. The flower grew, but the city grew too. Soon there was only one open space left. Crane said they needed a building there. Dozer blew smoke and cut the flower down. Digger saw little seeds in the rubble. He took the seeds and drove far away to a place no big truck had been. There he dug them into warm earth and cared for them every day.

summaries.summary: In India, on a big river island, a boy loved trees. He saw that the floods were taking away the land and leaving sandbars. Animals lost their homes, and the boy worried that people and animals would be in danger. He told the village, and the elders gave him 20 bamboo saplings. The boy went by canoe to a sandbar and planted them one by one. Every day he brought water, carried buckets, and cared for the young plants. He worked hard until the bamboo grew into a thick patch. Then he brought cow dung, earthworms, termites, ants, and seeds from other villages to make the soil better. He kept planting as he grew up. Soon the small patch became a big forest. Buffalo, rhinos, snakes, gibbons, birds, and elephants came back. The man kept planting more grass and fruit trees, and he protected the forest so it could stay alive.

The elders gave him 20 bamboo saplings and sent him to help. He rode a canoe to a sandy place and planted the bamboo. Each day he watered the plants, carried heavy buckets, and built a way to give them water. The bamboo grew into a healthy thicket. The boy wanted more plants to grow, so he brought soil helpers like cow dung, earthworms, termites, and ants. He also brought seeds from other villages and planted them. Over many years, he kept working, and the land changed into a forest. Animals came back to live there. When tigers came, he planted more grass. When elephants came to farms, he planted fruit trees. He also protected the forest from people who wanted to cut it or hunt the animals.

summaries.summary: Mouse woke in the night and heard strange sounds. She looked in many places in her house, but she did not find the thing making the noise. Mouse thought it was a ghost. The next day, she told her friends. Ren, Spider, Bunny, and Mole gave ideas for catching the ghost, but Goat said it would not work. Mouse tried the plan that night anyway. She made a web, spread peas, and turned off the light. But when the sounds came back, Mouse slipped on a pea and fell into the web. Goat then told Mouse that cheese was the best way. Mouse put cheese on the table, behind the door, and under the chair. She hid in the closet and listened. Soon she heard nibbling sounds. Mouse turned on the light and found a tiny, scruffy mouse named Mac. Mac said he had no home and asked to stay. Mouse said yes after a bath. Mac’s full name was Malachi Gim crack. Mouse called him Mac. After that, Mouse and Mac lived in the house together, and they had a party with cheese.

summaries.summary: Little Craig loved birthday parties, but he did not get invited to many. One day, Joey, the new kid at school, gave Craig a bright blue invitation to his party. Craig was very happy and told Joey he would be there. At home, Mom put Joey’s party on the family calendar. The next day, Craig got another invitation from his friend Dan. He thought he could go to both parties, but Mom showed him that both parties were at the same time on the same day. Craig first wanted to choose Dan’s party, then he wrote a letter to Joey saying he could not come. Mom asked him to think about how Joey would feel. Craig also thought about going to both parties for a short time, but Mom helped him see that would not be fair either. In the end, Craig kept his word and went to Joey’s party. He ate cake, played games, won a prize, and made a new friend. Mom was proud of him.

Craig loved parties with balloons, cake, games, and prizes. He was excited when Joey, the new boy at school, invited him to a birthday party. Craig said yes right away, and Mom wrote the party on the calendar. Soon after, Dan gave Craig another invitation. Craig thought he had two parties to enjoy, but Mom saw that both parties were on August 23rd at 1 p.m. Craig had to choose. He first thought about going to Dan’s dance party and crossing Joey off the calendar. Then he wrote Joey a letter to say he could not come. Mom asked him to imagine how Joey would feel if kids kept sending letters like that. Craig then tried to make a schedule so he could attend both parties, but Mom helped him think about how Joey would feel if everyone left early. That night Craig dreamed Joey was alone at his party. The next day he told Dan he could not come. On party day, Craig went to Joey’s party, had cake, played games, won a prize, and made a new friend.

summaries.summary: Goldilocks loved Baby Bear. They ate snacks, read books, and played hide and seek together. They did many things together, but they did not clean up. Then one day, Baby Bear was gone. Goldilocks looked everywhere, but the place was very messy. She saw messes on the table, on the chair, and on her bed. Goldilocks cried and fell asleep because her bear was lost. In her dream, she ran into the dark Woods to find Baby Bear. She came to a cottage inside a big oak tree. The door was open, so she went in. Inside, she saw a big mess. Goldilocks cleaned the dishes, fixed a broken chair, put books away, and tidied the bedroom. Then she took a nap. While she slept, the Three Bears came home. They saw the clean dishes, the fixed chair, and the tidy room. Baby Bear found someone sleeping on his pillow. Goldilocks woke up and saw Baby Bear.

summaries.summary: It is the first day of kindergarten, and a bus driver gets ready to take children to school. Polly is on the bus too. The driver tells the children the rules: stay in your seat, do not yell, keep your hands to yourself, and respect your friends. Some children say they miss their daddy, doggy, teddy, Mommy, and blankie. They also say they are scared. The driver tries to sound brave like a pirate, but Polly sees that the driver is scared too. The driver says the brave pirates were only pretending. The children learn that being brave means doing what you have to do even when you are scared. Then everyone sings and rides on to kindergarten. When they arrive, the driver says school is a treasure. The children will learn to read and write, play games, make new friends, and run around at recess. Polly follows the bus, and the children get off to begin kindergarten adventures.

summaries.summary: Mikey Yam danced to the front door and told his mom he was almost four years old. He said his birthday party would be full of friends, presents, and a big cake. He thought about pizza, tacos, burgers, hot dogs, pork and fried rice, and many other foods. He asked his family for help and remembered birthday meals from his granny, his Nona, and his cousin’s twins. Still, he could not choose between Chinese food and Italian food. Mikey felt mixed up and ran to the park. There, his friend Sophia asked what was wrong. Mikey said he could not pick a dish for his party. Sophia told him he did not have to choose only one and could have both. Mikey went home and decided on fried rice and marinara sauce. The next day, his mom and friends made the food, and everyone loved it. They all shouted, “Different is good!”

summaries.summary: Kora loved the smells and tastes of Mama’s Filipino dishes, and she wanted to be a real cook. Her older sisters and brother usually did the grown-up jobs in the kitchen, while Kora only got small jobs. One day, when her sisters went to the mall and her brother went outside, Kora asked Mama what they were making. Mama let Kora choose, and Kora asked to make pansit. Mama gave Kora Lolo’s red apron and told her about cooking with him in California for Filipino farm workers. Then Mama showed Kora how to wash her hands, soak the rice noodles, shred the cooked chicken, chop the vegetables, and stir the food in the big pan. Kora made one mistake with the noodles and spilled water, but Mama helped her clean it up. That night, the family ate the pansit, and Daddy said it tasted like Lolo’s pansit. Kora felt proud and thanked Mama.

Kora put the rice noodles in water, shredded the cooked chicken, and watched Mama chop celery, carrots, cabbage, onions, mushrooms, garlic, and ginger. When Mama sliced onions, both of them cried and laughed. Kora checked the noodles the wrong way and spilled water, so Mama gave her a towel. Then Kora stirred the food in the big pan while Mama added the noodles. At dinner, Mama served the pansit with adobo chicken, lumpia, and pineapple. The family ate it, and Daddy said it tasted like Lolo’s pansit.

summaries.summary: Anil loved hearing stories about a far away village with green wheat fields and coconut palms. One day he asked who was telling the story, and his grandfather, D, began to speak. D told of a lad in a village far away who amazed the villagers. The lad wrestled a water buffalo, tied cobras in a knot, and spun three elephants by their tails. D said the lad got his strength from hot, hot Roy made by Baba and Dma. The lad ate many Roy with mango pickle, and then his power came back like a great flood. Later Anil wanted to know if the power could return again, but there was no Roy at home. So Anil made the dough himself. In 1849 she ran North to Freedom. She helped other people escape too. Her secret path was called the Underground Railroad. Abraham Lincoln saw many people working as slaves in America. In 1863 he became president and signed a paper saying all the slaves would be free. Susan B. Anthony wanted girls to vote too. She tried to vote and got arrested. She kept speaking for fairness, and in 1920 women in America got the right to vote.

summaries.summary: Craig Robinson lived in his town with many kids who looked different from one another. Even so, they all wanted the same shiny yellow 10-speed bike. Craig wanted it too after seeing it in the store window. He asked and helped with chores and homework until Mom said they could buy the bike. Craig rode it happily all the way to Rainbow Beach and stopped at the ice cream stand for a double scoop chocolate brownie ice cream. Then a police officer stopped him and said the bike was stolen. Craig said his mom had bought it, but the officer took him home anyway. Mom talked with the officer, and he put the bike on the lawn and drove away. Later, Mom told Craig that some people treat others badly because of skin color, and that is called racism. She also told him to feel good about himself. Craig felt better, ate ice cream, and took one more ride on his bike.

summaries.summary: Louise was a cat who lived at the fire station after a big rescue long ago. He liked to go visiting in the fire truck and was often given leftovers. One night, after too much catnip and too many sardines, he took a wrong turn. He climbed a wall and saw Tabitha, a pretty cat behind a thick glass door. Louise and Tabitha looked at each other and fell in love from far away. Tabitha’s owner, Sho, was not happy. The next morning, Louise brought Tabitha a bouquet made of sardine tins, twine, and feathers. The next day he brought mice. After that he brought pigeons. Then he brought balloons, which was hard for a cat to do. Every day, Louise and Tabitha kept staring at each other until Sho chased Louise away. After that, Louise asked his friends for advice over a bowl of cream.

Crane said, “Let’s hoist,” Dozer said, “Let’s push,” and Digger said, “Let’s dig, together.” They built tall buildings, roads, and bridges until the loud whistle blew. Then the trucks took a break, but Digger found a tiny flower in the rubble. He greeted it and cared for it every day. He watered it when it looked dry, shielded it on windy days, and sang it a bedtime song at night. The flower grew, but the city kept growing too. Soon there was only one empty space left. Crane said they needed to put a building there, and Dozer cut the flower down. When the smoke cleared, Digger saw little seeds in the rubble. He scooped them up and drove far away to a place no big truck had ever been. There he planted the seeds in warm earth and cared for them every day.

summaries.summary: Leo was a busy boy with too many things to do. He thought making a list might help, but the list kept getting longer. Leo wished there were two of him. Then a knock came at the door, and another Leo appeared. This second Leo took the list and said they could finish it together. Soon a third Leo came, and then more Leos kept joining. They made a team of four, then five, then six. After talking for a long time, they decided they needed a seventh Leo. With seven Leos, there was even more work. Leo said they would need eight just to rest a little. Eight Leos worked very fast, but then they thought maybe nine or even ten Leos would help. All the Leos kept working. One Leo shouted that there was no time to stop or rest. Finally, Leo became tired and went to sleep. When he woke up, the other Leos asked what he had done. Leo said he had been dreaming. Dreaming was not on the list, so the other Leos disappeared. Leo then thought about doing less but doing his best, and he decided one Leo was enough.

With seven Leos, there was seven times as much work, so Leo said they would need eight just to catch their breath. The eight Leos worked hard and kept adding more ideas, like nine and ten Leos. At the end, Leo thought that doing less and doing his best might be enough.

Later, under the moon, a chipmunk waits in its underground home. At the hilltop fire, the child eats hot cocoa, hot dogs, and marshmallows while a black bear sleeps nearby. A queen bumblebee rests until spring. At the end, the child skis home tired and falls asleep, dreaming of the animals under the snow.

summaries.summary: There was a boy who had no toys. Every day he went to the park and sat under a big tree while other children played. Sometimes they let him join, and sometimes they did not, so he felt sad. One day he found an unusual stick leaning against the tree. When he picked it up, he became a pirate, a baseball player, and a knight. He saw words carved on the stick and sang them: "Imagination lives in you. It’s the fire in all you do. Use it well, and you can be anything you want to be." The boy carried the stick everywhere and imagined many things, like a fisherman, a canoe paddler, and a hiker. He grew up, built a house on a hill, and gave his time, wealth, and heart to others. When he became old, he still went to the park. He saw a little girl sitting alone under the tree, so he placed the stick there. She picked it up, became a princess, a fencer, and a surfer, and sang the words too. Then the old man smiled and went home.

summaries.summary: The child had a pet unicorn and had heard, “never let a unicorn scribble.” The child wondered why, so they gave the unicorn one crayon. The unicorn ate it. The child tried tying crayons to the unicorn’s horn. Then glitter scribbles shot everywhere, on the floor, ceiling, and lamp. The child worried because their mom was coming. The child explained the whole mess, but the mom smiled. She said it was not a mess. The scribbles were all on one big piece of paper on the easel. She called it a glowing masterpiece. In the end, the child learned that great art can begin with a scribble, and a unicorn can make art too.

summaries.summary: Mikey was getting ready for a party, but he could not choose what food to serve. He thought about pizza, tacos, burgers, hot dogs, pork, fried rice, pasta, Chinese food, and Italian food. He remembered food from family birthdays and felt confused because he liked both his mom’s Italian food and his dad’s Chinese food. He went to the park because his head felt full of choices. There, his friend Sophia saw that he was sad and asked what was wrong. Mikey said he could not pick a dish for his party tomorrow. Sophia told him he did not have to choose only one kind of food. She said he could have both. Mikey liked this idea and ran home to tell his family. He decided to make fried rice with marinara sauce. The next day, his mom cooked the rice and vegetables, and everyone helped. When the friends tasted the food, they liked it very much. The party ended with everyone saying, “Different is good.”

summaries.summary: Chelsea and her family get ready for Chinese New Year. They clean their house to get rid of bad luck and buy new red clothes because red means good luck. Chelsea says people in China have celebrated this holiday for a very long time. At night, the family goes to her grandparents’ house. Uncles, aunts, and cousins are there, and they talk, play games, and laugh. They eat a big feast with fish and other foods, and then they make dumplings. Chelsea waits for midnight to eat them. Firecrackers snap and fireworks shine in the sky. Chelsea stays awake until Chinese New Year begins. She also hears a story about a monster called NEN, who was scared by loud noises and the color red.

After the big night, Chelsea falls asleep in the morning. When she wakes up, Mom and Dad give her a red envelope, and money falls out. Chelsea learns that children often get red envelopes from grownups, family friends, and neighbors during Chinese New Year. The celebration does not end right away. Chelsea and her family keep wearing their new clothes, giving presents to friends and family, and trying to be very good. She hears that Chinese New Year used to last 15 days, and some people still celebrate for several days. This is part of starting the new year in a good way.

At the end of Chinese New Year, there is a big parade. Chelsea says her favorite part is the dragon. Dad says dragons are lucky. He also explains that many Chinese men moved to California in the mid 1800s and brought the Chinese New Year celebration there. Now San Francisco has a big Chinese New Year parade every year. The parade has a dragon that is very long. Chelsea feels that Chinese New Year is over, but she has enough luck to last until next year.

Chelsea tells about Chinese New Year, also called Spring Festival or Lunar New Year. Her family gets ready by cleaning the house and buying red clothes. On the night before the holiday, they go to her grandparents’ house. Many relatives come, and they celebrate together. They share food, make dumplings, and wait for midnight. Fireworks and firecrackers announce the start of Chinese New Year. Chelsea stays awake through it all. She also hears the story of NEN, a monster that people scared away with loud sounds and red things.

Chinese New Year is a very important holiday. Chelsea and her family are busy getting ready. They clean out bad luck and wear red for good luck. The holiday date changes each year and happens in January or February. On the holiday night, Chelsea stays at her grandparents’ house with many relatives. They talk, play games, eat a feast, and make dumplings. At midnight, fireworks go off, and the new year begins. Chelsea later gets a red envelope with money. The family keeps celebrating for days, and the holiday ends with a parade and a long dragon in San Francisco.

summaries.summary: Kora loved Mama’s kitchen and wanted to be a real cook. Her older sisters and brother usually did the grown-up jobs, while Kora only got small jobs. One day, when her sisters went to the mall and her brother went outside, Kora asked Mama what they would make. Mama let Kora choose, and Kora asked to learn pansit. Mama gave Kora her red apron and told her about L, who wore it long ago when he cooked for Filipino farm workers in California. Mama and Kora got the ingredients and soaked the rice noodles in water. Kora shredded cooked chicken, chopped vegetables, and helped stir the noodles in the big pan. She made a small mess with the noodles, and Mama showed her how to check if they were soft. At dinner, the family tasted the pansit and said Kora had done the grown-up jobs. Daddy said it tasted like L’s soup, and Kora felt proud.

Kora liked the smells of Mama’s Filipino food and wished she could cook like her older sisters and brother. Usually, they helped with shredding chicken, mixing noodles, and rolling lumpia, while Kora only had kid jobs. One day, her sisters and brother were gone, so Kora asked Mama what they were making. Mama asked Kora what she wanted to cook, and Kora chose pansit. Mama let Kora wear her red apron and told her about L, who had worn it before and cooked for Filipino farm workers. Mama gathered chicken, vegetables, soy sauce, ginger, and garlic, and Kora put the rice noodles in water to soak. She shredded chicken, helped chop and stir the food, and learned that onions make people cry. Kora spilled some noodle water, but Mama showed her how to check the noodles with two fingers. That night, the family ate the pansit, and everyone said Kora had done the grown-up jobs.

Mama and Kora got chicken, celery, carrots, mushrooms, onions, cabbage, ginger, garlic, soy sauce, and rice noodles. Kora put the noodles in water, shredded the chicken, and watched Mama chop the vegetables. When Mama cut onions, both of them cried a little. Then Kora helped stir the noodles in the big pan. summaries.summary: This is unicorn. This is horse. Unicorn has a sapphire horn, a silver coat, a rainbow mane, and perfect white teeth. Unicorn eats pink cupcakes, makes rainbows, and dances. Squirrel uses unicorn’s horn for ring toss, bird lines nests with unicorn’s long hair, and the animals share cupcakes. Horse says he does not like unicorn, but he really wishes he were unicorn. One night, two men come quietly to the paddock and tie up unicorn. They put him in their truck and drive away. The other animals wake up and try to help, but squirrel cannot run fast enough, bird cannot fly fast enough, fox cannot run on the road, and turtle cannot run at all. Horse thinks, then runs after the truck and uses his big teeth to free unicorn. Unicorn thanks horse, and horse says, “You’re welcome.” After that, horse and unicorn both share things, and they become friends.

summaries.summary: One day, a new family moved to Alphabet City. The family was made of punctuation marks, and Exclamation Point led the way on their first day at a new school. Exclamation Point was excited, Question Mark wondered about everything, Period helped bring the line to a stop, and Comma kept pausing and asking others to wait. When they arrived, the letters stared and asked who they were. The punctuation family explained that they were not letters, but they liked being around words. The class let them join in. Exclamation Point made the words sound exciting, Question Mark asked questions, and Period ended sentences neatly. Comma tried to fit in, but as the day went on, he felt smaller and smaller. He thought he only got in the way, so he quietly left the classroom. Soon the letters and punctuation made too much noise, the words became tangled, and everyone fell into a messy pile. Outside, the others found Comma and told him that he had an important job. Comma returned to the class, and the family worked together again.

Benji’s box was made by Benji, Mama, and Samuel last summer, and it is cozy and safe, but it is only big enough for Benji and his blue blanket. Samuel is supposed to tiptoe and speak softly when Benji has a bad day. Samuel wants a box like that too. He looks at Benji’s block city, tries a karate kick, and learns he cannot take karate classes that day because it is Tuesday and they must visit the super happy lady at Benji’s Clinic downtown. At the clinic, Benji never bounces the ball or plays games, and Samuel waits in the waiting room. Later, Mama usually makes berry smoothies and wraps Benji in his blanket like a burrito, but not today. Benji finally comes out, wraps Samuel in the blanket, and says, “You’re my little burrito.” Samuel lets Benji in too and says, “You’re my little brother.” Mama finds them together and asks to come in too.

summaries.summary: Little Sock lives in a drawer with other socks. At night, after the other socks go to sleep, he sneaks out of the drawer and through a hidden tunnel in the back of the dryer. This tunnel leads to Sock City, a place where only socks can go. In Sock City, there are many fun things to do, and some can be done alone. But some things are better with a friend. Little Sock looks around and sees another sock who is alone. He wonders if she could be his friend. He feels nervous and thinks about how to ask. Then he takes a deep breath and says, “Will you be my friend?” She says yes, and they are happy. The story ends by saying that making new friends is fun and that some things are better with a friend.

summaries.summary: A bus driver greets the children on the first day of kindergarten and says his parrot, Paulie, is with him. He acts like a pirate and tells the children the rules for the bus: stay in their seats, do not yell, keep their hands to themselves, and respect others. The children are worried because they miss their moms, dads, dogs, teddy bears, and blankets. The pirate bus driver says they should be brave, but then the ride gets bumpy and he becomes scared. He admits he was pretending to be brave so the children would feel brave too. The children say that it is okay to be scared and still do what you need to do. When the bus reaches school, the driver says kindergarten is a place for learning, playing games, and making new friends. Paulie follows the bus, and the driver is happy because Paulie stayed with him.

On the first day of kindergarten, a bus driver talks like a pirate and introduces his parrot, Paulie. He tells the children to stay in their seats, keep quiet, and follow the rules. Many children on the bus cry because they miss their families, pets, and special things from home. The driver tries to sound tough and says they should be brave. Then the road gets rough and full of puddles, and he gets scared. He tells the children that he was only acting brave so they would feel brave too. The children explain that being brave means being scared but still doing what you need to do. After that, everyone calms down and the bus reaches kindergarten. The driver says school is a place for learning, games, and new friends. At the end, Paulie follows the bus, and the driver is glad he did not leave.

summaries.summary: Little Craig loved birthday parties, but he did not get invited to many. One day, Joey, the new kid at school, gave Craig a bright blue invitation to his party. Craig was happy and told Joey he would be there. He ran home and showed the invitation to his mom, who wrote the party on the family calendar. The next day, Craig got another invitation from his friend Dan. He wanted to go to both parties, but the invitations were on the same day and the same time. Craig tried to make a plan, then thought about writing to Joey or leaving early, but his mom helped him think about how that would feel to Joey. Craig dreamed of Joey’s party with no friends there. The next day, he told Dan he could not come. On party day, Craig went to Joey’s party, ate cake, played games, won a prize, and made a new friend.

Craig loved parties, balloons, cake, games, and prizes. Then Joey gave him an invitation to a birthday party, and Craig said yes. Craig’s mom put the party on the calendar. The next day, Dan gave Craig another invitation. Craig was excited until he saw both parties were at the same time on the same day. He tried to solve the problem by thinking about a letter and then by making a schedule, but his mom asked him to imagine how Joey would feel if friends did not come or left early. Craig had a dream about Joey’s party being empty. After that, Craig told Dan he could not come to his party. When the day came, Craig went to Joey’s party. He enjoyed the balloons, cake, games, and prize. Craig felt good because he kept his word, and he made a new friend.

His mom asked him to think about how Joey would feel if every child did that. Craig then made a schedule so he could go to both parties, but his mom again helped him think about Joey’s party. Craig dreamed that Joey’s party was empty and sad. In the morning, Craig told Dan he could not attend. He kept his promise to Joey, went to the party, enjoyed the cake and games, won a prize, and made a new friend.

summaries.summary: Sammy has a very bad day. At recess he gets yelled at for kicking the fence. At lunch, the kitchen runs out of his favorite pizza, so he does not eat on the bus ride home. Then the bus driver misses his stop, and Sammy has to walk home in the rain. When he gets inside, he is hungry, cold, and wet. He sees Benji in his special box, which Mama made for him because Benji has bad days at preschool. When Benji has a bad day, everyone tiptoes and speaks softly. Sammy wishes he had a box like that too. Benji is in his box with his blue blanket, and Mama is busy. Sammy gets more upset when milk spills everywhere in the kitchen. He cries mad, sad, shivery tears. Then Benji comes out, wraps Sammy in the blue blanket, and calls him his little burrito. Sammy opens the blanket and lets Benji in too, calling him his little brother. Mama finds them together, and the family stays close and safe.

summaries.summary: A story speaks to a boy and tells him to dream big, work hard, be kind, and help others. It says to say hello, please, thank you, and I love you. It also says to listen to other people’s stories and tell your own. Then the story tells about Sarah, who lived before the Civil War and was forced to obey her owner. Sarah dreamed of a husband, a family, and a job she loved. When a new law freed people from slavery, Sarah moved to Chicago. She married Archibald Good, rented rooms to people who needed help, and saved money for her own furniture store. Sarah listened to her customers and learned that many families needed more space. She made a fold-up cabinet bed, fixed it when it broke, and kept trying until it worked. Sarah then asked for a patent. After waiting and sending papers again, she finally received the patent for her cabinet bed, and her name was printed in history.

The story begins by telling a boy to be himself, dream big, and work for what he wants. It says the world needs a smart, brave, kind boy who helps people and treats others well. She married Archibald Good, helped people by renting rooms in her home, and saved money to open a furniture store. Sarah worked with her husband and listened to customers who needed more room in their homes. She made a new kind of bed that folded into a cabinet. The first tries went wrong, but she kept fixing it until it worked. Then Sarah asked for a patent. The first answer said no, so she changed the papers and sent them again. At last, the patent office sent her the patent, and Sarah’s invention and name were remembered.

She made a fold-up cabinet bed, but it failed at first. Sarah kept trying until the bed worked well. Then she sent papers to get a patent. The first answer was no, so she changed the papers and sent them again. In the end, Sarah got the patent from the U.S. government, and her invention became part of history.
