summaries.summary: Craig Robinson lived in Craig's Town, where children looked different but all wanted the same shiny yellow 10-speed bike. Craig wanted that bike after seeing it in the store window. He asked and asked, did chores, and finished homework until Mom finally said they could buy it. Craig was very happy and rode his new bike to Rainbow Beach. He went to buy ice cream, but a tall police officer stopped him and said the bike was stolen. Craig said Mom had bought it, but the officer put the bike in his car and took Craig home. Mom was angry and talked to the officer. Then the officer gave the bike back and left. Craig and Mom went for ice cream in the park, and Mom told him that some people may treat him unfairly because of his skin color. She said no one can make him feel bad if he feels good about himself. Craig understood, and then he rode home with his bike.

Little Craig Robinson wanted a shiny yellow 10-speed bike that all the kids in his town wanted too. He saw it in a department store window and asked Mom for it many times. After lots of chores and homework, Mom said, “Let's go buy that bike.” Craig was excited and rode it to Rainbow Beach. He stopped at the ice cream stand and asked for a double scoop chocolate brownie ice cream. Before he got it, a police officer told him the bike was stolen and took it away. Craig said his mom had bought it, but the officer did not listen and drove him home. Mom argued with the officer, and then he put the bike back on the lawn and left. Craig and Mom sat in the park with ice cream. Mom explained that racism and prejudice can make people treat him badly because of his skin color. She told him to feel good about himself. Craig looked at his bike and wanted one more ride.

The child says that tomorrow they will ask to be a firefly knight.

summaries.summary: Po and Papa get ready for Chinese New Year by following many lucky rules. Po says the family must sweep out bad luck before the new year, so the child sweeps dirt out the back door and cleans the windows very well. Po also says not to clean on New Year’s Day, because that could sweep away good luck. Next, Po gets a bath ready and tells the child to wash hair before New Year’s Day, because washing on the holiday is bad luck. The child washes three times and helps with the baby brother too. Mama makes a whole chicken and a fish with the head and tail still on, so the family will stay together and have a good beginning and ending. She also cooks long noodles, and the child eats them without breaking them. Red and gold banners, paper cuts, and a lucky sign are put on the door, and everyone stays awake to welcome Chinese New Year’s Day.

summaries.summary: On Christmas Eve, Marie and Fritz waited outside a bright ballroom and peeped through the keyhole. They smelled spruce tree, puff pastry, and music. At last the doors opened, and Fritz ran to the gifts while Marie looked at the room and the tall Christmas tree with candles, ribbons, and apples. Their godfather, Judge Drosselmeyer, showed Marie a wooden doll called the Nutcracker. He cracked a walnut in the doll’s mouth, and Marie loved the toy and hugged it. Fritz wanted to try it too, but he used a very hard nut and broke the Nutcracker’s jaw. Marie took the doll away, bandaged his jaw with a ribbon, and sang to him until she fell asleep under the tree.

While Marie slept, she dreamed strange things. She saw a human queen and a mouse queen arguing. She saw a baby change into a goggle-headed creature. She also saw a young man help turn that creature into a lovely lady. Then the young man looked like her Nutcracker, bowed to the lady, and stumbled back. When Marie woke at midnight, the party was over. Toys and mice were lined up for battle. Fritz’s soldiers stood with the Nutcracker at the front, and a huge seven-headed Mouse King led the mice. The two sides fought hard, but the toy army was losing. Then the Mouse King jumped on the Nutcracker. Marie threw her shoe at the Mouse King, knocked off all seven crowns, and drove the mice away.

After the battle, the Nutcracker reached out to Marie, and she suddenly became small like him. The soldiers made an arch with their swords, and the Nutcracker led her under the Christmas tree. They walked through it like a forest, and snow began to fall. Soon they heard water and found a small river with a swan-shaped boat. The Nutcracker lifted Marie into the boat, and they floated past many strange lands. Marie looked at all the wonders, but she kept watching her dear Nutcracker, who sat beside her with his wooden sword and wide-eyed grin.

The boat stopped on a shining shore, and the Sugar Plum Fairy welcomed Marie and the Nutcracker to her kingdom. She led them to her palace. In a grand hall, dancers performed for them. First came Spanish dancers, then Arabian dancers, then Chinese dancers balancing teacups, and then Russian dancers who spun very fast. After that, Mother Ginger came out with her wide skirts, and gingerbread girls and boys danced from under them. At the end, the Sugar Plum Fairy danced too, and flowers moved around her. Marie held the Nutcracker’s hand and looked at all the lovely magic.

Marie blinked and woke up in the ballroom. Sunlight came through the windows, and she was still asleep behind the Christmas tree. Godfather Drosselmeyer stood nearby and smiled at her. Then he showed her a shy young man, his nephew, who had come from a distant land down a long and winding river. Marie saw that he was the boy from her dream and looked like her Nutcracker. She ran to him and hugged him. After that, Marie and the young man grew up and had many adventures together in kingdoms, forests, oceans, and mountains in the land down the long and winding river.

summaries.summary: Buu was a little ghost who loved carving pumpkins, trick-or-treating, and parading in the street. But he was afraid of the dark. He stamped his foot and said he needed help because it was hard to be brave alone. So he went to visit his friends. Witch, Frank, Dracula, Werewolf, and Mummy all told him that the dark was their friend and that they liked to do their special things at night. Witch made spells, Frank danced, Dracula flew like a bat, Werewolf howled at the moon, and Mummy walked in bandages. Buu went home smiling because his friends helped him feel better. He decided to thank them with a party. He closed the drapes, made the house dark, and got ready all day. When his friends came, they stayed up late, made potions, flew, howled, and danced. Buu danced too, glowed in the dark, and had fun until morning.

summaries.summary: Pierre was a little penguin in a big museum at the California Academy of Sciences. He lived with 19 other penguins in African Hall, where Pam fed them fish two times a day. One day, Pam saw that Pierre was in trouble. His feathers had fallen out, and his bottom was bare. Pierre was cold and scared to swim because he thought the water would make him even colder. Pam tried a heater, and the vet gave pills, but Pierre still shivered. The other penguins were afraid of him because he looked so strange. Then Pam had a new idea. She asked if Pierre could wear a wetsuit. Pam and a friend made a tiny wetsuit, and a company helped make it from neoprene. Pierre wore it, felt warm, and dived into the water. After six weeks, Pierre grew new feathers and did not need the wetsuit anymore.

summaries.summary: Two children talk about being scared. One says, “I am not scared,” but then they both name scary things like snakes, hairy spiders, fried ants, an alien with pink eyes and furry teeth, and a roller coaster with a snake. They decide to be scared together. Then they argue over a chair. Each one says the chair is theirs and says, “It’s mine.” They both get upset and say sorry. After that, they ask to play. At first they are not friends, but they try to play together. They make music, then play dinosaur hunters. A friend comes back, and all three children play together. They build a jeep, and one child pretends to be the dinosaur. They roar loudly and scarily. In the end, they say they are best friends and play spies and build a castle, adding flags, towers, arches, windows, stairs, a gatehouse, and a drawbridge until it is perfect.

summaries.summary: The story begins by saying that poop is yucky, but it also says that every creature poops, from aardvarks to the humped zebu. It explains that different animals have different names for poop, like guano for bat or sea bird poop and dung for other animals. summaries.summary: The story teaches that monsters can be noisy, messy, hungry, selfish, mean, wild, tired, or grumpy, and children can help them behave. If a monster is noisy, whisper, “Be quiet.” If it is hungry, give it a fork and a spoon and say, “Chew your food.” If it is selfish, say, “Take turns.” If it is mean, walk away and say, “Good bye.” If it scares you, scare it back and say, “Boo.” If it makes a mess, say, “Clean up.” If it is wild, give it a timeout and say, “Sit still.” If it is tired and grumpy, send it to bed and say, “Go to sleep.” If it asks nicely, kiss it and say, “Good night.” The story says that next time you catch a monster running wild, you will know what to do.

After teaching how to help monsters be good, the story shows how to make paper plate monster masks inspired by Monster Be Good. The materials are paper plates, colorful tissue paper, large googly eyes, construction paper, scissors, and lipsticks. First, the tissue paper is cut into small pieces, and each monster can have one color, such as blue or green. Next, glue is spread on the paper plate and the tissue paper is added one piece at a time. Then, a mouth and two ears are cut from construction paper. After that, googly eyes are added, followed by the ears and mouth. The makers say their masks can look like an ogre, vampire, cyclops, werewolf, or dracula. The story ends by saying there is no rule, so the monsters can be wacky and a little scary.

The story begins by repeating the rules for helping monsters behave: be quiet, chew your food, take turns, say good bye, say boo, clean up, sit still, go to sleep, and say good night. Then it starts a counting story about a hungry monster who wants one more of many things. A monster with one cookie gets another cookie and has two. A monster with two balloons gets one more and has three. A grumpy monster with three apples gets one more and has four. A sad monster with four beach balls gets one more and has five. A grabby monster with five strawberries gets one more and has six. A grouchy monster with six crackers gets one more and has seven. A candy-loving monster with seven jelly beans gets one more and has eight. A sleepy monster with eight teddy bears gets one more and has nine. Finally, a sleepy monster asks for more good-night kisses and gets ten. The story ends with the monster feeling cozy and snug and needing one big hug.

Monster Be Good explains that monsters are not always easy to handle because they can be noisy, messy, mean, hungry, selfish, wild, tired, or grumpy. A hungry monster should get a fork and spoon and be told to chew its food. A selfish monster should be told to take turns. A mean monster should be left with a good bye. A scary monster should be scared back with “Boo.” A messy monster should be told to clean up. A wild monster should be given a timeout and told to sit still. A tired, grumpy monster should be sent to bed. If the monster asks nicely, it should get a kiss and be told good night. The story ends by saying these steps will help a monster be good.

Each time, the number goes up by one, ending at ten. The final monster wants one big hug.

He shared everything with his friends, and things got better.

Bunny, Giraffe, and Bear painted the fence. Mole, Grasshopper, and Cheetah cleaned the sandbox. Soon the work felt hard and messy, and everyone got tired. Mouse stopped the group at lunch and said they should work smarter, not harder. He explained that this meant using clever ideas. The friends tried new ways to work. At the dog park, Canoli met Mac and Mr. Oinks, and they were worried too. Their owners had started holiday things early, and the dogs talked about bad behavior they had done, like chewing slippers, barking at a neighbor girl, and rolling in mud. Canoli said Thanksgiving was not just about food. It was also a time to show love and thanks. The dogs decided to be on their best behavior to show their owners they were thankful.

Canoli went home from the dog park and tried very hard to be good. He played in the yard without getting dirty and stayed clean when he came inside. Camy noticed this and asked if he was all right. She told Canoli that she loved him just the way he was, even when he got dirty or did silly things. Canoli thought about her words and realized that Camy was thankful for him too. He began to think that Thanksgiving might not be cancelled after all.

At last, the fourth Thursday in November arrived. Canoli smelled something delicious cooking in the house and ran into the kitchen. Camy was making Thanksgiving food, so Canoli knew his favorite holiday was safe. Soon the doorbell rang, and Mac, Mr. Oinks, and their owners came for dinner. The dogs said they had tried to be good boys too. Canoli saw that their owners were thankful for them just as they were. After the big feast, Canoli and Camy curled up on the couch with full bellies. Camy told Canoli that he was her best boy, and Canoli gave her a big kiss. He knew he had many things to be thankful for.

One hot day in the jungle of Nool, Horton the Elephant was splashing in a pool when he heard a tiny yelp from a speck of dust. Horton looked closely and guessed that a very small person must be on the speck. He gently lifted the dust speck onto a clover and said, “A person’s a person, no matter how small.” The sour Kangaroo and her young one laughed at him and said no one could live there. Horton kept the clover safe and walked with it, even when the news spread and the jungle animals made fun of him.

Later, the Wickersham brothers grabbed the clover and gave it to a black-bottomed eagle named Vlad Vladikoff. Horton chased after it all night. By morning, the clover had fallen into a huge field of clovers, and Horton searched and searched until he found it. The mayor of Whoville told Horton that all the Whos were safe but needed help after the fall. When the Kangaroos and Wickershams tried to take Horton away, the Whos made a loud noise, and Horton’s friends heard them. Their voices proved they were real, and Horton saved them.
